- Data governance is the discipline of exercising authority, control, and shared decision-making over the management of data assets — who can take what action, on which data, under what circumstances, using what methods. Catalogs and discovery are the operational layer that makes governance executable: a metadata platform that inventories assets, attaches meaning (glossaries, tags, classifications), traces movement (lineage), assigns accountability (stewardship), and exposes it all through search so people can *find and trust* data. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- This skill covers governance **as a practice and an architecture**, not the adjacent disciplines. Privacy law and ethics live in `da-11`; operational reliability/freshness monitoring lives in `da-19`; pipeline construction lives in `da-13`. Focus here: frameworks → metadata → discovery → lineage → meaning → roles → classification → access → products/mesh → tooling. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- Two macro-shifts define the 2024–2026 landscape: [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Passive → active metadata.** Catalogs stop being static inventories and become bidirectional orchestration layers that push metadata back into the stack to drive automation (Gartner; Atlan). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Centralized → federated governance.** Data mesh reframes governance as *federated computational governance* — global rules enforced computationally, local ownership by domain teams (Dehghani; Fowler). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **DAMA-DMBOK** (Data Management Body of Knowledge, DAMA International) organizes data management into **11 knowledge areas** rendered as the "DAMA wheel" with **Data Governance at the hub**: governance, architecture, modeling, storage & operations, security, integration & interoperability, document & content management, reference & master data, data warehousing & BI, metadata, and data quality. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **DCAM** (Data Management Capability Assessment Model, EDM Council) is a maturity-assessment standard organized into **eight core components** (data strategy, business case & funding, governance, architecture, technology, quality, operations, control environment). **DCAM v3** (released 2024) is the current standard. DCAM measures *how mature* the program is; DMBOK describes *what the disciplines are*. **CDMC** (Cloud Data Management Capabilities) extends DCAM-style assessment to cloud + sensitive-data controls. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Metadata** = data about data: **technical** (schemas, types, partitions), **business** (definitions, glossary terms, ownership), **operational** (run logs, freshness, query frequency). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Passive metadata** sits in a static catalog read by humans. **Active metadata** is continuously analyzed, curated, and *pushed back* into tools to drive automation — e.g., auto-propagating a PII tag from a source column to every downstream table. Metadata moves **both directions**. Gartner projected ~30% of orgs adopting active metadata by 2026 with up to 70% faster time-to-delivery, and reframed metadata management as foundational to **AI readiness** in its 2025 Magic Quadrant (first refresh in five years, Nov 2025). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- Discovery is the consumer entry point: search across assets ranked by relevance, enriched with ownership, quality, popularity, and lineage so a user can judge **trustworthiness**. Modern catalogs add natural-language/conversational search (Atlan) and **query-log ingestion** (Alation) that mines actual execution patterns to rank assets. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Table-level lineage** answers "which datasets feed which." **Column-level lineage** maps dependencies field-by-field, enabling precise impact analysis ("if I drop this column, what breaks?") and root-cause analysis. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- Lineage is derived by **SQL parsing**; parser choice matters: DataHub uses **SQLGlot** (schema-aware, highest correct-lineage rate); OpenMetadata uses **sqllineage**; OpenLineage/Marquez uses **openlineage-sql**. Native column-level support covers Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and BI tools (Looker, Power BI, Tableau). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- A **business glossary** is the controlled vocabulary of agreed business terms (e.g., "active customer") with definitions, owners, and relationships, linked to physical assets so technical columns inherit business meaning. Distinct from a **data dictionary** (technical, schema-level) and a **taxonomy/ontology** (semantic relationships). Stewards own glossary curation. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Data Owner** — accountable (senior business role) for classification, protection, use, and quality of a domain; results-focused; signs off on glossary and access policy. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Data Steward** — responsible for quality, definitions, documentation, glossary, and lineage; task-focused; day-to-day governance operator. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Data Custodian** — IT role; implements and maintains storage/security controls the Owner specifies; handles access provisioning, incident review, platform monitoring. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- RACI: Owner = Accountable, Steward = Responsible (meaning/quality), Custodian = Responsible (technical controls). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Classification** assigns sensitivity levels (public / internal / confidential / restricted) and compliance categories (PII, GDPR, HIPAA). Modern platforms auto-discover and tag sensitive data — Unity Catalog uses an **agentic/AI classifier** for continuous PII discovery. **Governed tags** enforce a controlled tag vocabulary (vs. free-form) so policies key off them reliably. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- Move from per-object grants to **policy-as-data**. **ABAC** (attribute-based access control) evaluates tag-based conditions and applies **row filters** (which rows you see) and **column masks** (what values you see) automatically across catalogs/schemas — e.g., mask any column tagged `PII` unless the user is in `pii-readers`. Unity Catalog made ABAC row filters, column masks, governed tags, and data classification **GA in 2025**. Pair classification (find) + tags (label) + ABAC (enforce) for scalable, declarative governance. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Data mesh** (Zhamak Dehghani, ThoughtWorks 2019) is a sociotechnical approach to analytical data at scale on **four principles**: domain-oriented ownership, **data as a product**, self-serve data platform, and **federated computational governance**. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Federated computational governance** = a decision model led by a federation of domain + platform product owners with local autonomy, adhering to **global rules enforced computationally** (encoded into the platform, not by committee). A **data product** is the smallest architectural unit encapsulating everything needed to share data (data + metadata + code + access + SLOs), owned by the domain team. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- A **data contract** is an enforceable agreement between producer and consumer covering schema, semantics, quality, and SLAs. **ODCS** (Open Data Contract Standard, v3.x, governed by **Bitol**, a Linux Foundation AI & Data project; originated at PayPal) defines schema-level executable contracts. **ODPS** (Open Data Product Specification) is broader — design, publish, discover, monetize, govern data products as business-value units, and can reference ODCS contracts inline or by URL. Use ODCS for the interface; ODPS for the product wrapper. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- Frameworks: **DAMA-DMBOK** (scope/vocabulary), **DCAM v3** + **CDMC** (maturity assessment), **data mesh** (federated operating model), **ODCS/ODPS** (contracts & product specs). [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Frame the operating model.** Centralized vs. federated (mesh). Map domains. Assign Owner/Steward/Custodian per domain (RACI). Use DCAM to baseline maturity and set a roadmap. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Pick the scope that delivers value first.** Highest-value or highest-risk domains, not boil-the-ocean. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Ingest technical metadata.** Connect sources (warehouses, lakes, BI, dbt); auto-harvest schemas + lineage; verify column-level coverage for key dialects. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Layer meaning.** Build the business glossary; link terms to physical assets. Stewards curate. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Classify & tag.** Run automated sensitive-data classification; apply *governed* tags, not free-form. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Enforce access declaratively.** Define ABAC policies keyed on tags (mask PII, row-filter by region). Test propagation across schemas. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Activate the metadata.** Wire automation: tag propagation along lineage, freshness/popularity into search ranking, push-back to source tools. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Operationalize.** Stewardship rituals, glossary review cadence, data contracts (ODCS) on critical interfaces, product specs (ODPS) for shared data products. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Measure.** Coverage (% cataloged/owned/classified), adoption (search usage, time-to-find), trust (% certified), policy compliance. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Certify, don't catalog everything.** A "verified/certified" badge on trusted assets beats 100% coverage of unmanaged junk. Discovery is about trust, not census. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Tag-driven policy.** Classify → governed tag → ABAC. One policy ("mask `PII`") covers thousands of objects and auto-applies to new ones. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Propagate along lineage.** Use column-level lineage to auto-inherit classifications/tags downstream. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Glossary terms as the bridge.** Bind business terms to physical columns so non-technical users search in business language. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Federated rules, central platform.** In mesh, encode global rules computationally in the self-serve platform; let domains own products within those rails. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Contracts on the boundaries.** Put ODCS contracts on cross-domain/producer-consumer interfaces where breakage is expensive; don't contract everything. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Query logs for relevance.** Rank search and recommend assets by actual usage (Alation-style), not alphabetical or last-modified. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Catalog as a graveyard.** One-time bulk ingest, no stewardship, no owners, stale within months. Governance is a continuous program, not a project. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Passive metadata only.** Treating the catalog as a read-only wiki — no automation, no push-back. Metadata that doesn't *act* decays. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Free-form tag sprawl.** Uncontrolled tags (`pii`, `PII`, `personal`, `sensitive`) make policies unreliable. Use governed vocabularies. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Governance-by-committee bottleneck.** Central team must approve every change — kills velocity. Federate ownership; enforce computationally. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Owner/steward/custodian conflation.** One overloaded "data person" can't be accountable, responsible for meaning, *and* run the platform. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Table-level lineage where column-level is needed.** Impact analysis on a schema change is guesswork without field-level lineage. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Tool-first, model-last.** Buying Collibra/Atlan before defining domains, roles, and policies yields shelfware. Operating model first. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Boil-the-ocean rollout.** Cataloging every asset before any are governed. Start narrow, prove value, expand. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Lineage incomplete / missing columns.** Check parser/dialect support (SQLGlot vs sqllineage), ensure schema context, confirm the connector ingests query history (not just DDL). Dynamic SQL and `SELECT *` degrade column-level resolution. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Sensitive data slipping through.** Automated classification missed it — re-run/expand classifiers, add custom patterns, propagate along lineage so derived columns inherit the tag. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **ABAC policy not applying.** Verify the object carries the governed tag the policy keys on, that the policy is at the right catalog/schema scope, and that classification ran before policy evaluation. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Low catalog adoption.** Usually a trust/relevance problem: no owners, no certification, poor search ranking. Add ownership, certify key assets, rank by query-log popularity, link glossary terms. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Purview ↔ Unity Catalog drift.** Schema/lineage/classification out of sync — confirm connector/API sync cadence; Purview is discovery/technical-metadata, UC is the enforcement plane. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Glossary nobody uses.** Terms not linked to physical assets, or no steward cadence. Bind terms to columns; put glossary review in the stewardship ritual. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]
- **Mesh governance chaos.** Global rules defined but not *computational* — encode them into the self-serve platform; agreement docs don't enforce. [src: da-30-data-governance-catalogs]

- Conformal prediction (CP) turns any point predictor into a set predictor with a [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **finite-sample, distribution-free marginal coverage guarantee**. Given a target [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- miscoverage rate alpha, CP outputs a prediction set C(X) such that [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- P(Y in C(X)) >= 1 - alpha — holding for any underlying model, any data [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- distribution, and any sample size, requiring only that the calibration and test [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- data are **exchangeable**. It is a wrapper, not a model. You keep your XGBoost, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- neural net, or random forest and bolt CP on top to get honest error bars. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- CP is the dominant frequentist answer to "how do I get valid uncertainty without [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- trusting my model's probabilities." Compared to Bayesian credible intervals [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (which require a correct prior/likelihood) and the bootstrap (asymptotic, can [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- under-cover), CP's guarantee is exact in finite samples and model-agnostic. The [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- modern reference is Angelopoulos & Bates, "A Gentle Introduction to Conformal [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification" (arXiv 2107.07511, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- v-series 2021-2023). The theoretical foundation is Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- "Algorithmic Learning in a Random World" (Springer, 2005; 2nd ed. 2022). [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Use this skill when someone needs **calibrated intervals/sets on top of an [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- existing model**. For full Bayesian modeling use da-25; for point forecasting use [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Split-conformal gives the exact two-sided bound [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- 1 - alpha <= P(Y_{n+1} in C(X_{n+1})) <= 1 - alpha + 1/(n+1), where n is the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibration set size. The guarantee is **marginal** (averaged over the random [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- draw of calibration + test points), not conditional on a specific X or a fixed [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibration set — coverage fluctuates around the target for any one fixed [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibration set, and the spread shrinks as n grows. Distribution-free and [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- finite-sample, no asymptotics. Source: Angelopoulos & Bates 2023 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511); Lei et al. "Distribution-Free Predictive Inference [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- for Regression" JASA 2018; Vovk et al. 2005. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- CP requires only that (X_1,Y_1)...(X_{n+1},Y_{n+1}) are **exchangeable**: their [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- joint distribution is invariant to permutation. This is weaker than i.i.d. but is [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- violated by distribution shift and temporal/serial dependence — the two main ways [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- CP breaks in practice. Source: Vovk et al. 2005; Barber, Candès, Ramdas & [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Tibshirani "Conformal Prediction Beyond Exchangeability" Annals of Statistics [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- 2023 (stat.cmu.edu/~ryantibs/papers/nexcp.pdf). [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- A function s(x,y) measuring how "strange" a label y is for input x given the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- model — e.g. residual |y - f(x)| for regression, or 1 - softmax(true class) for [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- classification. CP is entirely defined by your choice of score: the score [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- controls **adaptivity and set shape**, while the coverage guarantee holds for [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- *any* score. Designing a good score (heteroscedastic-aware, class-adaptive) is [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- the main lever for sharpness. Source: Angelopoulos & Bates 2023. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- The workhorse. (a) Split data into proper-training + calibration. (b) Fit the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- model on training. (c) Compute calibration scores s_i. (d) Set qhat = the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n empirical quantile of the calibration scores (the same [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- finite-sample-corrected quantile used in Methodology step 5). (e) For a [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- new x, output C(x) = { y : s(x,y) <= qhat }. One model fit, O(n log n) [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibration — cheap and the default for deep learning. The finite-sample [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- quantile correction (the +1) is what delivers exact validity. Source: [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Papadopoulos et al. 2002 (inductive CP); Angelopoulos & Bates 2023; [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- github.com/aangelopoulos/conformal-prediction. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- The original formulation: for each candidate label y, refit (or re-score) the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- model with (x_{n+1}, y) appended and test that point's conformity rank against [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- all others. Uses **all** data (no calibration split, so more statistically [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- efficient on small data) but costs one refit per candidate label per test point — [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- usually intractable except with closed-form/leave-one-out shortcuts. First [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- proposed by Gammerman, Vovk & Vapnik 1998. Source: Vovk et al. 2005; Vovk [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- "Transductive Conformal Predictors" 2013 (alrw.net/articles/08.pdf). [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Wraps a quantile regressor (estimating lower/upper conditional quantiles [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- q_lo, q_hi) with conformal calibration. Score is the signed exceedance [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- E_i = max(q_lo(x_i) - y_i, y_i - q_hi(x_i)); conformalize E to get qhat and output [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- quantile regression and **valid coverage** from CP — intervals widen where the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- data is noisy, producing shorter intervals than residual-based CP. Source: Romano, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Patterson & Candès, "Conformalized Quantile Regression" NeurIPS 2019 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (arxiv.org/abs/1905.03222); github.com/yromano/cqr. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **APS (Adaptive Prediction Sets):** score accumulates sorted softmax mass until [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- the true class is included; produces sets that adapt to difficulty (bigger sets [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- on hard examples). Source: Romano, Sesia & Candès, "Classification with Valid [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- and Adaptive Coverage" NeurIPS 2020. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **RAPS (Regularized APS):** adds a regularization penalty that discourages [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- including low-probability tail classes, yielding 5-10x smaller, more stable sets [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- than APS while keeping the coverage guarantee. Source: Angelopoulos, Bates, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Malik & Jordan, "Uncertainty Sets for Image Classifiers using Conformal [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Prediction" ICLR 2021 (arxiv.org/abs/2009.14193); [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- github.com/aangelopoulos/conformal_classification. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **LAC / naive softmax score** (1 - p_true) gives the smallest sets but worse [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- conditional coverage; APS/RAPS trade size for adaptivity. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Partition (X x Y) into disjoint categories (e.g. by class, sex, region) and run a [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- separate conformal calibration **per category**, giving group-conditional coverage [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- P(Y in C(X) | group=g) >= 1 - alpha for each g. Only requires exchangeability [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- within each category. Limitation: groups must be **non-overlapping**; overlapping [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- or continuous attributes need newer methods (Kandinsky CP 2025; Gibbs et al. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- conditional-guarantee CP 2023). Source: Vovk et al. 2005 (Mondrian CP); [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- MAPIE Mondrian docs (mapie.readthedocs.io); Ding et al. "Class-Conditional [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Conformal Prediction with Many Classes" NeurIPS 2023. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Under covariate shift (P_test(X) != P_train(X) but P(Y|X) unchanged), [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- exchangeability fails and CP under/over-covers. **Weighted conformal** reweights [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibration scores by the likelihood ratio w(x) = dP_test(x)/dP_train(x) (the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- "weighted exchangeability" notion) to restore validity when w is known or [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- estimable from unlabeled test data. Source: Tibshirani, Barber, Candès & Ramdas, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- "Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift" NeurIPS 2019 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (arxiv.org/abs/1904.06019); extended to feedback shift in Fannjiang et al. PNAS [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Serial dependence breaks exchangeability, so two main adaptations exist: [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **EnbPI (Ensemble batch Prediction Intervals):** Xu & Xie, ICML 2021 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (proceedings.mlr.press/v139/xu21h). Uses leave-one-out ensemble residuals, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- no data split, assumes stationary strongly-mixing errors; gives approximate [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- marginal coverage asymptotically. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **ACI (Adaptive Conformal Inference):** Gibbs & Candès, NeurIPS 2021 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (arxiv.org/abs/2106.00170). Online update of the effective miscoverage level [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- alpha_t after each observation; stable under arbitrary distribution shift and [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- guarantees long-run coverage regardless of dependence. Variants: AgACI / DtACI, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Zaffran et al. ICML 2022 (arxiv.org/abs/2202.07282); SPCI, Xu & Xie 2023. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Two orthogonal quality axes. **Calibration/validity** = the set actually covers at [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- the nominal rate (a 90% interval contains Y ~90% of the time). **Sharpness/ [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- efficiency** = sets are as small/tight as possible. CP *guarantees* marginal [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibration by construction; sharpness depends on the model and score and is the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- thing you optimize. Gneiting's maxim: maximize sharpness subject to calibration. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Report average set size / interval width alongside empirical coverage. Source: [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Gneiting et al. JRSS-B 2007; Angelopoulos & Bates 2023. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Generalizes CP from miscoverage to **any monotone bounded loss** (false-negative [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- rate, F1, recall), controlling E[loss] <= alpha. Useful for multilabel, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- segmentation, and structured outputs. Source: Angelopoulos, Bates et al. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- "Conformal Risk Control" 2022/ICLR 2024 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~angelopoulos/publications/downloads/conformal-risk.pdf). [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **MAPIE** (Model Agnostic Prediction Interval Estimator) — scikit-learn-native, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- the standard for tabular regression/classification; split/CV+/jackknife+, CQR, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- APS/RAPS, Mondrian, conformal risk control. mapie.readthedocs.io. Use this [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- first for sklearn workflows. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **crepes** — lightweight, clean conformal regressors & predictive systems [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (Boström); good for normalized/Mondrian regression and conformal predictive [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- distributions. github.com/henrikbostrom/crepes. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **TorchCP** — PyTorch-native, GPU-accelerated; deep classifiers, regressors, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- GNNs, LLMs; APS/RAPS/SAPS, CQR, time-series CP. JMLR 2025 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (arxiv.org/abs/2402.12683). Use for deep learning. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **PUNCC** (Deel), **Fortuna** (AWS), **nonconformist** (the original, now [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- largely superseded) — alternatives; nonconformist is NumPy-only and unmaintained. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Reference implementations: github.com/aangelopoulos/conformal-prediction [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (notebooks for every method), yromano/cqr, aangelopoulos/conformal_classification. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Define the task & alpha.** Pick target coverage 1-alpha (e.g. 0.9). Decide [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- regression (intervals) vs classification (sets), and whether you need marginal [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- or group-conditional coverage. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Three-way split.** proper-train / calibration / test. Calibration n>=~1000 [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- for stable 90% intervals; n>=~ a few hundred minimum. Never reuse training [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- data for calibration. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Fit the base model** on proper-train only. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Choose a score.** Regression: residual (simple) or CQR (heteroscedastic). [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Classification: LAC (small sets) or APS/RAPS (adaptive). The score is your [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Calibrate.** Compute scores on calibration set; take the finite-sample- [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- corrected quantile qhat = quantile(scores, ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n). [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Predict.** C(x) = {y : s(x,y) <= qhat}. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Evaluate on test:** empirical marginal coverage (should ~ 1-alpha), average [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- set size / interval width (sharpness), and **size-stratified / group coverage** [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- to expose conditional-coverage failures. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Handle violations.** Covariate shift -> weighted CP. Time series -> EnbPI/ACI. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Heterogeneous subgroups -> Mondrian/CQR. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Default stack:** sklearn model + MAPIE split or CV+ with CQR is the 80% case [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- for tabular regression. For deep classifiers use TorchCP + RAPS. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **CV+ / jackknife+** (Barber et al. Annals 2021) when data is scarce and you [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- can't afford a calibration split — gives slightly weaker (1-2alpha) guarantees [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Always **report coverage AND average width/size** — coverage alone hides a [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- useless predictor that returns the whole label space. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Stratify coverage checks** by feature bins / class / group; marginal coverage [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- can be 90% while a subgroup sits at 60%. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- For **online/streaming**, use ACI and monitor the running coverage; let alpha_t [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- Use a **fixed random seed for the split** and, where possible, average over [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- multiple splits (or use CV+) to reduce calibration-set variance. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Calibrating on training data.** Reusing fit data destroys validity — scores [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- are optimistically small and you under-cover. Always hold out calibration. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Trusting marginal coverage as conditional coverage.** CP guarantees marginal, [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- not P(Y in C | X=x); a model can be 90% overall and badly miscalibrated per [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- subgroup. Use Mondrian / size-stratified checks. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Ignoring exchangeability.** Applying vanilla CP to time series or shifted test [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- data silently breaks the guarantee. Use ACI/EnbPI or weighted CP. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Optimizing the score for coverage.** Coverage is guaranteed regardless — tune [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- the score for *sharpness*, not coverage. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Tiny calibration sets.** n in the tens makes the realized coverage swing wildly [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- around the target; the +1/(n+1) slack and quantile granularity dominate. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Confusing CP with calibrated probabilities.** CP gives valid *sets*, not [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- calibrated softmax scores; Platt/temperature scaling is a different (and [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Reusing the calibration set to also select alpha or the model.** That is [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- double-dipping; it invalidates the guarantee. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Empirical coverage below target:** check for data leakage (calibration overlaps [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- training), non-exchangeability (shift/time), or too-small n. Verify the quantile [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- used the (n+1) finite-sample correction. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Coverage fine but intervals huge:** the base model is weak or the score is [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- non-adaptive; switch residual->CQR, LAC->APS/RAPS, or improve the model. Width [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- is a model problem, not a CP problem. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Good marginal coverage, bad subgroup coverage:** move to Mondrian/ [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- group-conditional CP or CQR; report stratified coverage. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Time-series coverage drifts over time:** exchangeability violated — use ACI [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- (online alpha_t update) or EnbPI; plot rolling coverage. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Coverage degrades after deployment:** likely covariate shift — estimate the [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- likelihood ratio and apply weighted conformal, or recalibrate on fresh data. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- **Classification sets sometimes empty or all-classes:** empty sets are valid [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- under some scores (force-inclusion of the top class if a non-empty set is [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]
- required); full-label sets signal an uninformative model or too-small alpha. [src: da-31-conformal-prediction-uq]

- Real-time OLAP databases are the **query and storage engines** that answer [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- analytical questions (aggregations, group-bys, filters, top-N, time-series [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- rollups) over large, **continuously updating** datasets with **sub-second [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- latency** and **high concurrency**. They sit between stream processing (which [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- transforms events in flight — da-14) and the BI/semantic layer (da-18), serving [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- as the low-latency serving layer for dashboards, monitoring, and [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- user/customer-facing analytics. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- What makes an engine "real-time OLAP" rather than a cloud data warehouse: [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Fresh data**: rows are queryable seconds (often sub-second) after they land, [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- via streaming ingestion — not after a nightly batch load. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **High concurrency / QPS**: built to serve thousands of concurrent queries [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- (a per-user dashboard feature), not a handful of internal analysts. ClickHouse [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- reports 1,000+ concurrent queries per node; Snowflake defaults to ~8 queries [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- per warehouse, Redshift caps ~50 concurrent across queues [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([ClickHouse, 2025](https://clickhouse.com/blog/cloud-data-warehouses-cost-performance-comparison)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Tight latency SLAs**: tens of milliseconds, achieved with columnar storage, [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- vectorized execution, and pre-aggregation/indexing. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- This skill covers the **engines and the query layer**. It is the OLAP-database [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- node of the data-analytics curriculum (da-1 onward); it does not cover stream [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- processing (da-14), pipeline orchestration (da-13), or the metrics layer (da-18). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Data is stored **by column, not by row**. Analytical queries touch few columns [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- but many rows, so columnar layout reads only the needed columns, drastically [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- cutting I/O, and stores like-typed values together so they compress far better [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- (delta, dictionary, RLE, LZ4/ZSTD). This is the foundational OLAP advantage over [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- row stores ([SQLFlash, 2025](https://sqlflash.ai/article/20250722_olap-database-architecture/); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Compression both saves storage and increases effective scan throughput. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Instead of processing one row at a time through a tuple-at-a-time interpreter, [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- the engine processes **batches (vectors) of column values** in tight loops, [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- exploiting CPU **SIMD** instructions, cache locality, and amortized [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- virtual-function/branch overhead. This yields multi-x to order-of-magnitude [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- speedups and is paired with columnar storage in every modern engine [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([SQLFlash, 2025](https://sqlflash.ai/article/20250722_olap-database-architecture/); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Even hybrid OLTP/OLAP systems (Google Spanner's columnar engine, OceanBase 4.3) [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- adopt columnar + vectorized execution for analytics, up to ~200x faster on live [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- data ([InfoQ, 2025](https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/09/google-spanner-oltp-olap-unify/)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Batch**: data loaded and computed periodically; high latency, high accuracy, [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- cheap recompute (classic warehouse / BI pattern). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Real-time**: data queryable seconds after arrival; low latency, continuous [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Lambda** keeps two paths: a batch layer for correctness and a speed layer [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- for low latency, at the cost of dual code and reconciliation. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Kappa** collapses everything into a single streaming path over an immutable [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- log (e.g., Kafka), replaying when recompute is needed; simpler but harder for [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- large historical batch jobs [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([bix-tech, 2025](https://bix-tech.com/kappa-vs-lambda-vs-batch-choosing-the-right-data-architecture-for-your-business/); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Most 2025 teams run a hybrid: streaming for operational decisions, batch for [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- trusted reporting and model training [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([makitsol, 2025](https://makitsol.com/real-time-analytics-vs-batch-processing-in-us-eu/)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Real-time OLAP engines ingest directly from **Kafka, Pulsar, and Kinesis**. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Apache Pinot transforms bytes from Kafka into queryable segments with sub-second [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- visibility from write to query as the default; end-to-end latency under 5s is [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([StarTree, 2025](https://startree.ai/resources/inside-the-flight-path-of-real-time-ingestion-in-apache-pinot/); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Append-only** is the simplest model (events never change). Pinot was [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- append-only until 2022. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Upserts** let the same key be ingested many times but return only the latest [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- value at query time. Pinot supports **full upsert** (new row replaces the old [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- entirely) and **partial upsert** (only specified columns update) [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([Pinot deep dive, 2026](https://pdpspectra.com/blog/apache-pinot-realtime-olap-2026/)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- StarRocks uses a **primary-key table model** (cloud-native PK index in [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- shared-data) for upserts and CDC-style mutable data [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([StarRocks, 2025](https://www.starrocks.io/blog/vbill-payment-handling-billions-of-records-in-real-time-with-starrocks)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Precompute aggregates so dashboard queries hit ready answers instead of scanning [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Pinot star-tree index**: precomputes selected aggregation paths during [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- segment generation; returns aggregation/group-by over billions of rows in [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- milliseconds when the query shape matches configured dimensions/metrics, with [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- no separate MV maintenance. Benchmarks show ~126x throughput over an inverted [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- index (27 to 3,494 QPS on 4 vCPU) [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([Pinot docs](https://docs.pinot.apache.org/build-with-pinot/indexing/star-tree-index); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **StarRocks / Doris asynchronous materialized views**: precompute joins and [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- aggregations; the optimizer **automatically rewrites** base-table queries to [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- use the MV (transparent query rewrite). Can be built over external lake [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- catalogs (Iceberg/Hive/Hudi/Paimon) [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([StarRocks docs](https://docs.starrocks.io/docs/using_starrocks/async_mv/use_cases/query_rewrite_with_materialized_views/); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **ClickHouse materialized views / projections**: MVs are insert-time triggers [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- that populate a target table (often with `AggregatingMergeTree`); projections [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- store an alternate sorted/aggregated copy inside the part. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ClickHouse's `MergeTree` family writes each `INSERT` as an immutable **data [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- part** (one file per column + index), merged in the background. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Sparse primary index**: one mark per **granule** (default 8,192 rows), stored [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- in `primary.idx`; it does **not** enforce uniqueness, it lets the engine skip [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- granules that cannot match a filter [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([ClickHouse docs](https://clickhouse.com/docs/guides/best-practices/sparse-primary-indexes)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- **Data-skipping indexes** (`minmax`, `set(N)`, `bloom_filter`, `ngrambf_v1`, [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- `tokenbf_v1`) summarize non-key columns so granules can be skipped on [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- secondary predicates; tune `GRANULARITY` and materialize after adding to [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]

- inverted (bitmap) indexes for fast filtering [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- ([Druid docs](https://druid.apache.org/docs/latest/design/segments/)). [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- Two camps: (a) **flatten/denormalize** into one wide table for fastest scans [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- (historically favored by Druid/ClickHouse, which are weaker at large joins); [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]

- Rule of thumb: denormalize when joins dominate latency and the engine joins [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]
- poorly; keep the star schema when the engine joins well and dimensions change. [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]

- **Classify the workload.** Internal batch BI / ad-hoc to cloud DW (Snowflake/ [src: da-28-realtime-olap-databases]

- Spatial analytics studies data with a geographic/locational dimension, where the [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- core methodological premise is **Tobler's First Law**: "everything is related to [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- everything else, but near things are more related than distant things." This makes [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- location an explanatory variable, not just an attribute — and means standard [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- non-spatial statistics (which assume independent observations) are often invalid [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- on spatial data. This skill covers general spatial analysis. For MongoDB geo [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- queries (`2dsphere`, `$geoNear`, `$geoWithin`), defer to `mongodb-geospatial`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Two fundamental representations of geographic phenomena: [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Vector**: discrete features as points, lines, and polygons defined by [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- coordinate vertices. Best for objects with crisp boundaries (parcels, roads, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- administrative areas). In Python, vector geometry is handled by Shapely and [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- exposed through GeoPandas as a `GeoSeries`/`GeoDataFrame` (a pandas DataFrame [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- with one or more geometry columns; only one is the *active* geometry, accessed [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- via `.geometry` and switched with `set_geometry()`) ([GeoPandas, Data [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- structures, 2026](https://geopandas.org/en/stable/docs/user_guide/data_structures.html)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Raster**: a regular grid of cells/pixels, each holding a value. Best for [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- continuous fields (elevation, temperature, satellite imagery). Handled in [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Python by `rasterio`/`xarray`/`rioxarray`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Choose vector for object/topology-centric analysis (joins, networks); raster [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- for surface/field analysis (interpolation outputs, map algebra). Conversion [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (rasterize/vectorize) loses information — avoid round-tripping. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- A CRS maps coordinates to real locations; without it, geometries are just numbers [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- in arbitrary space ([GeoPandas, Projections, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2026](https://geopandas.org/en/stable/docs/user_guide/projections.html)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Geographic CRS** uses lat/lon on a 3D ellipsoid. **EPSG:4326 (WGS84)** is the [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- GPS/GeoJSON default; its units are *degrees*, not meters. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Projected CRS** flattens the earth onto a plane with linear (meter) units. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator)** is the default for web tiles (Google/OSM/Mapbox): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- good for display, *bad for area* (massively distorts toward the poles). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **UTM** divides earth into 60 zones for accurate local distance/area; pick the [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- zone covering your data ([8th Light, Geographic Coordinate Systems 101, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2023](https://8thlight.com/insights/geographic-coordinate-systems-101); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://developers.arcgis.com/documentation/spatial-references/)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **`set_crs()` vs `to_crs()`**: `set_crs` *assigns/labels* the CRS without moving [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- coordinates (use when CRS is missing/wrong); `to_crs` *reprojects* (transforms [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- coordinate values). Never confuse them. Use `estimate_utm_crs()` to pick a local [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- metric CRS ([GeoPandas, Projections, 2026](https://geopandas.org/en/stable/docs/user_guide/projections.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Topological relationships between two geometries are formalized by the [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Dimensionally Extended 9-Intersection Model (DE-9IM)** — a 3×3 matrix comparing [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- the interior/boundary/exterior of each geometry. Named predicates are shortcuts [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- over this matrix ([PostGIS, ch.5 Spatial Queries, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-dev/using_postgis_query.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `intersects` (share any space — the inverse of `disjoint`), `contains`, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `within` (inverse of contains), `touches` (share only a boundary), `overlaps`, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `crosses`, `equals`, `covers`/`covered_by`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `ST_Relate` (PostGIS) / Shapely `relate()` return the raw DE-9IM string for [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- custom relationships. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- A **spatial join** attaches attributes from one layer to another by spatial [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- relationship rather than a key. `geopandas.sjoin(left, right, predicate=..., [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- how=...)` supports `intersects` (default), `within`, `contains`. `sjoin_nearest` [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- joins to the closest feature. PostGIS performs the equivalent with predicate [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- functions in the `WHERE`/`JOIN ON` clause, automatically using a spatial index [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- when present ([PostGIS workshop, §13 Spatial Joins, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://postgis.net/workshops/postgis-intro/joins.html); [pythonGIS, Spatial [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- queries, 2024](https://pythongis.org/part2/chapter-06/nb/05-spatial-queries.html)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Unary**: `buffer(d)` (zone within distance d — units follow the CRS!), [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `centroid`, `simplify(tol)` (Douglas-Peucker vertex reduction), [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `convex_hull`, `envelope`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Binary / set**: `intersection`, `union` (`union_all()`/`unary_union` to [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- dissolve a collection), `difference`, `symmetric_difference`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- GeoPandas `overlay(df1, df2, how=...)` applies set operations across two whole [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- layers (`intersection`/`union`/`identity`/`difference`/`symmetric_difference`) [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- ([GeoPandas, Set operations with overlay, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2026](https://geopandas.org/en/stable/docs/user_guide/set_operations.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://py.geocompx.org/04-geometry-operations)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Without an index, every pairwise spatial test is O(n²). Two index families: [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Tree indexes (R-tree)**: bounding-box hierarchy used internally by GeoPandas [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (`.sindex`), Shapely STRtree, and PostGIS GiST. Fast pairwise filtering; node [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- rectangles may overlap ([Corso, Geospatial Indexing, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2020](https://austincorso.com/2020/12/02/geospatial-indexing.html)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Discrete global grid systems (DGGS)** encode location as a hierarchical [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- cell ID for prefix/integer lookups and aggregation: [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Geohash** (Niemeyer, 2008): Z-order rectangles; shared string prefix ⇒ [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- shared parent cell. Suffers boundary discontinuity (adjacent points can [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- differ at the first char). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Google S2**: projects sphere onto cube faces, Hilbert-curve ordered [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 64-bit IDs; square cells; used in Google Maps. Strong for hierarchical [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- coverings/aggregation. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Uber H3** (open-sourced 2018): hexagonal cells; near-uniform centroid [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- spacing and a single neighbor distance, ideal for grid traversal, binning, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- and ML features. Hexagons can't perfectly nest, so parent/child is [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- approximate ([Feifke, Geospatial Indexing Explained, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2023](https://benfeifke.com/posts/geospatial-indexing-explained/); [KunYu, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- H3 vs Geohash vs S2, 2024](https://ky-gis.com/en/blog/h3-vs-geohash-vs-s2)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Rule of thumb: **H3** for neighbor/traversal and binning; **S2** for exact [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- nesting/aggregation; **geohash** for simple prefix-range queries in a B-tree. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- ESDA and spatial regression require a **spatial weights matrix** encoding which [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- observations are neighbors. Built with libpysal ([Geographic Data Science with [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Python, ch.4 Spatial Weights, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://geographicdata.science/book/notebooks/04_spatial_weights.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://pysal.org/libpysal/user-guide/weights/weights.html)): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Contiguity**: `Queen` (share a vertex *or* edge) vs `Rook` (share an edge [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- only) — for polygons. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Distance-based**: `KNN` (k nearest), `DistanceBand` (all within a threshold), [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `Kernel` (distance-decayed weights). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Row-standardization** (`w.transform = 'r'`) rescales each row to sum to 1 so [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- the spatial lag is a neighbor *average*; usually required before Moran's I / [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Measures whether similar values cluster in space ([Geographic Data Science with [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Python, ch.7 Local Autocorrelation, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://geographicdata.science/book/notebooks/07_local_autocorrelation.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2023](https://r-spatial.org/book/15-Measures.html)): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Global Moran's I**: one statistic for the whole map: positive ⇒ clustering, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- ~0 ⇒ spatial randomness, negative ⇒ dispersion/checkerboard. Significance via [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- permutation inference (`esda.Moran`). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Geary's C**: ranges ~0–2 (1 = no autocorrelation); more sensitive to *local* [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- differences and inversely related to Moran's I but not identical. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **LISA / Local Moran's I** (`esda.Moran_Local`): decomposes the global [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- statistic per location, classifying significant units into **HH, LL** (spatial [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- clusters) and **HL, LH** (spatial outliers); visualize with a Moran scatterplot [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- and LISA cluster map (`splot`). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Analyzes the locations of events themselves (not attribute values), testing [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- against **Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR)** ([Geographic Data Science with [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Python, ch.8 Point Pattern Analysis, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://geographicdata.science/book/notebooks/08_point_pattern_analysis.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2025](http://pysal.org/pointpats/)): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Kernel Density Estimation (KDE)**: smooth continuous intensity surface [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (hotspot map); bandwidth choice dominates the result. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Nearest-neighbor / G & F functions**: distribution of nearest-neighbor [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- distances; clustered if observed distances < CSR expectation. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Ripley's K (and the variance-stabilized L)**: counts neighbors within [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- increasing radii to test clustering vs dispersion *across scales*; assess [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- against simulation envelopes. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Predict values at unsampled locations from sampled points ([pygis, Spatial [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Interpolation, 2024](https://pygis.io/docs/e_interpolation.html); [Columbia MSPH, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Kriging Interpolation, 2024](https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/research/population-health-methods/kriging-interpolation); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **IDW (Inverse Distance Weighting)**: deterministic; weight ∝ 1/dist^p. Simple, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- no uncertainty estimate, prone to "bull's-eyes." [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Kriging**: geostatistical; weights derive from a fitted **variogram** [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (semi-variance vs lag distance), so it accounts for spatial structure *and* [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- yields prediction variance. **Ordinary kriging** assumes an unknown constant [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- mean; PyKrige supports linear/power/spherical/gaussian/exponential variogram [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- models and 2D/3D ordinary & universal kriging. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Forward **geocoding** = address → coordinates; **reverse geocoding** = coordinates [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- → address. `geopy` wraps providers (OSM **Nominatim** = free, Google/Bing/etc.). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Wrap calls in `geopy.extra.rate_limiter.RateLimiter` and set a unique [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `user_agent` — Nominatim enforces ≤1 req/s and bans bulk abuse ([GeoPy 2.4 docs, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://geopy.readthedocs.io/); [Spatial Dev Guru, Geocoding with geopy, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2023](https://spatial-dev.guru/2023/03/12/geocoding-and-reverse-geocoding-in-python-using-geopy/)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- A **choropleth** shades areal units by a value; the **classification scheme** [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (binning) drives the visual message ([Geographic Data Science with Python, ch.5 [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://geographicdata.science/book/notebooks/05_choropleth.html); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Choropleth data classification, 2024](https://gisgeography.com/choropleth-maps-data-classification/)): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Equal Interval**: equal value ranges; intuitive but skewed data collapses [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Quantiles**: equal *count* per class; good general-purpose readability but [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- can place similar values in different classes. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Natural Breaks (Fisher-Jenks)**: minimizes within-class variance, maximizes [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- between-class variance; respects data structure but breaks aren't comparable [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Always **normalize counts to rates/densities** before mapping, and use [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `mapclassify` (`NaturalBreaks`, `Quantiles`, `EqualInterval`, `FisherJenks`). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Standard OLS on spatial data violates the independence assumption; residuals are [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- autocorrelated. Two model families ([Spatial Modelling for Data Scientists, ch.9 [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- GWR, 2024](https://gdsl-ul.github.io/san/09-gwr.html); [Esri, GWR tool reference, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/tool-reference/spatial-statistics/geographically-weighted-regression.htm); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- PySAL `spreg`/`mgwr`): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Spatial lag model (SAR)**: adds a spatially-lagged *dependent* variable [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (Wy); models spillover/interdependence between units. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Spatial error model (SEM)**: autocorrelation in the *error* term (Wε); [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- unmodeled spatially-structured omitted variables. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Choose between them with Lagrange Multiplier diagnostics in `spreg`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR)**: fits a *local* regression at each [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- location with distance-weighted neighbors, producing spatially-varying [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- coefficients (models **non-stationarity**, not interdependence). Watch local [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- multicollinearity and bandwidth selection. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Shapely 2.x**: geometry engine (GEOS); vectorized ops on geometry arrays. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **GeoPandas 1.x** (2026): pandas + Shapely + pyproj + Fiona/pyogrio; the [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Python workhorse for vector I/O, CRS, joins, overlay, plotting. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **PostGIS**: spatial extension for PostgreSQL; production spatial SQL with GiST [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- indexes; the most feature-complete OSS spatial engine. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **PySAL**: spatial *statistics* (libpysal weights, esda autocorrelation, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- pointpats, mapclassify, spreg/mgwr regression). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **H3 / S2**: DGGS libraries for binning, indexing, and ML features. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **DuckDB spatial extension**: `INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;`; fast in-process [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- analytical spatial SQL, reads/writes GeoParquet; lighter than PostGIS but fewer [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- functions ([DuckDB Spatial Extension docs, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2025](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/spatial/overview)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Apache Sedona / SedonaDB**: distributed (Spark) and single-node (SedonaDB, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- released 2025) engines treating spatial as first-class; for cluster-scale data [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- ([Apache Sedona, Introducing SedonaDB, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2025](https://sedona.apache.org/latest/blog/2025/09/24/introducing-sedonadb-a-single-node-analytical-database-engine-with-geospatial-as-a-first-class-citizen/)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **kepler.gl 3.1**: browser-based large-scale visualization; embeds DuckDB to [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- query GeoParquet client-side ([Foursquare, Kepler.gl 3.1, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2024](https://foursquare.com/resources/blog/products/foursquare-brings-enterprise-grade-spatial-analytics-to-your-browser-with-kepler-gl-3-1/)). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **GeoParquet**: columnar, compressed interchange format read by GeoPandas, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- DuckDB, Sedona, QGIS, kepler.gl; the emerging standard for analytical vector [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Tool selection** ([Forrest, Geospatial Tools Compared, [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- 2025](https://forrest.nyc/geospatial-tools-compared-when-to-use-geopandas-postgis-duckdb-apache-sedona-and-wherobots/)): [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- single-machine exploration/notebooks → GeoPandas; persistent transactional [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- spatial DB → PostGIS; fast analytical queries on files → DuckDB; cluster-scale [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- batch → Sedona; spatial statistics/modeling → PySAL. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Ingest & set CRS**: load, confirm `.crs`; `set_crs` if missing, never to fix [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Reproject**: `to_crs` to a **metric/projected CRS** (UTM via [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `estimate_utm_crs()`) before any distance/area/buffer step. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Clean geometry**: fix invalidities (`make_valid`/`buffer(0)`), drop [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- empties, set precision. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Build/attach index**: rely on `.sindex` / GiST; for binning encode H3/S2. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Operate**: joins, overlays, geometric ops. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Analyze**: build weights → ESDA (Moran/LISA) → point pattern / interpolation [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- / spatial regression as the question demands. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Communicate**: choropleth with a justified classifier on normalized rates; [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- interactive map (kepler.gl/folium) for exploration. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Reproject to UTM/equal-area **before** measuring length, area, or buffering; [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- back to 4326/3857 only for output/display. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Pre-filter with the spatial index (or H3 cell join) before exact predicate [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- tests on large datasets. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Use H3 to turn messy point data into tidy, joinable grid features for ML and [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Map **rates/densities**, not raw counts; pick the classifier deliberately [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (quantiles for readability, Jenks for structure, equal interval for comparison). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Push heavy joins/aggregations into DuckDB-spatial or PostGIS; keep GeoPandas for [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Computing distance/area in EPSG:4326**: degrees aren't meters; results are [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- nonsense and vary with latitude. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **`set_crs` to "fix" wrong coordinates**: it only relabels; you need `to_crs` [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (or the correct source CRS). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Mixing CRS across layers**: silently wrong joins/overlays; always reproject [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- to a common CRS first. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Using Web Mercator for area/statistics**: extreme high-latitude distortion; [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- use an equal-area projection. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Skipping row-standardization of W** before Moran's I / spatial lag. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Mapping raw counts as a choropleth** (population artifact) instead of rates. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Bulk-hammering Nominatim** without rate-limiting/user_agent — gets you banned. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- **Trusting OLS on spatial data** without checking residual autocorrelation. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *"Geometry is in a geographic CRS. Results may be incorrect" (GeoPandas [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- warning)* → reproject to a projected CRS before the area/length/buffer op. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *Empty/NaN spatial join result* → CRS mismatch between layers, or wrong [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- `predicate`; check `.crs` on both and the relationship direction [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- (within vs contains). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *`TopologyException` / invalid geometry* → run `make_valid()` or `buffer(0)`; [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- inspect with `.is_valid` and `.explain_validity`. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *Moran's I ≈ 0 but a visible pattern* → wrong/under-connected weights (try [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- Queen vs KNN), or scale mismatch; verify W connectivity (no islands). [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *Kriging variogram won't fit* → too few points, duplicate coordinates, or wrong [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- model; try IDW as a baseline and inspect the empirical variogram. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *H3/geohash boundary artifacts* → neighbors split across cells; buffer the query [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- or use `grid_disk`/`kRing` to include adjacent cells. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- *DuckDB function missing* → spatial coverage is narrower than PostGIS; fall back [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
- to PostGIS/GeoPandas for that op. [src: da-26-geospatial-analytics]
