- The discipline of structuring data for analytics: how to shape facts, dimensions, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- and layered models so a warehouse or lakehouse is queryable, consistent, and [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- maintainable. This skill covers the **modeling** decisions, not the engines or [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- pipelines that move the data. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Scope boundaries.** Document/NoSQL schema design → `mongodb-schema-design`. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Ingestion/orchestration/ETL → `da-13-data-engineering-and-pipelines`. Metric & [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- headless-BI semantic layer → `da-18-semantic-layer-headless-bi`. OLAP engine [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- internals → `da-28-realtime-olap-databases`. This skill owns the analytical [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- modeling discipline that those skills sit on top of. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Dimensional modeling organizes data into **fact tables** (numeric measurements of [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- a business process) and **dimension tables** (the descriptive "who/what/where/ [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- when/why/how" context, wide and denormalized). Instantiated in a relational DB [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- this is a **star schema**: a central fact table joined to dimensions via [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- primary/foreign keys. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Four-step design process** (always in this order): [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Select the business process** (e.g. orders, shipments, web sessions) — a [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- process produces one or more fact tables, not a department or report. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Declare the grain** — exactly what one fact row represents. This is the [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- pivotal step; every candidate dimension and fact must be consistent with it. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Prefer the lowest (atomic) grain — it is the most flexible and future-proof. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Identify the dimensions** — descriptive context that applies at that grain. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Identify the facts** — numeric measures valid at that grain. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Star vs snowflake.** A star keeps each dimension as one flat denormalized table. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- A **snowflake** normalizes dimension hierarchies into sub-tables (e.g. product → [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- brand → category). Kimball discourages snowflaking: it saves little storage, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- complicates queries, and hurts BI-tool usability. Normalize a dimension only for [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- genuine outriggers or very large/volatile sub-hierarchies. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Fact additivity.** Facts are *additive* (summable across all dimensions, e.g. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- sales amount), *semi-additive* (summable across some dims but not time, e.g. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- account balances, inventory levels — use periodic snapshots), or *non-additive* [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- (ratios, percentages — store the numerator and denominator as additive facts and [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- compute the ratio at query time, never store the ratio). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: Kimball Group, [Four-Step Design Process](https://www.kimballgroup.com/data-warehouse-business-intelligence-resources/kimball-techniques/dimensional-modeling-techniques/four-4-step-design-process/); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- A **conformed dimension** is shared across multiple fact tables/business processes [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- with identical keys, attribute names, and meanings (or one is a perfect subset of [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- the other). Conformed dimensions are what let you **drill across** and integrate [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- results from different processes (e.g. compare Sales and Returns by the same [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Customer and Date dimensions). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- The **bus matrix** is the planning artifact: **rows = business processes**, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **columns = dimensions**, shaded cells mark which dims a process uses. Scanning a [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- column shows where a dimension must be conformed. The matrix is how a team plans [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- incremental, integrated delivery (deliver one process/data mart at a time, but [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- plan the shared dimension bus up front so marts integrate later). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: Kimball Group, [Enterprise DW Bus Matrix](https://www.kimballgroup.com/data-warehouse-business-intelligence-resources/kimball-techniques/dimensional-modeling-techniques/enterprise-data-warehouse-bus-matrix/); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- How to handle dimension attributes that change over time. The three basics are [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- type 1, 2, 3; the rest are hybrids. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Type 2 is the workhorse — most "track history" requirements resolve to type 2. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: Kimball Group, [Design Tip #152: SCD Types 0,4,5,6,7, 2013](https://www.kimballgroup.com/2013/02/design-tip-152-slowly-changing-dimension-types-0-4-5-6-7/); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- The accumulating snapshot is the only type whose rows are routinely **updated**. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Factless tables answer "did it happen / what was eligible" questions. The three [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- core types complement each other and often coexist for the same process. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: Kimball Group, [Periodic Snapshot](https://www.kimballgroup.com/data-warehouse-business-intelligence-resources/kimball-techniques/dimensional-modeling-techniques/periodic-snapshot-fact-table/); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Surrogate keys** — meaningless integer (or hash) primary keys on dimensions, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- generated by the warehouse. Required for SCD type 2 (each version gets its own [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- key), insulates the warehouse from source-system key changes/reuse, and joins [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- faster than wide natural keys. Facts carry surrogate FKs, not business keys. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Natural / business keys** — the source-system identifier (e.g. `customer_id`). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Keep it as a **durable attribute** on the dimension; under type 2 it is *not* [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- unique (it repeats across versions). The durable key joins all versions of an [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Degenerate dimension** — a dimension key with no attributes of its own, stored [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- directly on the fact (e.g. order number, invoice number, ticket ID). No separate [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Role-playing dimension** — one physical dimension referenced multiple times in [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- one fact under different roles (e.g. Date as order_date, ship_date, due_date). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Expose via views/aliases with role-specific column names. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Junk dimension** — a single table collecting low-cardinality flags and [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- indicators (yes/no, status codes) that would otherwise clutter the fact, holding [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- the distinct combinations actually observed. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: Kimball Group, [Dimensional Modeling Techniques index](https://www.kimballgroup.com/data-warehouse-business-intelligence-resources/kimball-techniques/dimensional-modeling-techniques/); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Data Vault 2.0 building blocks** (Dan Linstedt): **Hubs** store unique business [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- keys; **Links** store the relationships (often M:N) between hubs; **Satellites** [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- store descriptive attributes and their history, are **append-only** (every change [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- is preserved, like type-2 history), and hang off hubs or links. DV2.0 adds hash [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- keys, hash diffs, and load metadata for parallel, scalable, auditable loads. The [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- raw vault is *not* a query layer — you build dimensional marts on top for users. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- A common real-world pattern is **hybrid**: an Inmon/3NF or Data Vault integration [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- core feeding Kimball star-schema marts for consumption. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: [Keboola — Kimball vs Inmon](https://www.keboola.com/blog/kimball-vs-inmon); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Modern columnar MPP warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Databricks SQL) [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- change the normalization math. Columnar storage with run-length/dictionary [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- encoding makes repeated dimension values cheap, and join-heavy star queries incur [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- cross-node shuffles. So a fully denormalized **One Big Table** (facts + all [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- dimension attributes pre-joined into one wide table) is often *faster* than a star. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Benchmarks: OBT ~10-45% faster than star across many queries; BigQuery ~49% [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- average improvement (parallel engine, fewer shuffles). Snowflake is **mixed** — [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- the star sometimes wins on simpler queries, so test on your engine. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **OBT cost**: heavy redundancy and painful updates — renaming one product means [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- rewriting millions of rows, vs a one-row dimension update in a star. SCD history [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- is also awkward in an OBT. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Recommended hybrid (2024-2026)**: keep a **star schema in the silver layer** [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- for integrity, history (SCD), and exploration; **materialize OBT/wide tables in [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- the gold layer** to power high-concurrency BI dashboards. dbt makes this a single [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- extra model — build the OBT as a `ref()` over your dimensional marts. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Don't reflexively denormalize: a star is still the better default when you need [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- SCD history, frequent dimension updates, governed conformed dimensions, or [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- ad-hoc exploration. Reach for OBT for read-heavy, high-concurrency dashboard [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: [Fivetran — Star Schema vs OBT](https://www.fivetran.com/blog/star-schema-vs-obt); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- A lakehouse layering pattern that progressively improves data quality: [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Bronze** — raw landing, source structure "as-is" plus ingest metadata [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- (load timestamp, source file, process ID). Append/immutable; no business logic. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Silver** — cleansed, conformed, deduplicated, type-cast; matched and merged [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- to an "enterprise view" of key business entities ("just-enough" cleaning). This [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- is the natural home for normalized/3NF or dimensional integration models. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Gold** — business-level aggregates, dimensional marts, and OBT/wide tables [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- ready for BI, reporting, and ML features. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- It is a **reference architecture, not a mandate** — add or remove layers to fit. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Databricks guidance: don't write to silver directly from ingestion (schema [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- drift / corrupt records); prefer streaming reads from bronze for append-only [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- sources; use Unity Catalog with a separate catalog/schema per layer. Medallion [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- is *orthogonal* to Kimball/Inmon/Data Vault — those describe how you model [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- *within* a layer (typically silver and gold). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: [Databricks — What is Medallion Architecture](https://www.databricks.com/blog/what-is-medallion-architecture); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- dbt's recommended **3-layer structure** maps cleanly onto medallion silver/gold: [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Staging** (`stg_<source>__<entity>`) — one model per source table, **1:1** [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- with the source. Rename/recast/clean only; no joins. Materialize as **views**. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Organize subfolders **by source system**. Define raw inputs as **sources** in [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- YAML and reference them with `source()`. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Intermediate** (`int_<concept>`) — purpose-built transformation steps that [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- combine a handful (~4-6) of staging models. Shift to **business-conformed** [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- subfolders by area of concern. Ideal as **ephemeral** (interpolated as CTEs). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Marts** (`fct_<process>`, `dim_<entity>`, or plain entity names) — the [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- business-defined fact and dimension tables, each at its own grain. Materialize [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- as **tables** (or incremental). If a mart pulls together more than ~4-5 [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- concepts, factor out intermediate models. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **`ref()` and `source()`** build the DAG: models reference each other with [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- `ref('model_name')` and raw tables with `source('schema','table')`, so dbt infers [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- lineage and build order. Set defaults per folder in `dbt_project.yml` (e.g. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- staging→view, marts→table, separate schemas per layer). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Five built-in materializations**: `view` (default, logic only, instant/cheap), [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- `table` (stores data), `incremental` (only transform new/changed rows), `ephemeral` [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- (no DB object, inlined as a CTE), `materialized_view` (platform-managed refresh of [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- incremental logic). Choose incremental for large append-mostly facts; views for [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- staging; tables for marts users hit directly. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: dbt Labs, [How we structure our dbt projects](https://docs.getdbt.com/best-practices/how-we-structure/1-guide-overview) [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- ([Staging](https://docs.getdbt.com/best-practices/how-we-structure/2-staging), [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Physical model** — the actual tables/views in the warehouse: facts, dims, marts, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- OBTs, their grain, keys, types, and materializations. This is everything above. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Semantic model** — a metadata layer *on top* of the physical marts that defines [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- metrics, dimensions, and join paths once, so every BI tool computes "revenue" or [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- "active users" identically (avoids metric drift). In dbt this is the Semantic [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Layer / MetricFlow; semantic marts sit above physical marts. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Keep physical marts clean and conformed; express reusable business metrics in the [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- semantic layer rather than baking every aggregate into a physical table. **Deep [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- semantic-layer / headless-BI work belongs to `da-18-semantic-layer-headless-bi`** — [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- this skill stops at the modeling boundary and the handoff. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Sources: dbt Labs, [Semantic structure / semantic-layer marts](https://docs.getdbt.com/best-practices/how-we-structure/5-semantic-layer-marts); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- -- [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Always declare the grain in one sentence before modeling anything.** "One row [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- per ___." If you can't, you don't understand the process yet. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Model the atomic grain first.** Aggregates are derivable; you can't drill into [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- detail you didn't keep. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Plan the dimension bus up front, deliver marts incrementally.** Conform Date, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Customer, Product early — retrofitting conformance is painful. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Default dimension change handling = type 2 with surrogate keys**, unless the [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- business explicitly only wants the current value (type 1) or "original" (type 0). [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Store additive components, not ratios.** Compute percentages/averages at query [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- time from additive numerator+denominator facts. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Hybrid layering**: 3NF/Data-Vault or conformed star in silver for integrity + [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- history; OBT/wide tables in gold for dashboard speed. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **In dbt**: staging=views 1:1 with sources, intermediate=ephemeral, marts=tables; [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- one fact/dim concept per mart at its own grain. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Mixed grain in one fact table** — the cardinal sin; forces double-counting. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Split into separate fact tables. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Storing non-additive ratios** as facts — they can't be summed correctly. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Snowflaking everything** — normalizing dimensions for "cleanliness"; hurts [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- usability and performance with negligible storage gain on columnar engines. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Smart/natural keys as fact FKs** — couples the warehouse to source key changes [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- and breaks SCD type 2. Use surrogate keys. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Reflexive OBT everywhere** — denormalizing without considering update cost, [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- SCD history, or that Snowflake sometimes favors the star. Benchmark your engine. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Writing to silver directly from ingestion** — schema drift and bad records [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- leak in; always land in bronze first. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Reports as the design driver** — designing the fact table around a specific [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- report instead of the physical measurement event; build at the atomic event [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- grain and let reports aggregate. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Baking every metric into physical tables** — causes metric drift; define [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- reusable metrics in the semantic layer. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Numbers double-count when joining two facts** → you joined fact-to-fact. Never [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- do that; drill across via conformed dimensions and combine aggregated results. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Totals wrong after summing a snapshot over time** → the fact is semi-additive [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- (balances/levels); don't sum across the time dimension — take a point-in-time or [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Dimension table row count exploding** → a fast-changing attribute under type 2; [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- split it into a type-4 mini-dimension. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Can't reproduce a historical report** → attributes were handled as type 1 [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- (overwritten). Convert the relevant attributes to type 2. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Star query slow / shuffling on columnar DW** → consider a gold-layer OBT/wide [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- table for that dashboard; keep the star for exploration. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **Same metric differs across dashboards** → metric defined per-report in physical [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- tables; move it to the semantic layer. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- **dbt build slow / rebuilding huge facts every run** → switch the large fact mart [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- from `table` to `incremental`. [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]

- dbt Labs — [How we structure our dbt projects](https://docs.getdbt.com/best-practices/how-we-structure/1-guide-overview); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Data Vault — [Scalefree DV2.0 Definition](https://www.scalefree.com/consulting/data-vault-2-0/); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Inmon vs Kimball — [Keboola (2024)](https://www.keboola.com/blog/kimball-vs-inmon); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- Medallion — [Databricks — What is Medallion Architecture](https://www.databricks.com/blog/what-is-medallion-architecture); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- OBT vs Star — [Fivetran — Star Schema vs OBT](https://www.fivetran.com/blog/star-schema-vs-obt); [src: da-29-dimensional-data-modeling]
- A **recommender system** predicts, for each user, which items from a (often huge) catalog they are most likely to engage with, then **orders** a small slate to show. As a data-analysis discipline it sits at the intersection of three problems: (1) *modeling* preference from sparse interaction data, (2) *ranking* candidates under a relevance objective, and (3) *evaluating* both offline and online while fighting the bias the system itself creates. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Scope boundaries (read first):** [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **vs da-7 (machine learning):** da-7 covers generic supervised/unsupervised model training, regularization, and hyperparameter tuning. da-38 covers the *recommendation- and ranking-specific* objectives (BPR/WRMF losses, NDCG-aware LambdaMART), the retrieve-then-rank funnel, and recsys evaluation. Use da-7 for "train a classifier"; use da-38 for "rank items for a user." [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **vs da-27 (network/graph analytics):** da-27 owns graph structure metrics (centrality, community detection, link prediction *as graph analysis*, GNNs as graph models). da-38 references GNN-for-recsys and bipartite user-item graphs only at the *recommendation* level; graph-structure questions belong to da-27. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **vs da-12 (A/B testing & causal inference):** da-12 owns general experiment design and causal estimators. da-38 owns the *recsys-specific* online-eval wrinkles: interleaving, feedback-loop confounding, and off-policy/counterfactual evaluation (IPS, doubly-robust) of a ranking policy. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **vs rag-architecture / vector search:** semantic retrieval with no personalization or ranking-quality objective is RAG; ranked personalization is da-38. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Explicit vs implicit feedback.** *Explicit* = ratings/likes (sparse, signed). *Implicit* = clicks, views, dwell, purchases (abundant but **positive-only and ambiguous** — a non-click is not a dislike). Implicit dominates production and forces *positive-unlabeled* modeling: model **confidence** that an interaction is a preference, not a rating value. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Popularity bias & the feedback loop.** A deployed recommender only logs feedback on items it *showed*, chosen because they scored high — so the next training set over-represents popular/previously-recommended items (**exposure bias**). Unchecked, a self-reinforcing loop narrows the catalog and creates **filter bubbles**. Breaking it needs exploration and/or de-biasing (propensity weighting). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Cold-start, three flavors.** *User* (new user), *item* (new item), *system* (brand-new product). Mitigations: content/side features, hybrid models, factorization machines, popularity fallbacks, bandit exploration, and (2025-26) LLM/semantic-ID content grounding for long-tail items. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- CF predicts preference purely from the user-item interaction matrix, no content. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **User-user CF:** find similar users (cosine/Pearson on co-rated items). Sensitive to sparsity; similarities go stale. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Item-item CF:** precompute item-item similarity ("users who interacted with X also interacted with Y"). More stable than user-user, scales better, Amazon's production workhorse, still a strong baseline. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Limitations:** cold-start, sparsity, popularity skew, no side features — motivating latent-factor models. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- Factor R ≈ **P·Qᵀ** into low-rank user (P) and item (Q) latent factors; prediction = pᵤ·qᵢ. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **SVD / funkSVD.** Not literal SVD — learns factors by **SGD on observed entries only** with L2 regularization plus user/item **bias terms**. SVD++ adds implicit signal. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **ALS.** Fix P, solve Q in closed form, alternate. Parallel → standard for large distributed (Spark) training. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Implicit-feedback MF / WRMF (Hu-Koren-Volinsky 2008).** Treat all entries; weight observed interactions by **confidence** cᵤᵢ = 1 + α·rᵤᵢ; fit preference (0/1) with weighted ALS. What `implicit`'s `AlternatingLeastSquares` does. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **BPR — Bayesian Personalized Ranking (Rendle 2009).** **Pairwise ranking** objective for implicit feedback: maximize σ(x̂ᵤᵢ − x̂ᵤⱼ) over sampled (user, pos, neg) triples. Optimizes ranking (AUC), not rating error — better top-N fit than pointwise MF. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Content-based:** recommend items similar to liked ones via item features → good for item cold-start, over-specializes (no serendipity). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Hybrid:** combine CF + content (weighted, switching, feature-augmented, cascade). Solves cold-start, keeps collaborative signal. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Factorization Machines (FM, Rendle 2010):** model all pairwise feature interactions with low-rank factorized weights — generalizes MF to arbitrary side features, natively handles cold-start. **FFM (field-aware)** gives each feature a latent vector per *field* — strong for CTR. **DeepFM** shares an embedding between a wide FM (low-order) and a deep DNN (high-order), no manual crosses — standard CTR/ranking model. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Two-tower retrieval.** Separate **user/query tower** and **item tower** into a shared embedding space; relevance = dot product. Item embeddings precomputed and indexed in an ANN/vector store → sub-linear nearest-neighbor lookup → dominant **candidate-generation** architecture (TorchRec's headline target). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Neural CF (NCF):** replace the MF dot product with an MLP — more expressive (though a tuned dot product is a strong baseline). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Sequential / session-based:** **GRU4Rec** (RNN over session events); **SASRec** (*causal* left-to-right self-attention, next-item); **BERT4Rec** (*bidirectional* self-attention, masked-item cloze training). **Caveat:** with the *same* loss, SASRec generally matches or beats BERT4Rec at lower cost — BERT4Rec's edge often came from its training objective, not bidirectionality. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **LLM-augmented & generative recommenders (2025-2026).** **Semantic IDs**: quantize an item's content embedding (RQ-VAE) into a short code that reflects content → generalizes to **cold-start/long-tail** and slots into an LLM vocabulary (YouTube, Spotify gains). **Generative retrieval**: an LLM *generates* the next item's semantic ID instead of scoring a candidate set. **LLMs as data augmenters / rerankers** and knowledge-guided RAG (ColdRAG) for cold-start — watch LLM-reranker exposure/coverage issues. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- Directly optimize the *order* of a candidate list given relevance labels/features. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Pointwise** — predict each item's relevance independently; ignores list context. Weakest ranking fidelity. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Pairwise** — learn from item pairs. **RankNet** (neural, pairwise cross-entropy) is the archetype; its loss correlates only loosely with NDCG. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Listwise** — optimize the whole list. **ListNet** uses Plackett-Luce permutation probability; **LambdaRank/LambdaMART** weight pairwise gradients by **ΔNDCG**, directly targeting NDCG. **LambdaMART** (LambdaRank gradients + gradient-boosted trees) is the workhorse — XGBoost (`rank:ndcg`), LightGBM, RankLib. Pairwise-vs-listwise is *how the loss treats the list*, not the model family. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Retrieval → ranking → re-ranking funnel.** (1) **candidate generation** — cheap, high-recall, millions→hundreds (two-tower+ANN, item-item, popularity); (2) **ranking** — expensive, high-precision scorer (DeepFM/LambdaMART/DLRM); (3) **re-ranking** — business rules, diversity (MMR), freshness, fairness, exploration on the top slate. Each stage trades recall for precision. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- Evaluate on held-out interactions (time-based split more honest than random). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Accuracy @k:** **Precision@k**, **Recall@k**, **Hit Rate@k**, **MAP** (order-aware), **MRR** (rank of first relevant — best when one correct answer, e.g. next-item), **NDCG@k** (graded, position-discounted — the headline metric). Empirically cluster: {Recall}, {MRR, NDCG, HR}, {Precision, MAP}. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Beyond-accuracy:** **Coverage**, **Diversity** (intra-list dissimilarity), **Novelty** (non-popularity), **Serendipity** (relevant *and* surprising). Optimizing accuracy alone degrades these. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Offline/online gap.** Offline metrics measure fit to *logged* (biased) behavior. Higher offline NDCG does **not** guarantee online lift; too much novelty can hurt novice users. Treat offline as a *filter*, beware sampled-negative distortion and random-split leakage. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **A/B testing** is the gold standard, but recommenders create **feedback loops** that contaminate populations over time — keep tests short, watch novelty/interference. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Interleaving** mixes two rankers into one list per user and attributes clicks → far more sensitive than A/B (Airbnb search). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Counterfactual / off-policy evaluation (OPE):** **IPS** (weight by 1/propensity — unbiased but high variance, clip it); **Direct Method** (reward model — low variance, biased if misspecified); **Doubly Robust** (DM+IPS — unbiased if *either* model is correct, lower variance; standard for large action spaces). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Two-stage serving** (candidate gen vs ranking); embeddings in a **vector/ANN store**, features in a **feature store** (Feast) shared across train/serve to prevent skew. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Real-time features & embeddings:** session/recency features computed at request time; huge embedding tables sharded (TorchRec). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Exploration vs exploitation:** **contextual bandits** (LinUCB, **Thompson sampling**) inject controlled exploration to break feedback loops; ε-greedy/random injection in re-ranking mitigates filter bubbles. Caveat (RecSys 2025): in pure offline eval, greedy models often *appear* to beat bandits — a structural eval bias. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Fairness & filter bubbles:** monitor provider-side exposure fairness, popularity bias, diversity; randomization/fairness constraints in re-ranking. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Frame the problem.** Implicit/explicit? Top-N, CTR, or next-item? Decides loss (BPR/WRMF vs pointwise vs LambdaMART) and metric (Recall@k/NDCG vs MRR). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Baseline first.** Popularity + item-item CF + WRMF/BPR — many "deep" wins vanish against a tuned MF baseline. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Split honestly.** Time-based (leave-last-out per user); avoid leakage; beware sampled-negative metrics. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Add structure as needed.** Side features → FM/LightFM/DeepFM; sequence → SASRec; cold-start → content + semantic IDs. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Build the funnel** at scale: two-tower retrieval → DeepFM/LambdaMART ranker → diversity/fairness/exploration re-rank. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Evaluate in layers:** offline → off-policy (IPS/DR) → interleaving → A/B. Never ship on offline alone. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Close the loop safely:** log propensities, add exploration, monitor popularity bias and exposure fairness. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Trusting offline NDCG as ground truth** — confirm online. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Treating implicit non-interactions as negatives** — they're unlabeled; use confidence weighting (WRMF) or sampled pairwise negatives (BPR). [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Random split for sequential/temporal data** — leaks the future. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Assuming BERT4Rec > SASRec** — loss, not bidirectionality, drove the gap. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Optimizing accuracy only** — tanks coverage/diversity/serendipity and feeds the feedback loop. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Raw IPS with no clipping** — variance explodes; clip or use doubly-robust. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]
- **Deep model with no MF/CF baseline** — can't claim a win without the bar. [src: da-38-recommender-systems-and-ranking]

- Pricing and revenue analytics is the analytical discipline of estimating how **price** [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- moves **demand, revenue, and margin**, and converting those estimates into pricing [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- decisions. It sits at the intersection of microeconomics (demand theory, elasticity), [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- econometrics (causal estimation under price endogeneity), survey/choice methodology [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- (stated- and revealed-preference WTP), and operations research (constrained price [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- optimization). The defining question is always *"what happens to quantity, revenue, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- and margin if we change the price?"* — distinct from forecasting a time series, from [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- attributing marketing spend, or from generic optimization. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Scope boundary (what this skill is NOT):** [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **da-15-forecasting** — predicting demand/revenue forward in time with no price [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- decision lever. This skill uses demand *models* where price is the causal driver. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **da-22-marketing-mix-modeling** — decomposing sales into media/promo/base with [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- adstock and saturation for *budget* allocation. Promotion analytics here is the [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- *price-discount* slice (lift, cannibalization, pantry-loading), not media ROI. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **da-33-prescriptive-analytics** — the LP/MILP/convex solver machinery and decision [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- science generally. This skill *applies* that machinery to the pricing objective [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- (profit/revenue subject to elasticity and business constraints) and frames it. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **da-12-ab-testing-causal-inference** — experiment design and causal theory in [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- general. Here we cover only the *price-specific* experiment and its pitfalls. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Own-price elasticity** e = (%dQ)/(%dP); demand is **elastic** (|e|>1), **unit-elastic** [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- (|e|=1), or **inelastic** (|e|<1). Revenue is maximized at |e|=1; **profit**-maximizing [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- price sits where |e|>1 (you never price in the inelastic region with positive marginal cost). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Cross-price elasticity** e_AB = (%dQ_A)/(%dP_B): positive = substitutes, negative = [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- complements. The full **own/cross elasticity matrix** drives portfolio and cannibalization analysis. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Functional forms.** *Linear* demand Q = a - bP gives elasticity that varies along the [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- curve. *Log-log / constant-elasticity* ln Q = a + b ln P makes b the (constant) elasticity [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- directly — the workhorse spec. *Semi-log* ln Q = a + bP gives a constant *semi-elasticity*. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Add ln P_competitor, promo flags, seasonality, and ln income as controls. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Arc vs point elasticity:** arc (midpoint) elasticity for two discrete price points; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- point elasticity = derivative-based, read off a fitted curve. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **The Lerner / inverse-elasticity rule:** at the optimum, (P - MC)/P = 1/|e|. Markup is [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- the inverse of elasticity — the bridge from a fitted elasticity to an optimal price. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **The core problem:** price is **not exogenous**. Firms set high prices when they expect [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- high demand (demand shocks correlate with price), and OLS on ln Q ~ ln P is biased — [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- typically *toward zero / upward-sloping*, understating true elasticity. This is the central [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- technical pitfall in observational pricing work. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Instrumental variables (IV / 2SLS):** find a variable that shifts price but is [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- uncorrelated with the demand shock. Standard instruments: [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Cost shifters** — input costs, wages, exchange rates, fuel, freight. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Hausman instruments** — prices of the same product in *other markets* (common cost [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- shock, independent local demand shock); criticized when demand shocks are correlated [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- across markets (e.g. national advertising). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **BLP instruments** — characteristics of *rival* products in the same market. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Wholesale/list price as instrument for retail price; promotion calendars set in advance. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Diagnostics:** first-stage F (weak-instrument rule of thumb F>10; use effective F / [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Montiel-Olea-Pflueger for robustness), over-identification (Sargan/Hansen J), [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- endogeneity test (Durbin-Wu-Hausman). Weak instruments are worse than OLS. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Panel fixed effects** (store x week, product, time FE via linearmodels.PanelOLS) [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- absorb confounders and are often combined with IV. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Gaussian-copula control function** (Park & Gupta) — corrects price endogeneity *without* [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- an external instrument by exploiting non-normality of the endogenous regressor; convenient [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- but assumes non-normal price and normal errors, and is fragile in small samples. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Aggregate demand curves** — fit Q(P) (linear, log-log, exponential/decay, logistic) to [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- observed price-quantity points, then read elasticity and optimal price off the curve. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Discrete-choice (random utility) demand** — model the probability a consumer picks a [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- product as a function of its attributes and price: [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Multinomial logit (MNL):** closed-form shares; suffers **IIA** (independence of [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- irrelevant alternatives) -> the **red-bus/blue-bus** problem and unrealistic substitution. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Nested logit (GEV):** groups alternatives into nests, relaxing IIA across nests. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Mixed / random-coefficients logit:** random taste coefficients -> flexible, realistic [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- substitution; no closed form, simulated likelihood. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **BLP (Berry-Levsohn-Pakes):** random-coefficients logit for **differentiated products** [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- using *aggregate market-share* data, with a demand inversion and **GMM** using BLP/cost [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- instruments to handle the endogenous price inside utility. The standard for IO-style [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- market demand and merger/price-change simulation. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- WTP and elasticity fall out of the estimated utility (price coefficient -> marginal utility [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- of income -> WTP for attributes; simulate share changes for elasticities). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter (PSM):** 4 questions (too cheap / cheap-bargain / [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- expensive / too expensive); intersections give Point of Marginal Cheapness (PMC), Point of [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Marginal Expensiveness (PME), Optimal Price Point (OPP), Indifference Price Point (IPP), [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- and the **range of acceptable prices**. Best **early**, for new-to-world products; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- directional only — no demand/volume. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Gabor-Granger:** show each respondent a sequence of specific prices, record purchase [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- intent at each -> builds a **demand curve** and a revenue-maximizing point. Needs a known [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- price range (often follows Van Westendorp). Prone to demand artifacts / anchoring. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Conjoint analysis (choice-based, CBC):** respondents choose among product profiles where [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- price is one attribute among many; estimate part-worth utilities (HB/logit) -> derive WTP, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- share-of-preference simulators, and price elasticities. The gold standard for trade-offs [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- and feature-vs-price decisions. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **MaxDiff (best-worst scaling):** forces respondents to pick best/worst from sets -> a stable [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- ranked importance of features (no scale-use bias). Used to *prioritize* features feeding a [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- conjoint/Gabor-Granger, not to set price directly. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Stated vs revealed preference:** surveys (above) are stated-preference and overstate WTP; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- transaction/experiment data is revealed-preference. Triangulate. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Objective:** revenue-maximizing price (|e|=1) vs **profit-maximizing** price (Lerner rule, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- requires marginal cost). Build a profit function pi(P) = (P - MC)*Q(P) from the fitted demand [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Constrained price optimization:** maximize profit/revenue subject to constraints — price [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- bounds, margin floors, price-ladder/gap rules across a line, MAP (minimum advertised price), [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- cross-elasticity/cannibalization terms, inventory. Solve with scipy.optimize (nonlinear), [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **CVXPY** (convex formulations), or OR-Tools/Gurobi for MILP price-point selection. (Solver [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- mechanics -> da-33; here it's framed as the pricing objective.) [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Yield vs revenue management:** *yield management* = price/allocate a **fixed, perishable** [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- capacity (airline seats, hotel rooms) by segment and time; *revenue management* is the [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- broader discipline (also assortment, overbooking, distribution). EMSR heuristics, booking [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- limits, protection levels. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Dynamic / surge pricing:** prices adjust to real-time demand/inventory; increasingly [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- ML-driven (demand prediction at each candidate price). Watch **perceived-fairness** backlash. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Markdown optimization:** for seasonal/perishable goods, choose the markdown depth and [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- timing that maximizes sell-through revenue before end-of-life. UPPMO = unified pricing, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- promotion & markdown optimization across the lifecycle. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Price laddering / line pricing:** coherent price steps across good-better-best tiers and [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- pack sizes; preserve sensible per-unit ladders to avoid arbitrage and trading-down. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Baseline estimation:** the counterfactual non-promoted sales level. Must strip promo weeks, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- stock-outs, seasonality, and trend; a contaminated baseline misstates lift. Methods: moving- [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- average/regression baselines, structural time-series, or causal-impact-style counterfactuals. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Lift & incrementality:** Lift = Actual - Baseline. Decompose total lift into **true [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- incremental** volume, **pantry-loading/forward-buy** (pulled-forward demand -> post-promo dip), [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **cannibalization** (own promoted SKU steals from sibling SKUs — cross-elasticities), and [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **halo** (lifts adjacent non-promoted items — market-basket/affinity). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Trade-promotion ROI / TPO:** net incremental margin vs promo cost; many promos are [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- ROI-negative once cannibalization and forward-buy are netted out. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- This is the **price-discount** slice of promotion. Media/advertising ROI and adstock -> [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- da-22-marketing-mix-modeling. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Packaging & tiering:** good-better-best, feature gating, seat vs usage vs hybrid pricing; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- 2025 trend toward **usage-based / consumption** pricing (correlates with higher NRR and lower [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Price-volume-mix for ARR:** decompose ARR/MRR growth into new, expansion, contraction, and [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- churn; **NRR = expansion - contraction - gross churn** relative to starting base. Expansion is [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- the dominant lever at scale (often >50% of growth at NRR >=100%). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **WTP segmentation:** estimate WTP by segment (conjoint, surveys, behavioral/usage signals) [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- and align tiers/fences (feature, usage, identity) so each segment self-selects — price [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- discrimination via versioning. (NRR/GRR curve math and retention cohorts -> da-34.) [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **PVM bridge / sales bridge:** decompose the change in revenue or gross margin between two [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- periods into **price**, **volume**, and **mix** effects (plus FX and cost for margin), as a [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- signed **waterfall** from prior-period to current-period margin where every dollar is accounted. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Standard decomposition: Price effect = dP x Q (at a reference); Volume effect = dQ x P; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Mix effect = shift toward higher/lower-margin products at constant total volume. Margin walk [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- adds the COGS side (margin volume effect = sales volume effect - COGS volume effect). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Used in FP&A and commercial reviews to explain *why* margin moved and assign accountability. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Why it's hard/fraught:** charging different customers different prices for the same product [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- raises **fairness, trust, and legal** issues; visible price tests damage trust and, in the EU, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- create exposure (consumer-protection, hidden-test, and location-manipulation rules). Geo or [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- segment splits that correlate with **protected characteristics** risk discriminatory pricing. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Design pitfalls:** price is a high-variance, low-frequency conversion outcome -> low power, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- long runtimes; novelty/anchoring effects; contamination across billing/sales/finance systems; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- honoring the lower price for everyone after the test. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Geo-based tests / matched markets:** randomize or match at the **market** level (designated [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- market areas) instead of user level to avoid within-customer price discrimination and arbitrage; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- use synthetic-control / matched-market analysis for the readout. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Switchback designs:** alternate price A/B over time windows for the whole market when [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- user-level randomization is unethical or infeasible (marketplaces). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Elasticity / regression:** statsmodels (OLS, semi/log-log), linearmodels (IV2SLS, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- PanelOLS for FE + IV) — the standard Python stack for IV elasticity. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Bayesian elasticity & price optimization:** PyMC (priors on elasticity, full posterior of [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- optimal price/profit), PyMC-Marketing (also used for promo/MMM-adjacent work). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Differentiated-products / BLP:** pyblp (Conlon & Gortmaker; v1.x, micro-moments [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- framework, nested/mixed logit tutorials on the Nevo cereal data). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Choice modeling:** biogeme (MNL/nested/mixed logit, hybrid choice), pylogit, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- xlogit (GPU-accelerated mixed logit), apollo (R). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Conjoint / MaxDiff / WTP surveys:** Sawtooth Software (Lighthouse/CBC), Conjointly, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Qualtrics; HB estimation for part-worths. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Constrained price optimization:** scipy.optimize, CVXPY, OR-Tools / Gurobi (see da-33). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Revenue management / markdown:** commercial suites (o9, Blue Yonder, Revionics, Vendavo, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Pricefx, PROS); UPPMO patterns. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Causal/promo readout:** CausalImpact/structural time series for baseline counterfactuals. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Frame the decision** — what price lever, what objective (revenue vs profit vs share), what [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- constraints (margin, ladder, MAP, fairness/legal). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Choose data regime** — observational transactions, panel/scanner, survey/stated-preference, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- or experiment. Decide revealed vs stated preference up front. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Identify causal price effect** — never trust raw OLS; use IV, panel FE, copula CF, or a [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- designed experiment. Validate instrument strength and exogeneity. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Estimate demand** — pick functional form / choice model matching the data and substitution [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- structure; report elasticity matrix with uncertainty. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Optimize** — build profit/revenue function, apply Lerner rule or constrained optimizer; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- simulate scenarios and sensitivity to elasticity uncertainty. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Account for promo/portfolio effects** — net out cannibalization, halo, pantry-loading. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Validate** — out-of-sample, holdout markets, or a controlled price/geo test before rollout. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Communicate** — PVM/margin bridge to explain expected vs realized impact. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Always log-log first** for a quick, interpretable elasticity, then check robustness with a [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- flexible form. A coefficient that comes out *positive* is the classic endogeneity tell. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Pair IV with panel FE** (store x week FE + cost-shifter IV) — FE absorbs persistent confounders, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- IV handles the simultaneity that FE can't. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Sequence WTP methods:** MaxDiff (what matters) -> Van Westendorp (acceptable range) -> [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- Gabor-Granger or CBC (price/demand curve and optimum). [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Use BLP only when you have aggregate share data + differentiated products + endogenous price [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- and need realistic substitution** (merger/price-change simulation); otherwise a mixed logit on [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- individual choice data is simpler. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Decompose every promo** into incremental / pantry / cannibalization / halo before claiming ROI. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Test price at the market (geo) level**, not the user level, to dodge fairness/legal landmines. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Express optimal price as a posterior/range**, not a point — elasticity uncertainty dominates. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Running OLS of ln Q on ln P and reporting the coefficient as "the elasticity"** — ignores [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- price endogeneity; the single most common error in pricing analytics. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Using a weak instrument** (first-stage F < 10) — biased *worse* than OLS; check, don't assume. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Trusting stated-preference WTP as absolute** — surveys overstate; calibrate against behavior. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Plain MNL where substitution matters** — IIA gives the red-bus/blue-bus absurdity; use nested [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Claiming promo lift = total uplift** without netting pantry-loading and cannibalization — [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- inflates ROI and hides portfolio cannibalization. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **User-level price A/B tests** — fairness, trust, and legal exposure; honoring-the-low-price tax. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Optimizing price in the inelastic region with positive MC** — always raise price there. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Mixing up yield vs revenue management**, or treating dynamic pricing as pure profit max while [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- ignoring perceived-fairness backlash. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Positive or near-zero elasticity coefficient** -> endogeneity / reverse causality; instrument [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- price or use a designed test; check for stockout-driven and promo-contaminated weeks. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Wrong-signed cross-elasticities** -> omitted seasonality/promo confounders or collinear prices. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Weak first stage** -> instrument too weak; find a stronger cost shifter, pool markets, or run [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- an experiment instead. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Choice model gives implausible substitution** -> relax IIA (nested/mixed logit); add random [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- coefficients on price. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Van Westendorp range too wide / no clear OPP** -> respondents don't understand the product; [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- add anchoring/context or switch to CBC. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Promo "worked" but margin fell** -> forward-buy/pantry-loading and cannibalization eating the [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- lift; rebuild baseline and decompose. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- **Price test inconclusive** -> underpowered (price is low-frequency, high-variance); lengthen, [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]
- use geo/matched-market design, or model elasticity from history instead. [src: da-40-pricing-and-revenue-analytics]

- How AI **augments or automates the analytical loop** — preparing data, finding insights, answering natural-language questions, and explaining results — instead of a human writing every query and reading every chart. The audience is an analyst, data/BI engineer, or product owner deciding **whether and how** to put an LLM between users and data, and how to keep the answers correct. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Scope boundary.** This skill is about the *AI/LLM layer over analytics*. It deliberately does **not** re-teach: [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- The **semantic/metrics layer itself** → `da-18-semantic-layer-headless-bi`. Here we only cover *how an LLM is grounded in* that layer. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Unstructured-text NLP** (topic modeling, sentiment, NER, text embeddings) → `da-36-text-analytics-nlp`. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Generic ML / LLM training, fine-tuning, eval theory** → `da-7-machine-learning`. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Generic RAG pipeline architecture** with no numeric/analytical angle → `rag-architecture`. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- Gartner (Rita Sallam, 2017) defined **augmented analytics** as using ML/AI to assist **data preparation, insight generation, and insight explanation** to augment how people explore and analyze data. Gartner's evaluation criteria span six capabilities: **ML-assisted insight discovery, NLP/NLQ querying, automated explanations (NLG), data-prep assistance, GenAI integration, and augmented data science**. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- The 2025 evolution is **agentic analytics** (Gartner *Market Guide for Agentic Analytics*, Feb 2025): AI agents that don't just *assist* but **autonomously plan, investigate, and act**. Gartner predicts ~75% of analytics content will use GenAI for contextual intelligence by 2027, evolving toward "autonomous analytics" managing a slice of business processes. The four classic analytics tiers map onto this: **descriptive** (what happened) → **diagnostic** (why) → **predictive** (what will) → **prescriptive** (what to do) — augmented/agentic analytics automates the first two and increasingly drives toward the latter two. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- Natural-Language Query (NLQ) turns a plain-English question into a query against governed data, returns a result, a chart, and (via **NLG**) a written explanation. The non-negotiable lesson of 2024-2026: **accuracy depends on grounding the LLM in a governed semantic model, not the raw schema.** The semantic layer (see `da-18`) supplies business term → table/column/metric mappings, relationships, synonyms, and metric definitions so "revenue" always means the same SQL. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Snowflake Cortex Analyst** is built around a **YAML semantic model** (now **Semantic Views** as the recommended form) plus a **Verified Query Repository** of approved question→SQL pairs that the model references at generation time. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Guardrails**: restrict to a curated model/views, prefer verified queries, validate generated SQL, constrain output (e.g., function-calling / JSON-schema-constrained SQL), enforce row/column security so the agent inherits the user's permissions. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- The research workhorse of LLM-assisted analytics. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Schema linking** — selecting the relevant tables/columns for a question — is the dominant accuracy lever, especially on large/enterprise schemas. 2025 SOTA approaches use **context-aware bidirectional retrieval** and **autonomous schema exploration** (e.g., AutoLink reports ~97% strict linking recall on BIRD-dev, ~91% on Spider 2.0-Lite). Hybrid **dense-vector + symbolic** schema retrieval (Semantic-RAG, CSR-RAG) scales linking to enterprise schemas. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Prompt patterns**: provide schema (DDL), few-shot question→SQL exemplars, value/sample hints, and dialect notes; decompose complex questions; use RAG to retrieve schema fragments + similar verified queries. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Correctness & self-correction**: never trust SQL on syntax. Use **execution-guided self-correction** — run the SQL (or a dry-run/EXPLAIN), feed errors/empty-results back, and let the model repair (e.g., LitE-SQL: 72.1% EX on BIRD, 88.45% on Spider 1.0 via execution-guided correction without multi-candidate sampling). **Majority-vote / consensus** over candidates (ReFoRCE) filters unreliable outputs. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Benchmarks & metrics**: **Spider** (cross-domain) and **BIRD** (large, dirty, real-world DBs with efficiency scoring) are the classics; **Spider 2.0** targets enterprise workflows (huge schemas, dialects, nested query plans) and is *hard* — frontier **execution accuracy** sits in the ~25-35% range vs. ~70%+ on BIRD-dev. Primary metrics: **Execution Accuracy (EX)** — does the result match the gold result — and the stricter, brittler **Exact-Match (EM)** on SQL text. Prefer EX; note that benchmark annotation errors are a known caveat (CIDR 2026 "Text-to-SQL Benchmarks are Broken"). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- An analytics agent decomposes a goal into steps, calls tools (SQL, search, a **sandboxed Python code interpreter**), executes, reflects, and synthesizes a narrative. Pattern: **select → aggregate → rank → explain**, presented in plain language. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Code interpreter / sandboxed Python**: the agent writes and runs Python (pandas/plots) in an isolated sandbox to do analysis beyond SQL (stats, joins across sources, charts). Managed sandboxes (e.g., Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter) handle isolation/scaling; ReAct-style loops (LangGraph) drive write→execute→observe. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Multi-agent specialization**: planner / builder / critic / reflector agents make the final narrative more reliable (e.g., CoDA for collaborative visualization). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Engineering guardrails**: bound the number of tool calls and self-correction iterations, sandbox all code, scope DB credentials to the requesting user, and log every step for replay. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Diagnostic automation** answers **"what changed and why."** **Key-driver analysis** decomposes a metric movement into contributing dimensions/segments (often shown as a **waterfall**), automatically ranking drivers. **Anomaly detection** surfaces unexpected movements proactively (Tableau Pulse's model). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Significance-aware mining**: only narrate insights that are statistically meaningful — guard against spurious "drivers" from multiple comparisons / small segments (ties to `da-12` multiple-comparison discipline). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **NLG** converts the result into a human-readable descriptive/diagnostic/prescriptive narrative attached to a chart or dashboard, making insight portable and actionable (heavy adoption in finance reporting). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- Analytical questions often need **both** numbers (in tables/warehouse) and context (in docs/metric definitions). **Hybrid retrieval** combines **vector + keyword + metadata filtering**: [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Route by question type**: structured/aggregate questions → text-to-SQL against governed data (do *not* answer "what was Q3 revenue" from a vector store); definitional/context questions → vector retrieval over docs. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **RAG-to-SQL**: retrieve schema fragments, FK relationships, column descriptions, and similar verified queries to improve schema linking and grounding (Semantic-RAG, CSR-RAG — ~80%+ recall at ~30ms on commodity hardware). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Agentic RAG over long text in SQL tables** handles documents stored alongside structured columns. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- LLM-produced numbers are a *correctness* problem, not just a fluency one. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Hallucination types**: **faithfulness** (output not grounded in the retrieved context/query result) vs **factuality** (wrong vs the real world). For analytics, **faithfulness to the executed query result** is the key bar — every number should trace to a query. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Controls**: execution-guided validation, **verified-query repositories**, self-consistency / consensus decoding, RAG grounding, **span-level attribution** (claim → source/query), and **SelfCheckGPT-style** inter-sample contradiction checks. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Metric consistency**: route metrics through the governed semantic layer so the same business term yields the same SQL every time (the anti-"metric sprawl" argument from `da-18`). [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Human-in-the-loop & auditability**: keep humans verifying high-stakes answers; expose the **generated SQL/query and lineage** so analysts can audit how a number was produced; integrate **agent observability** (distributed tracing, span-level evaluators) to run quality checks on live traffic. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Choosing**: if your data already lives in Snowflake → Cortex Analyst; Databricks lakehouse → Genie; Power BI/Microsoft → Copilot; want warehouse-independent NLQ → ThoughtSpot; building it yourself / embedding → Vanna or a LangChain/LlamaIndex SQL agent. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Ground before you generate.** Put a governed semantic model / verified queries between the LLM and the warehouse. Raw-schema text-to-SQL is a demo, not a product. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Execute to validate.** Run (or EXPLAIN/dry-run) generated SQL, feed errors back, and self-correct. Prefer execution accuracy over trusting the text. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Seed a verified-query repository.** Curated question→SQL pairs are the single highest-ROI accuracy lever and double as regression tests. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Route by question type.** Aggregate/metric questions → SQL; definitional/context → vector RAG; complex/multi-source → agent with code interpreter. Don't answer numeric questions from a vector store. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Bound the agent.** Cap tool calls + self-correction loops, sandbox all code, scope credentials to the user, and log every step for replay/audit. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Narrate only significant insights.** Significance-test before NLG; rank drivers; show the waterfall and the supporting query. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Make every number auditable.** Surface the generated query + lineage; keep humans in the loop for high-stakes answers. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Build an eval set.** Golden NL→SQL→result triples; track EX (not just EM), faithfulness, and metric-consistency over time. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Pointing text-to-SQL at a raw, ungoverned schema** and expecting reliable answers — accuracy collapses without semantic grounding. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Trusting SQL because it parses** — syntactically valid SQL can return wrong or empty results; always execute-validate. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Answering numeric questions via vector RAG** — vector similarity does not aggregate; route to SQL. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Narrating "drivers" without significance testing** — manufactures spurious explanations from noise / multiple comparisons. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Unbounded agent loops or unsandboxed code execution** — cost blowups and security holes. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Numbers with no audit trail** — if you can't show the query and lineage behind a figure, it isn't trustworthy for decisions. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Optimizing for Exact-Match** — EM is brittle (many correct SQLs differ textually); optimize Execution Accuracy. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **One metric, many definitions** — bypassing the semantic layer reintroduces metric sprawl. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Wrong/empty results despite "good" SQL** → schema-linking failure; add column descriptions, synonyms, sample values, and verified-query exemplars; check FK/join paths. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Inconsistent numbers for the same question** → route through the governed semantic layer; pin metric definitions; add the pair to the verified repository. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Agent loops or runs up cost** → cap iterations/tool calls; add a termination check; cache schema retrieval. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Plausible-but-wrong narrative** → faithfulness failure; require claims to cite the executed query result; add self-consistency / SelfCheckGPT-style checks; insert HITL for high stakes. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
- **Great on BIRD, fails in prod** → enterprise schemas (Spider 2.0 regime) are far harder; invest in schema linking, dialect handling, and retrieval over the real catalog. [src: da-39-augmented-analytics-llm-assisted]
