- `nodejs-concurrency-internals.md` — this file assumes that foundation and focuses on what differs. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- There are now four practically-relevant server-side JS/TS execution targets: [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- The unifying thread is **WinterTC** (formerly WinterCG): the standard defining the **Minimum Common [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Web Platform API** — the subset of browser/Web APIs every server runtime implements identically, so [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- code written to that surface is portable across all of them. Understand WinterTC first; it is the [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- shared branch every runtime below inherits from. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- -- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **History.** WinterCG (Web-interoperable Runtimes Community Group, a W3C CG founded by Cloudflare, [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Vercel, Deno, Shopify and others) incubated a "minimum common API." In **January 2025** WinterCG was [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- wound down and the work moved to **Ecma TC55** ("WinterTC" — Technical Committee on Web-interoperable [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Server Runtimes). The spec is now **ECMA-429** ("Minimum common web API"), adopted by the Ecma [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- General Assembly in December 2025, with **yearly snapshots**. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **What's in the Minimum Common Web Platform API** (the portable surface): [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Fetch & data:** `fetch()`, `Headers`, `Request`, `Response`, `Blob`, `File`, `FormData` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Streams:** `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, `TransformStream` + controllers; `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Encoding/text:** `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` (+ stream variants), `atob`/`btoa` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Crypto:** `crypto` (`Crypto`, `CryptoKey`, `SubtleCrypto`) — Web Crypto, not Node `crypto` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **URL:** `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `URLPattern` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Events/messaging:** `Event`, `EventTarget`, `CustomEvent`, `AbortController`/`AbortSignal`, `MessageChannel`/`MessagePort`, `MessageEvent` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Timers:** `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`clear*`, `queueMicrotask`, `performance` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Utilities:** `structuredClone`, `console`, `navigator.userAgent`, `reportError` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **WebAssembly:** `WebAssembly.*` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Global handlers:** `onerror`, `onunhandledrejection`, `onrejectionhandled` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Explicitly NOT required:** Web Workers, the DOM (`window`, `document`), and HTML element [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- interfaces. (WinterTC plans future *conformance levels* — e.g. CLI/File-Systems, Graphics, Servers [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- with advanced networking — layered above the minimum.) [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Runtime Keys** (separate WinterTC registry): standardized identifiers for runtimes used in [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `package.json` `exports` conditions, `engines`, and runtime detection. Common keys: `node`, `deno`, [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `bun`, `workerd`, `edge-light`, `electron`, `fastly`, `netlify`, `react-native`, `react-server`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Keys are immutable once approved and require "proof of use." Use them to ship runtime-specific entry [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- { "exports": { "workerd": "./dist/edge.js", "deno": "./dist/deno.js", [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- "node": "./dist/node.js", "default": "./dist/default.js" } } [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- > Practical rule: write to the **Minimum Common API** by default; only branch on a Runtime Key when [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- > you genuinely need a runtime-specific capability. Branching is the exception, portability the rule. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- -- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Deno 2.0 shipped **October 2024** (four years after 1.0); the line is now considered stable and [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- production-ready, with a **Long-Term Support (LTS)** channel. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Headline of 2.x = Node/npm backwards compatibility** (the thing that blocked adoption in 1.x): [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Understands `package.json`, `node_modules/`, and **npm workspaces** — run Deno inside existing [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `npm:` specifiers (`import express from "npm:express@4"`) and `node:` builtins [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- (`import { createServer } from "node:http"`). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Package-management subcommands: `deno install`, `deno add`, `deno remove` (so `deno` doubles as a [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- package manager). `deno install` is reported ~15% faster than npm cold-cache, ~90% faster hot-cache. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `nodeModulesDir: "auto" | "manual"` in `deno.json` (or `--node-modules-dir=auto|manual`) controls [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- whether a real `node_modules/` is materialized. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Defining Deno traits (still true in 2.x):** [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Secure by default** — no file/network/env access unless granted: `--allow-net`, `--allow-read`, [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `--allow-env`, or `--allow-all`/`-A`. This is the biggest behavioral difference from Node/Bun. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- (Node has since added an *opt-in* parallel — the stable 24.x Permission Model, `node --permission` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- + `--allow-fs-read`/`--allow-net`/etc.; see the sibling reference `nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features.md`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Deno's is the inverse default: deny-by-default vs Node's allow-by-default.) [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **TypeScript with zero config** — run `.ts` directly, no `tsconfig`/transpile step required. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Web-standard first** — `fetch`, Web Crypto, streams are globals (WinterTC alignment). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Built-in toolchain** — `deno fmt`, `deno lint`, `deno test`, `deno bench`, `deno compile` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- (single-file executables), `deno task` (script runner). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Config:** `deno.json`/`deno.jsonc` — imports map, tasks, lint/fmt config, compiler options. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **JSR** (`jsr:` / jsr.io) — Deno's TypeScript-first registry; publishes TS source, generates docs, [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- works across runtimes (also installable from npm). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Deno KV** — built-in key-value store (`Deno.openKv()`); on Deno Deploy it's globally distributed [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- on FoundationDB. Available in Node via the `@deno/kv` npm package (SQLite-backed locally). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Deno Queues** — `kv.enqueue()` / `kv.listenQueue()`, at-least-once delivery. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- -- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Bun is an **all-in-one toolkit** written in **Zig**, powered by **JavaScriptCore** (not V8) — the [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- JSC choice drives its fast startup and low memory. Positioned as a **drop-in Node.js replacement**. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Node compatibility:** since 1.2, Bun runs the **Node.js test suite on every commit**; many core [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- modules (`node:http`, `node:http2`, `node:dgram`, `node:cluster`, `node:zlib`, etc.) pass **>90%** of [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- their tests. Bun also implemented V8 C++ APIs inside JSC so native N-API addons (e.g. `cpu-features`) [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **As a package manager (`bun install`)** — works in any `package.json` project: [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Up to ~25x faster than npm; supports **workspaces** (reads the `workspaces` key, single-pass install, [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- de-dup), git/http/tarball deps, custom registries, `.npmrc`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **`bun.lock`** — text-based JSONC lockfile (default since **1.2**, replacing binary `bun.lockb`); [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- reviewable in PRs, mergeable. Migrate with [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `bun install --save-text-lockfile --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only` then delete `bun.lockb`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Isolated installs** (1.3): central store in `node_modules/.bun/` with symlinks → packages only see [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- declared deps (kills phantom deps). Default linker: *isolated* for new monorepos, *hoisted* for new [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- single packages and pre-existing projects (backward compat). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Commands: `bun add/remove/update`, `bun outdated`, `bun publish`, `bun patch`, `bun run --filter`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Built-in runtime APIs (the `Bun.*` namespace + `bun:` modules):** [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `Bun.serve()` — HTTP/WebSocket server with static routes (~40% faster than dynamic handlers); [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Express runs ~3x faster on Bun than Node. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `bun:sqlite` — native SQLite (`query.as(Class)` for ORM-less mapping). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `Bun.sql` — native PostgreSQL client, tagged-template parameterized queries, pooling (~50% faster [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- than popular Node Postgres libs); also `Bun.redis`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `Bun.s3` — built-in S3 client (~5x faster downloads than `@aws-sdk/client-s3`), presigned URLs, [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- multipart `writer()`, integrates with `fetch()`/`Bun.serve()`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `Bun.file()` (`.delete()`, `.stat()`, S3-backed), `Bun.udpSocket()`, `Bun.color()`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Test runner (`bun test`):** Jest-compatible expect, JUnit XML + LCOV for CI, inline snapshots [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- (`toMatchInlineSnapshot()`), `test.only()` w/o flags. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Bundler/build:** HTML imports, built-in CSS parser (LightningCSS-derived), bytecode caching (~2x [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- faster startup), cross-compilation (build Windows/macOS binaries on Linux), `bun build --compile`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- -- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Edge runtimes run JS in **V8 isolates** (lightweight contexts, not containers) distributed across [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- global POPs — **sub-millisecond cold starts**, no per-request VM boot. The execution model is a [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- handler: `Request → Response`. They expose the **WinterTC Minimum Common API**, *not* full Node. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Hard constraints to design around:** [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Stateless** — no durable in-memory state between requests; persistence needs external stores [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- (KV, D1, Durable Objects, databases-over-HTTP). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Tight CPU/memory budgets** — e.g. memory commonly capped ~128 MB, CPU time tens of ms (provider- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- and plan-specific; Cloudflare offers higher CPU limits on paid tiers). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **No raw filesystem / no long-running event loop / no Node `net` server** by default. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- TCP/raw-socket and many npm packages that assume Node internals won't work unless a compat shim is on. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Cloudflare Workers (workerd)** — V8 isolates, 330+ POPs. **`nodejs_compat`** is an umbrella [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- compatibility flag enabling Node APIs incrementally (granular sub-flags exist). Unsupported APIs are [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- polyfilled by **Wrangler via `unenv`** when `nodejs_compat` is on and the **compatibility date** is [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- ≥ `2024-09-23`. 2025 added real implementations gated by compat date: `node:net`/`node:dns`/ [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `node:timers` (Jan 2025), `node:fs` + Web FS (`enable_nodejs_fs_module`, auto ≥ `2025-09-15`), [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `node:os` (≥ `2025-09-15`), `node:console` (≥ `2025-09-21`), `node:vm` stub (≥ `2025-10-01`). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Storage/compute primitives: KV, R2, D1, Durable Objects, Queues, Cron Triggers. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Vercel Edge Functions / Edge Runtime** — V8 + a **subset of Node APIs** ("Edge Runtime"), [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- WinterCG/WinterTC-compliant; open-source `edge-runtime` package emulates it locally. Fast cold [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- starts; many npm packages work if they stick to the Web-standard subset. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Deno Deploy** — multi-tenant V8 **isolate cloud**; TS-first, native ESM, no bundler step. Now [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- supports **`npm:` specifiers and `node:` builtins** (run existing Node apps like `node:http` at the [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- edge). Primitives: **Deno KV** (FoundationDB-backed, globally replicated), **Deno Queues**. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Subhosting** = run *your users'* untrusted code securely in isolates (multi-tenant PaaS). Dec 2025: [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- detects Deno/npm **workspace/monorepo** configs to deploy from subdirectories. (Note the [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- "Deploy Classic" → new Deno Deploy migration path.) [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Compatibility-date discipline (Cloudflare):** the `compatibility_date` (+ optional [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `compatibility_flags`) pins runtime behavior. Bumping the date can flip on new Node modules or change [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- defaults — treat it as a deliberate, tested upgrade, not a passive value. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- -- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Maximum ecosystem certainty / existing large app** → Node.js (the baseline; see `javascript-nodejs.md`). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **TS-first, security sandboxing, batteries-included tooling, JSR** → **Deno 2.x**. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Raw speed + single-tool DX (install/run/test/bundle), heavy local I/O (SQLite/Postgres/S3)** → **Bun 1.x**. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Global low-latency, request/response, sub-ms cold start, no servers to manage** → **Edge**. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Portability strategy (works everywhere):** [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Code to the **Minimum Common Web Platform API** (fetch/streams/Web Crypto/URL/TextEncoder). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Prefer ESM; use `package.json` `exports` with **Runtime Keys** only for genuine per-runtime branches. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Keep Node-specific built-ins (`fs`, `net`, native addons) behind an abstraction so edge targets can [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- swap them for a Web-standard or platform primitive. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Verify with each runtime's compat tracking (Bun's Node test-suite pass rate; Cloudflare's [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `nodejs_compat` + compat-date matrix; Deno's `node:`/`npm:` support). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- -- [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **One server, three runtimes:** a handler exporting `default { fetch(req) { return new Response(...) } }` [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- is the portable shape — it runs on Deno (`Deno.serve`), Bun (`Bun.serve`/default export), and edge [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- (workerd/Vercel) with minimal glue. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Deno running a Node app:** add `package.json`, set `nodeModulesDir: "auto"` in `deno.json`, use [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `deno install` then `deno run -A npm:...` — no rewrite needed for ESM projects. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Bun as a faster CI package manager only:** drop `bun install` into a Node project (commit [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `bun.lock`), keep running the app on Node — Bun-as-pm is decoupled from Bun-as-runtime. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Edge + state:** never hold state in module scope expecting persistence; route durable state to KV/ [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- D1/Durable Objects (Cloudflare) or Deno KV/Queues (Deno Deploy). [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Assuming "Node-compatible" = 100%.** Bun ~90%+ on *supported* modules; Cloudflare's coverage is [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- gated by compat date/flags; Deno supports `node:`/`npm:` but not every native edge case. Test, don't assume. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Using Node `crypto`/`Buffer`/`fs` in edge code** that targets the Web-standard subset — reach for [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- Web Crypto (`crypto.subtle`), `Uint8Array`/`Blob`, and platform storage instead. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Leaving Cloudflare `compatibility_date` stale (or bumping it blind).** Stale = you miss fixes/new [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- modules; blind bump = behavior changes silently. Pin and upgrade deliberately. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Committing `bun.lockb` (binary) in 2025+.** Migrate to text `bun.lock` for reviewable diffs. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Relying on phantom dependencies** under Bun's hoisted linker — use isolated installs in monorepos. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- **Shipping a Deno script that silently needs broad perms** — scope `--allow-*` tightly; `-A` defeats [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- *npm package fails on edge* → it likely imports a Node built-in; enable `nodejs_compat` + check [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- compat date (Cloudflare), or refactor to the Web-standard subset. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- *Deno "Requires net access" / permission error* → add the matching `--allow-net`/`--allow-read` flag. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- *Bun behaves differently from Node on a module* → check Bun's Node compatibility tracker for that [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- `node:` module's pass rate; file/upstream if it's a gap. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- *Cold start still slow on "edge"* → confirm you're on an isolate runtime (workerd/V8 isolates), not a [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- container-backed serverless function masquerading as edge. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]
- *Lockfile merge conflicts in Bun* → you're on binary `bun.lockb`; migrate to text `bun.lock`. [src: javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge]

- <!-- hub-reference-banner --> [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- > **Reference file — part of the `programming-languages` hub.** Authored via `/dr` (deep-research). Cross-refs: `python-patterns` (modern Python idioms) and `nodejs-concurrency-internals` (the parallel runtime-concurrency-internals reference for Node/libuv). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Deep reference for the 2023–2026 CPython runtime overhaul. Three PEPs reshape how the interpreter executes, all touching the same machinery (eval loop, reference counting, per-interpreter state): [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- These are three answers to "how do I use more than one core / go faster in Python." Free-threading removes the lock; subinterpreters give each thread its own lock + isolated heap; the JIT speeds up single-threaded execution. They compose. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- The eval loop is tiered: **Tier 1** = specializing adaptive interpreter (PEP 659, 3.11+) rewrites hot bytecodes in place into type-specialized forms while profiling. **Tier 2** = micro-op (uop) IR (3.13+, `-X uops`/`PYTHON_UOPS=1`). **Tier 3** = JIT machine code (PEP 744). Runtime state lives in C globals, `_PyRuntimeState`, and per-interpreter `PyInterpreterState`; each thread has a `PyThreadState`. **Immortal objects (PEP 683, 3.12)** — small ints/None/True/False/interned strings/code constants have refcounts that are never modified and are never freed; this is the enabling primitive for *both* subinterpreters (shareable immutable singletons) and free-threading (no refcount contention). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- **Status:** 3.13 experimental; 3.14 **supported but not default** (PEP 779, "phase II"). **Internals:** biased reference counting (fast path for thread-owned objects, atomic slow path for shared); deferred reference counting (module objects/functions/descriptors/`threading.local` — cleanup deferred to GC); per-thread reference counting (heap types, code objects, module `__dict__`, merged at safe points); immortalization of code constants + `sys.intern()`ed strings (3.14); `mimalloc` replaces `pymalloc`; lock-free structures use **QSBR**; per-object locks + **`PyMutex`** (1-byte lock) keep list/dict/set ops atomic; stop-the-world GC pauses; non-GC object header 16→32 bytes (AMD64). **Cost:** ~1% single-thread overhead on macOS aarch64, up to ~8% on x86-64 Linux. **Build/detect:** `./configure --disable-gil`; `python -VV` shows "free-threading build"; `sys._is_gil_enabled()`; `sysconfig.get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED")`. **Runtime GIL control:** `-X gil=0|1` / `PYTHON_GIL=0|1`. **Behavioral:** `sys.flags.thread_inherit_context` and `context_aware_warnings` default True; reading another thread's `frame.f_locals` is unsafe; sharing one iterator across threads can drop/dup elements. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- An extension that doesn't declare support **auto-re-enables the GIL at import with a warning** — silently negating no-GIL process-wide. Multi-phase init (PEP 489): add slot `{Py_mod_gil, Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED}`. Single-phase init (`PyModule_Create`): `#ifdef Py_GIL_DISABLED` then `PyUnstable_Module_SetGIL(module, Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED);`. Free-threaded wheels use the **`cp314t`** ABI tag. NumPy/Cython/pybind11/PyO3 ship FT-aware paths (track: py-free-threading.github.io/tracking/, hugovk.github.io/free-threaded-wheels/). Test with a tiny `sys.setswitchinterval(...)` and ThreadSanitizer. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Subinterpreters exist via C API since 1.5 (1997); **PEP 684** (3.12) gave each its own GIL by isolating runtime state into `PyInterpreterState`; **PEP 734** (3.14, final) exposes them in Python (predecessor draft: **PEP 554**; module renamed `interpreters` → **`concurrent.interpreters`**). Parallelism by isolation: N interpreters → N cores without no-GIL thread-safety hazards. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- from concurrent import interpreters [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- interp = interpreters.create()          # -> Interpreter [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- interp.id; interp.is_running() [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- interp.prepare_main(x=10)               # bind globals [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- interp.exec("print(x)"); interp.call(fn); t = interp.call_in_thread(fn) [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- interpreters.get_current(); interpreters.list_all() [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- q = interpreters.create_queue()         # put/get/put_nowait/get_nowait/empty/full/qsize [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- **Sharing:** nearly anything picklable crosses (copied via pickle); `memoryview`/buffer-protocol objects share the buffer directly. Synchronize by passing tokens through queues, not shared mutable objects. **Exceptions:** `exec()` → `ExecutionFailed` (`.type/.msg/.snapshot`); `call()` propagates directly; plus `InterpreterError`, `InterpreterNotFoundError`, `QueueEmpty`, `QueueFull`. **Pool:** `concurrent.futures.InterpreterPoolExecutor`. **Probe:** `sys.implementation.supports_isolated_interpreters`. **Caveats:** heavier startup than a thread; not all C extensions are subinterpreter-safe (process-global C state). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Compiles hot **tier-2 micro-op** sequences to native code. New/experimental in 3.13, off by default through 3.14. **Technique:** at build time LLVM (Clang, needs `musttail`) compiles each micro-op into a machine-code **stencil** dumped to a header; at runtime the JIT copies each stencil almost verbatim and patches operands (tiny JIT latency). **Build/run:** `./configure --enable-experimental-jit` (values `yes|no|interpreter|yes-off`; `yes-off` = build but run interpreter mode); `PYTHON_JIT=1`. Build-time LLVM dep adds ~3–60 s; no runtime dep, no API/ABI change. **Reality (3.13/3.14):** ~on par with the specializing interpreter, **10–20% memory overhead** — a foundation, not yet a free win. Tier-1 platforms: x86-64 + aarch64 on Linux/macOS/Windows. **Non-experimental criteria (PEP 744):** ≈5% speedup on a popular platform, deployable with minimal disruption, Steering Council sign-off. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- CPU-bound, shared mutable state, threads → **free-threading (703)** (you own the locking; FT-incompatible C ext re-enables the GIL). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- CPU-bound, little sharing, want isolation → **subinterpreters (734)** (per-interpreter GIL → multi-core; pass data via queues). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Hard isolation / crash containment → **multiprocessing**. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- I/O-bound → **asyncio/threads** (GIL releases on I/O). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Single-thread speed → **JIT (744)** + specializing interpreter (modest today). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Shipping a C extension without `Py_mod_gil`/`PyUnstable_Module_SetGIL` → silent process-wide GIL re-enable. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Assuming no-GIL ⇒ thread-safe code: container *ops* are atomic, but multi-step invariants still need your own `threading.Lock`; cross-thread iterator sharing is unsafe. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Reading another thread's running `frame.f_locals` on the FT build — may crash. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Treating subinterpreters as cheap threads — use `InterpreterPoolExecutor`. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Expecting a big JIT win today (≈parity, +10–20% memory). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Sharing mutable objects between subinterpreters — use the queue. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- "GIL was re-enabled at runtime" → an imported C ext lacks `Py_mod_gil`; check `sys._is_gil_enabled()`, find/fix the offender. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Objects not freed promptly (FT) → deferred/QSBR; `gc.collect()` or tune `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0` (perf cost). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Subinterpreter import crash → extension keeps process-global C state. [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- JIT no speedup → expected at 3.13/3.14; verify it's built (`--enable-experimental-jit`) and on (`PYTHON_JIT=1`). [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- PEP 703 https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ · PEP 779 https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Free-threading HOWTO https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- C-API extension support https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-extensions.html [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Free-Threading Guide https://py-free-threading.github.io/ [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- PEP 734 https://peps.python.org/pep-0734/ · PEP 684 https://peps.python.org/pep-0684/ · PEP 554 https://peps.python.org/pep-0554/ · PEP 683 https://peps.python.org/pep-0683/ [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- Per-interpreter GIL (LWN) https://lwn.net/Articles/941090/ [src: cpython-runtime-internals]
- PEP 744 https://peps.python.org/pep-0744/ · pydevtools JIT https://pydevtools.com/handbook/explanation/what-is-cpythons-jit-compiler/ · Following up on the JIT (LWN) https://lwn.net/Articles/1029307/ [src: cpython-runtime-internals]

- -- [src: pydantic-v2]
- Pydantic is the most widely used data-validation library for Python. It validates [src: pydantic-v2]
- data at runtime against Python type hints and produces structured, user-friendly [src: pydantic-v2]
- errors when data is invalid. **Pydantic v2** (released mid-2023, stable and current [src: pydantic-v2]
- through 2026) rewrote the validation/serialization engine in Rust as a separate [src: pydantic-v2]
- package, **`pydantic-core`** (built with PyO3). The result is **~5–50× faster** than [src: pydantic-v2]
- v1 (≈17× on a typical mixed-field model), with the Python layer reduced to schema [src: pydantic-v2]
- *definition* while the hot path runs in compiled Rust. [src: pydantic-v2]
- Three packages make up the ecosystem: [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`pydantic`** — the Python API (`BaseModel`, `Field`, validators, `TypeAdapter`). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`pydantic-core`** — the Rust validation/serialization engine (not used directly). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`pydantic-settings`** — `BaseSettings` for config from env vars, `.env`, secrets. [src: pydantic-v2]
- Use it when you need to **parse untrusted input** (API bodies, config, JSON, ORM [src: pydantic-v2]
- rows) into typed Python objects with guarantees, and serialize them back out. [src: pydantic-v2]
- Subclass `BaseModel`; annotate fields with type hints. Validation runs on [src: pydantic-v2]
- construction and on the explicit `model_validate*` entry points. [src: pydantic-v2]
- from pydantic import BaseModel, Field [src: pydantic-v2]
- from typing import Annotated [src: pydantic-v2]
- class User(BaseModel): [src: pydantic-v2]
- name: str = "anonymous"                     # default [src: pydantic-v2]
- tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # mutable default → factory [src: pydantic-v2]
- age: Annotated[int, Field(ge=0, le=130)]    # constraint via Annotated [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Validation entry points:** `User(**data)`, `User.model_validate(dict_or_obj)`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `User.model_validate_json(json_str_or_bytes)`. JSON parsing happens *inside Rust* [src: pydantic-v2]
- in `model_validate_json` — faster than `json.loads()` then `model_validate`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`Field(...)`** carries metadata/constraints: `default`, `default_factory`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `alias` / `validation_alias` / `serialization_alias`, `ge/gt/le/lt`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `min_length/max_length`, `pattern`, `description`, `frozen`, `exclude`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Prefer `Annotated[type, Field(...)]`** over `field: type = Field(...)` for [src: pydantic-v2]
- constraints. Constraints inside `Annotated` are compiled into the core schema and [src: pydantic-v2]
- run in Rust (no Python call overhead). They also compose with `list[...]`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `dict[...]`, etc. (e.g. `list[Annotated[int, Field(gt=0)]]`). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`from_attributes=True`** (in `model_config`, replaces v1 `orm_mode`) lets [src: pydantic-v2]
- `model_validate` read attributes off arbitrary objects (e.g. ORM rows). [src: pydantic-v2]
- Pydantic distinguishes **validators** (input → validated value) from **serializers** [src: pydantic-v2]
- (value → output). Validators run in a defined order around the core (Rust) validation. [src: pydantic-v2]
- from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator, model_validator, ValidationError [src: pydantic-v2]
- from typing_extensions import Self [src: pydantic-v2]
- class Account(BaseModel): [src: pydantic-v2]
- password_confirm: str [src: pydantic-v2]
- @field_validator("username")          # decorate per-field [src: pydantic-v2]
- @classmethod                          # field_validator is a classmethod [src: pydantic-v2]
- def no_spaces(cls, v: str) -> str: [src: pydantic-v2]
- raise ValueError("username must not contain spaces") [src: pydantic-v2]
- @model_validator(mode="after")        # whole-model, cross-field [src: pydantic-v2]
- def passwords_match(self) -> Self: [src: pydantic-v2]
- if self.password != self.password_confirm: [src: pydantic-v2]
- raise ValueError("passwords do not match") [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Modes (the most-confused part of Pydantic v2):** [src: pydantic-v2]
- `mode="before"` — runs on **raw input** *before* core coercion. Receives whatever [src: pydantic-v2]
- was passed (often a `dict` or `str`); use to reshape/normalize input. [src: pydantic-v2]
- `mode="after"` — runs on the **already-validated, typed** value. Safest default for [src: pydantic-v2]
- business rules; you get a real `int`/`str`/submodel, not raw input. [src: pydantic-v2]
- `mode="wrap"` — most powerful: receives the value **and** a `handler` callable; you [src: pydantic-v2]
- decide whether/when to call the inner validator and can transform around it. [src: pydantic-v2]
- `mode="plain"` — terminates validation; your function fully replaces core validation [src: pydantic-v2]
- for that field (no core coercion runs). [src: pydantic-v2]
- `model_validator(mode="before")` receives the raw input dict for the whole model; [src: pydantic-v2]
- `mode="after"` receives `self` (return `self`). Raise `ValueError` or `AssertionError` [src: pydantic-v2]
- inside a validator and Pydantic wraps it into a `ValidationError`. Validators can [src: pydantic-v2]
- take an `info: ValidationInfo` param for `info.data` (already-validated siblings), [src: pydantic-v2]
- `info.context`, `info.field_name`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Reusable validators:** attach a validator to a type once with [src: pydantic-v2]
- `Annotated[str, AfterValidator(func)]` / `BeforeValidator` / `WrapValidator` / [src: pydantic-v2]
- `PlainValidator` — cleaner than repeating `@field_validator` across models. [src: pydantic-v2]
- By default Pydantic is **lax**: it coerces compatible types (`"123"` → `123`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `"true"` → `True`). **Strict mode** disables coercion and requires exact types. [src: pydantic-v2]
- from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict [src: pydantic-v2]
- model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)   # whole-model strict [src: pydantic-v2]
- M.model_validate({"x": "123"})               # raises: str is not a valid int [src: pydantic-v2]
- Strictness is layered (most → least specific): per-call `model_validate(..., strict=True)` [src: pydantic-v2]
- > field-level `Field(strict=True)` / `Strict()` annotation > `model_config`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- Common `ConfigDict` keys: [src: pydantic-v2]
- `strict`, `frozen` (immutable + hashable; replaces v1 `allow_mutation`), [src: pydantic-v2]
- `extra` = `"ignore"` (default) / `"forbid"` / `"allow"`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `validate_assignment=True` (re-validate on attribute set; off by default), [src: pydantic-v2]
- `from_attributes=True` (ORM reads), `populate_by_name=True` (accept field name [src: pydantic-v2]
- *and* alias on input; renamed `validate_by_name` in newer versions), [src: pydantic-v2]
- `str_strip_whitespace`, `use_enum_values`, `arbitrary_types_allowed`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `json_schema_extra`, `ser_json_timedelta`, etc. [src: pydantic-v2]
- `model_config` is a **dict** (`ConfigDict(...)`), not the v1 nested `class Config`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- m.model_dump()                  # → dict, Python objects (datetime stays datetime) [src: pydantic-v2]
- m.model_dump(mode="json")       # → dict with JSON-safe values (datetime → str) [src: pydantic-v2]
- m.model_dump_json()             # → JSON str, serialized in Rust (fast) [src: pydantic-v2]
- Key options (apply to all three): `include` / `exclude` (sets or nested dicts), [src: pydantic-v2]
- `by_alias=True` (use `serialization_alias`), `exclude_unset` (only fields explicitly [src: pydantic-v2]
- set — great for PATCH semantics), `exclude_defaults`, `exclude_none`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `round_trip=True`, `warnings="error"`, `context=...`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Custom serializers:** `@field_serializer("foo", mode="plain"|"wrap")` for one [src: pydantic-v2]
- field; `@model_serializer` for the whole model; `Annotated[T, PlainSerializer(...)]` [src: pydantic-v2]
- for reusable type-level serialization. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`@computed_field`** — expose a derived `@property` in the serialized output: [src: pydantic-v2]
- from pydantic import BaseModel, computed_field [src: pydantic-v2]
- class Box(BaseModel): [src: pydantic-v2]
- def area(self) -> float: [src: pydantic-v2]
- return self.w * self.h [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`RootModel[T]`** — a model whose top level is *not* an object (e.g. [src: pydantic-v2]
- `RootModel[list[int]]`, `RootModel[dict[str, User]]`); replaces v1 `__root__`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- `TypeAdapter` brings Pydantic's machinery to *any* type — `list[User]`, `dict[str,int]`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `TypedDict`, dataclasses, unions — without wrapping it in a model. Build the adapter [src: pydantic-v2]
- once (it compiles a core schema) and reuse it. [src: pydantic-v2]
- from pydantic import TypeAdapter [src: pydantic-v2]
- ta = TypeAdapter(list[User]) [src: pydantic-v2]
- users = ta.validate_python([{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}])   # list[User] [src: pydantic-v2]
- users = ta.validate_json(raw_bytes)                  # parse + validate in Rust [src: pydantic-v2]
- ta.dump_json(users)                                  # serialize [src: pydantic-v2]
- ta.json_schema()                                     # JSON Schema for the type [src: pydantic-v2]
- Use it for bulk validation of homogeneous collections (build the adapter at module [src: pydantic-v2]
- scope, not per call) and for validating request/response bodies that aren't models. [src: pydantic-v2]
- Add a `discriminator` so the core validator picks **one** union member by a tag field [src: pydantic-v2]
- instead of trying each — faster, and produces one clean error instead of N. [src: pydantic-v2]

- For tags that aren't a plain field, use a **callable discriminator** via [src: pydantic-v2]

- callable also runs during serialization. Discriminated unions also emit cleaner [src: pydantic-v2]

- default; left-to-right is available but usually worse. [src: pydantic-v2]

- **FastAPI** — built on Pydantic; request/response models *are* Pydantic models. [src: pydantic-v2]

- **`bump-pydantic`** — automated V1→V2 codemod (renames `@validator`→`@field_validator`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `Config`→`model_config`, `.dict()`→`.model_dump()`, etc.). Run it, then review diffs. [src: pydantic-v2]

- **Validating a whole object with named fields?** → `BaseModel`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Validating a bare collection / TypedDict / union, no model needed?** → `TypeAdapter`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Reshaping raw input before typing?** → `@field_validator(mode="before")` or a [src: pydantic-v2]
- model `mode="before"` validator. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Cross-field business rule on typed data?** → `@model_validator(mode="after")`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Same validation reused across models/types?** → `Annotated[T, AfterValidator(...)]`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **A union you can tag?** → discriminated union (`Field(discriminator=...)`). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **App configuration?** → `BaseSettings` from `pydantic-settings`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Need exact types, no coercion (e.g. money, ids)?** → `strict=True` (per-field or model). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Parse, don't validate-then-pass-dicts:** convert at the boundary [src: pydantic-v2]
- (`Model.model_validate_json(body)`) and pass typed models inward. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **PATCH/partial update:** `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` to send only fields the [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Aliases for external naming:** `Field(validation_alias="userId", [src: pydantic-v2]
- serialization_alias="user_id")`; set `populate_by_name=True` to also accept the [src: pydantic-v2]
- Python field name on input. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Immutable value objects:** `model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)` → hashable, [src: pydantic-v2]
- usable as dict keys / in sets. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Bulk validation:** build one module-level `TypeAdapter(list[Model])` and call [src: pydantic-v2]
- `validate_python` once on the whole batch rather than looping per item. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Context-aware validation:** `Model.model_validate(data, context={...})`, read via [src: pydantic-v2]
- `info.context` in validators (e.g. inject locale, feature flags). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Overusing `@field_validator` for simple bounds.** A Python validator always runs in [src: pydantic-v2]
- Python (function-call overhead, duplicates checks). → Use `Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)]` [src: pydantic-v2]
- so the constraint runs in Rust. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`mode="before"` when you wanted typed data.** Before-validators get *raw* input [src: pydantic-v2]
- (often a `str`/`dict`), causing `AttributeError`/type bugs. → Use `mode="after"` for [src: pydantic-v2]
- rules on validated values. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Building a `TypeAdapter` inside a hot loop / per request.** It recompiles the core [src: pydantic-v2]
- schema each time. → Construct once at module scope and reuse. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`json.loads()` then `model_validate(dict)`.** → `model_validate_json(raw)` parses [src: pydantic-v2]
- and validates in one Rust pass. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **v1 carry-overs:** `class Config` (→ `model_config = ConfigDict(...)`), `@validator` [src: pydantic-v2]
- (→ `@field_validator`), `@root_validator` (→ `@model_validator`), `.dict()` [src: pydantic-v2]
- (→ `.model_dump()`), `.json()` (→ `.model_dump_json()`), `parse_obj` (→ `model_validate`), [src: pydantic-v2]

- (→ `frozen=True`), `each_item=True` (→ annotate the inner type). [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Mutable default shared across instances** (`tags: list = []`). → `Field(default_factory=list)`. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Mixing Pydantic v1 and v2 models** in one validation graph — they don't nest cleanly; [src: pydantic-v2]
- migrate the whole graph (`bump-pydantic`), or use the `pydantic.v1` shim deliberately. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Expecting `validate_assignment` by default.** It's off; set [src: pydantic-v2]
- `ConfigDict(validate_assignment=True)` if you mutate after construction. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`ValidationError`** — iterate `exc.errors()` for structured dicts (`loc`, `msg`, [src: pydantic-v2]
- `type`, `input`); `exc.json()` / `exc.error_count()` for reporting. The `type` [src: pydantic-v2]
- string (e.g. `int_parsing`, `missing`, `string_too_short`) is the stable machine key. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **"Input should be a valid integer" under strict mode** — you passed a string to a [src: pydantic-v2]
- strict `int`; coerce upstream or drop strictness for that field. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **Serialization warning "Expected X but got Y"** — a field's runtime value doesn't [src: pydantic-v2]
- match its declared type (common with `Any`/subclasses); set [src: pydantic-v2]
- `model_dump(serialize_as_any=True)` for duck-typed/polymorphic output, or fix the type. [src: pydantic-v2]
- **`PydanticUndefinedAnnotation` / forward refs** — call `Model.model_rebuild()` after [src: pydantic-v2]
- the referenced type is defined (self-referential or late-bound models). [src: pydantic-v2]

- feature layer**: running `.ts` files with no build step, the third-party runners that fill the gaps, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]

- Node.js 24 (the 2025 "Krypton" LTS line) turned three previously experimental capabilities into [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- default-or-stable features: it **runs TypeScript directly** by stripping types, ships a **stable [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Permission Model** for restricting what a process can touch, and supports **Single Executable [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Applications (SEA)** for distributing a CLI as one binary. These features share one premise — reduce [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- the toolchain around a Node app: fewer build steps (type stripping), fewer ambient privileges [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- (permissions), fewer install prerequisites (SEA). They do **not** replace a type checker, a bundler, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- or OS-level sandboxing; each has a sharp, documented boundary. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Version anchors (memorize these — they drive most "does my Node have X" questions):** [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Node executes `.ts` by **erasing** type syntax and running the remaining JavaScript — it does *not* [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- compile or downlevel. Erased syntax (type annotations, `interface`, `type`, `import type`, type-only [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `namespace`) is replaced **in place with whitespace**, so line/column numbers are preserved and no [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- source map is needed. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **No type checking happens.** Type errors silently pass at runtime. Run `tsc --noEmit` separately [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- in CI/editor for safety. This is the single most important caveat. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Unsupported (throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`):** `enum`, parameter properties [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- (`constructor(private x: number)`), runtime `namespace` (with executable code), and (legacy [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- TS) `import =`/`export =` aliases — these all require *emitting* JS, not just erasing. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Decorators / JSX:** `.tsx` is **not** supported by type stripping; legacy experimental decorators [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- need a transform. Use a runner (tsx) or a real compile step. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Extensions:** `.ts` (module type from nearest `package.json` `"type"`), `.mts` (always ESM), [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `.cts` (always CJS). Relative imports **must carry the extension** (`import './x.ts'`) — there is no [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- extensionless resolution. `node_modules` `.ts` files are refused (libraries must ship `.js`+`.d.ts`). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **`--experimental-transform-types`** historically *emitted* the unsupported constructs (enums etc.) [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- and enabled source maps — but it was **removed in v26.0.0**. On v26+, code using enums/namespaces [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- must move to erasable patterns or use an external tool. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **`--no-strip-types`** disables the behavior (e.g. to force a loader to handle `.ts`). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Recommended `tsconfig.json` for the native path (TS 5.8+): [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- "module": "nodenext", [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- "erasableSyntaxOnly": true, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- "verbatimModuleSyntax": true, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- "rewriteRelativeImportExtensions": true, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- "allowImportingTsExtensions": true [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `erasableSyntaxOnly` is the key alignment knob: it makes `tsc` reject exactly what Node refuses, so [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- the editor catches the mismatch instead of a runtime crash. `tsconfig` `paths` are **not** honored by [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- the runtime — use Node subpath imports (`#alias` in `package.json` `imports`) instead. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Native stripping covers dev scripts and simple services; the third-party runners remain necessary for [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- the constructs Node refuses or for full type checking. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **tsx** — esbuild-powered runner. Transpiles (does **not** type-check, like `ts-node --swc`), [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- supports enums, decorators, JSX/`.tsx`, `tsconfig` `paths`, CJS+ESM transparently, and has a fast [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- integrated watch mode. Invoke as `tsx file.ts`, `tsx watch file.ts`, or as a loader: [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `node --import tsx file.ts`. Best default for "I want it to just run everything." [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **ts-node** — uses the real `tsc` (or `--swc`). Its draw is **type checking during execution** and [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- full language fidelity; its pain is fiddly ESM setup and slower starts. Use `ts-node --esm` for ESM. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Decision rule:** dev script / simple service with erasable code → **native** `node file.ts` [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- (zero deps). Need enums/decorators/JSX/path-aliases but not runtime type-checking → **tsx**. Want [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- type errors to *halt* execution → **ts-node** (or just gate with `tsc --noEmit` in CI and use native). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Production:** none of these replace a real build. For shipping, still run `tsc`/`esbuild`/a [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- bundler with optimization, tree-shaking, and minification. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `node --permission app.js` denies, by default, access to: the filesystem (`fs`), child processes, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- worker threads, native addons, WASI, and the inspector. It is a **trusted-code seatbelt** (prevent a [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- dependency from *unintentionally* reaching resources), **not** a sandbox against malicious code. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Grant flags (each can repeat; comma lists also work): [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Path syntax: `*` = all; absolute or CWD-relative paths; a trailing `/` on an existing directory auto- [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- adds `/*`; `*` mid/end is a wildcard (`/home/test*`). The entrypoint (and `-r` preloads) are [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- auto-added to `--allow-fs-read`. Declarable in `node.config.json` under a `"permission"` object and [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- loaded with `--experimental-default-config-file`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Runtime API: `process.permission.has('fs.write')` and `process.permission.has('fs.read', '/path')` [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- return booleans. Denials throw `Error … code: 'ERR_ACCESS_DENIED', permission: 'FileSystemRead', …`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Documented limitations (cite these — they are common gotchas):** permissions **do not inherit to [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- worker threads** (grant per-worker); **symlinks are followed** even to unauthorized targets (traversal [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- bypass); pre-init flags (`--env-file`, `--openssl-config`) run before the model initializes; existing [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **file descriptors via `node:fs` bypass** the model; `sqlite` loadable extensions and OpenSSL engines [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- can't be requested at runtime; `process._debugProcess()` is not gated. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Distribute a Node app as one binary to machines without Node installed, by injecting a blob into a copy [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- of the `node` binary. **CommonJS or ESM** main, single entrypoint per app. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `sea-config.json` fields: `main`, `mainFormat` (`"commonjs"` default | `"module"`), `output`, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `disableExperimentalSEAWarning`, `useSnapshot`, `useCodeCache`, `execArgv` + `execArgvExtension` [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- (`"none"`|`"env"`|`"cli"`), and `assets` (key→path map). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **New single-step build (v25.5.0+, recommended):** [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- node --build-sea sea-config.json   # generates blob AND injects it; no postject, no LIEF knowledge [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `--build-sea` ported postject's injection logic into core (`src/node_sea_bin.cc`, statically links [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- LIEF, ~5 MB binary growth). Joyee Cheung landed it in v25.5.0; may backport to LTS. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Legacy two-step (still valid, needed where `--build-sea` isn't available):** [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- node --experimental-sea-config sea-config.json           # writes sea-prep.blob [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- cp $(command -v node) myapp                               # copy the runtime [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- codesign --remove-signature myapp                         # macOS/Windows: strip sig first [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- npx postject myapp NODE_SEA_BLOB sea-prep.blob \ [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- -sentinel-fuse NODE_SEA_FUSE_fce680ab2cc467b6e072b8b5df1996b2 \ [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- codesign --sign - myapp                                   # macOS: re-sign (required to run) [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Blob placement is format-specific: PE resource (Windows), Mach-O `NODE_SEA_BLOB` section in segment [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `NODE_SEA` (macOS), ELF note (Linux). The fuse sentinel marks the binary as carrying a blob. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **`node:sea` API** (call from inside the app): `isSea()`, `getAsset(key[, encoding])`, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `getAssetAsBlob(key)`, `getRawAsset(key)` (no-copy reference), `getAssetKeys()`. Inside a SEA, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `__filename`/`module.filename` equal `process.execPath` and `__dirname` is its directory; use [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `module.createRequire()` to load files off disk (built-ins always work). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Node 24+ runtime** — `node file.ts` (strip), `--permission` + `--allow-*`, `--build-sea`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **tsx** — `tsx file.ts`, `tsx watch`, `node --import tsx file.ts` (transpile-only, full TS feature set). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **ts-node** — `ts-node`, `ts-node --esm`, `ts-node --swc` (type-checking runner). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **tsc** — `tsc --noEmit` for the type-check gate that native stripping omits; full build for prod. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **postject** — `npx postject` blob injection (legacy SEA path / pre-25.5 runtimes). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **codesign / signtool** — macOS/Windows binary (re)signing around postject. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Pick the run path.** Erasable code + dev → native `node`. Enums/decorators/JSX/aliases → tsx. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Need runtime type enforcement → ts-node. Always pair native/tsx with a separate `tsc --noEmit`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Align tsconfig** with `erasableSyntaxOnly` + `verbatimModuleSyntax` so the editor mirrors Node. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Lock down** long-running or third-party-heavy processes with `--permission` and the minimal [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `--allow-*` set; verify at runtime via `process.permission.has(...)`; remember workers need their own. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Ship a binary** with `node --build-sea sea-config.json` on v25.5+, else the config+postject+codesign [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- chain. Disable `useCodeCache`/`useSnapshot` for cross-platform reproducibility. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Zero-build CLI:** ship `.ts` directly; `node bin.ts`; gate types with `tsc --noEmit` in CI. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Subpath aliases without a bundler:** `package.json` `"imports": { "#db/*": "./src/db/*.ts" }` — Node [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- honors these where it ignores `tsconfig` `paths`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Least-privilege service:** `node --permission --allow-fs-read=./config --allow-net app.js` (network [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- is open unless a build gates it; today fs/child/worker/addon/wasi/inspector are the gated axes). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- **Asset-bundled SEA:** put templates/migrations in `assets`, read with `sea.getAsset('schema.sql','utf8')`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Treating native stripping as a type checker — it never validates types; CI must run `tsc`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Writing `enum`/`namespace`/parameter-properties expecting native to run them (use `const` objects, [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- union types, plain assignment, or switch to tsx). [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Relying on `--experimental-transform-types` going forward — **removed in v26**. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Importing without extensions under native execution — resolution will fail. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Assuming `--permission` sandboxes malicious code or inherits to workers/symlink targets — it does not. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- Combining `useSnapshot: true` with `mainFormat: "module"`, or `import()` with `useCodeCache: true` — unsupported. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` → erase the offending construct or run via tsx. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `Cannot find module './x'` under native TS → add the explicit `.ts` extension. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- A `.ts` dependency under `node_modules` won't run → libraries must publish compiled `.js` + `.d.ts`. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- `ERR_ACCESS_DENIED` with `permission: 'FileSystemRead'` → add `--allow-fs-read=<path>`; check the [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- worker is granted separately. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- SEA "is experimental" warning → set `disableExperimentalSEAWarning: true` in the config. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]
- SEA binary won't launch on macOS → you must `codesign --sign -` after injection. [src: nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features]

- Three post-Express Node.js/TypeScript backend frameworks. They share the HTTP-handler foundation captured in the `express-patterns` hub reference (middleware chains, routing, error handling, graceful shutdown, security hardening) — read that first; this reference covers what each framework does *differently*. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- > Full reference: `~/.claude/skills/software-engineering-patterns/references/nodejs-backend-frameworks.md`. Cross-refs: Express baseline → express-patterns; API surface design → api-design-patterns; backend architecture → backend-patterns; auth flows → web-auth-patterns; Zod/TypeBox depth → zod-schema-validation; edge/Bun/Deno runtimes → programming-languages/javascript-runtimes-deno-bun-edge. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **NestJS** — heavyweight, opinionated architecture + DI container + enterprise modules (decorator/Angular-style). Node only; uses Express OR Fastify as the HTTP adapter; no edge runtimes. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Fastify** — mid-weight, Express-like ergonomics + raw speed + built-in JSON-Schema validation/serialization; minimal opinions. Node only. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Hono** — lightweight (~14KB), Web-Standards (Request/Response) based, edge-native, tight type inference. Runs on Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, Lambda, Fastly, Node. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- Synthetic JSON throughput: Hono ~78k req/s, Fastify ~62k req/s. Raw speed rarely decides real apps — DB/business logic dominate. Choose on architecture, runtime target, team conventions. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Plugins + encapsulation context** governs which decorators/hooks/schemas a route sees; child contexts are isolated. **`fastify-plugin` (`fp`)** breaks encapsulation on purpose — wrap shared capabilities (DB, auth decorator) so parent/siblings see them. "Decorator not defined on parent" = missing `fp`. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Lifecycle hooks** (all encapsulated except onClose): onRequest → preParsing → preValidation → preHandler → handler → preSerialization → onSend → onResponse. `onError` is read-only; change error responses via `setErrorHandler()`. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **JSON Schema** on a route validates input AND compiles response serialization (fast-json-stringify) — a big speed source. `addSchema()` registers reusable schemas (encapsulated). **TypeBox + @fastify/type-provider-typebox** = one schema is both runtime validator and TS type. Async custom validators must return `{error}`, not throw (thrown → unhandled rejection → crash). [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Decorators**: `decorateRequest('x', {})` shares ONE object across requests — init `null`, assign in `onRequest`. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Gotchas**: returning `undefined` from async handler = "no response"; mixing `return value` + `reply.send()` discards the second; after async `reply.send()` do `return reply`; arrow-function handlers don't bind `this`. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Modules + hierarchical DI**: providers encapsulated by default; `exports` is the public API; other modules access via `imports`. `@Global()` sparingly. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Providers + scopes**: default singleton; `Scope.REQUEST` (per request, perf cost, bubbles up injection chain); `Scope.TRANSIENT` (per injection site). Custom providers: useClass/useValue/useFactory/useExisting. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Request pipeline (fixed order)**: Middleware → Guards → Interceptors(pre) → Pipes → Handler → Interceptors(post) → Exception Filters. Guards = authZ; Interceptors = wrap handler (RxJS, transform req/resp); Pipes = validate/transform input; Filters = shape error responses. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Dynamic modules** (`forRoot`/`forFeature` → DynamicModule) for configurable infra. **Circular deps** → `forwardRef()` on both sides; treat as a smell, prefer refactor. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **HTTP adapter**: swap `@nestjs/platform-express` for `@nestjs/platform-fastify` for Fastify throughput under Nest's architecture. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Web-Standards core + Context `c`**: built on WHATWG Request/Response → runs everywhere. Middleware is `async (c, next) => {...}` (Koa onion model), no separate req/res. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Routing + typed generics**: default `RegExpRouter` is fastest on Workers. `new Hono<{ Variables, Bindings }>()` makes `c.get('user')` and `c.env.DB` typed end-to-end. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Validation + RPC**: `@hono/zod-validator` (+ Valibot/Typia/ArkType) gives typed `c.req.valid()`. RPC mode: export app type, `hc<typeof app>(url)` infers paths/args/returns — type-safe client, no codegen. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Batteries**: JWT, basic/bearer auth, CORS, CSRF, secure-headers, ETag, cache, compression, body-limit, IP restriction, timing, timeout, SSE, WebSockets, JSX SSR. Edge wins are mostly geography (Workers at nearest PoP) + low overhead. Recommended for Node→Bun migration. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **NestJS** — enterprise architecture, 3+ team, long-lived backend, first-party modules, Angular/.NET background, edge not required. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Fastify** — standalone Node API, Express-shaped + faster + built-in validation, pick-your-own ORM/auth. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Hono** — Cloudflare Workers/Vercel Edge/Deno/Bun/Lambda, smallest/fastest/most-inferred, serverless/edge, Node→Bun. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **Express** — max middleware ecosystem/familiarity, no strong perf/validation/edge need. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- **NestJS + Fastify adapter** = Nest architecture + Fastify speed. NestJS does NOT run on edge runtimes. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- Fastify docs (Encapsulation, Plugins, Hooks, Validation-and-Serialization, Decorators, Errors); Nearform Fastify plugin guide; Strapi Fastify APIs; NestJS docs (Modules, Circular dependency, Performance/Fastify); DeepWiki NestJS request pipeline; LogRocket circular deps; Hono docs (Concepts, RPC, Validation, Benchmarks, Stacks); Cloudflare Hono story; freeCodeCamp Hono; Encore NestJS-vs-Fastify-vs-Hono (2026); Better Stack Hono-vs-Fastify; HireNodeJS frameworks 2026. [src: nodejs-backend-frameworks]
- <!-- hub-reference-banner --> [src: python-static-type-checking]
- > **Reference file — part of the `programming-languages` hub.** Authored via `/dr` (deep-research). Not a standalone skill. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- > Sibling topics in this family are reference files under the hubs (`programming-languages`, `software-engineering-patterns`) — **not** standalone skills. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- > Cross-refs: `references/python-patterns.md` (PEP 695 type-hint *syntax*, generics — this file covers the *checkers*), `references/pydantic-v2.md` (runtime validation + the `pydantic.mypy` plugin), `references/typescript-expert.md` (the TS analog of gradual static typing). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Python type checkers are **external static-analysis tools**, not part of the interpreter. The CPython runtime ignores annotations (beyond storing them in `__annotations__`); a separate tool reads the same annotations a human reads and proves type consistency *before* the code runs. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- As of mid-2026 the landscape is a **two-generation split**: established Python-implemented checkers (**mypy**, **Pyright**) and new **Rust-implemented** checkers (**Astral ty**, **Meta Pyrefly**) that are 10-80x faster. Pyrefly reached stable **1.0.0 (May 2026)**; ty is still **beta (0.x)**. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **PEP 483 + PEP 484 (2015)** define *gradual typing*: hints are optional, coexist with dynamic typing, added incrementally. Goal is NOT runtime enforcement — annotations exist for external tools. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **`Any`** is consistent with every type (assignable to/from anything) — the seam between static and dynamic. Unannotated code is effectively `Any`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **The gradual guarantee:** removing an annotation should never add new errors (adding annotations only narrows errors). ty and Pyright honor it strictly; mypy and Pyrefly infer aggressively and can violate it. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **PEP 561:** inline-typed packages ship a **`py.typed`** marker; stub-only packages are **`types-<pkg>`** (types-requests) or **`<pkg>-stubs`**; stub files are **`.pyi`**; resolution order stubs → inline → **typeshed** (the community stub repo). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **typing-spec conformance suite** is the shared benchmark. Pyrefly 1.0.0 reports >90% (above ty and mypy); Pyright tracks the spec closely. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- *Declared* types (you annotated) vs *inferred* types (deduced) — checkers agree on declared, disagree on inference (§3). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- CLI: `mypy <path>`, `pyright <path>`, `ty check <path>`, `pyrefly check <path>`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- For `my_list = []; my_list.append(1)`: [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **mypy, Pyrefly** infer `list[int]` from usage → later `append("foo")` is an **error**. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Pyright, ty** infer `list[Unknown]`, stay permissive → `append("foo")` **allowed** (gradual guarantee). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Generics: `c: C[int] = C()` reveals `C[int]` (Pyrefly) vs `C[Unknown]` (ty). mypy/Pyrefly catch more bugs in loose code but more false positives; Pyright/ty cause fewer surprises during adoption. `reveal_type(x)` prints inferred type during a check. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Skips unannotated function bodies by default** (#1 gotcha) — `--check-untyped-defs` or `--strict` to check inside them. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- `--strict` bundles all optional checks. Key flags: `disallow_untyped_defs`, `disallow_incomplete_defs`, `disallow_any_generics`, `warn_return_any`, `warn_unused_ignores`, `no_implicit_optional`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Config: `mypy.ini` / `setup.cfg` / `[tool.mypy]`. Per-module `[[tool.mypy.overrides]]` for strict-by-default, loose-for-legacy: [src: python-static-type-checking]
- plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"] [src: python-static-type-checking]
- module = ["legacy.*"] [src: python-static-type-checking]
- disallow_untyped_defs = false [src: python-static-type-checking]
- ignore_missing_imports = true [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Plugins (unique to mypy):** understand dynamic patterns (ORMs, metaclasses) — `pydantic.mypy`, `sqlalchemy.ext.mypy.plugin`. mypy 2.0 added `--num-workers` (~1.3x). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Checks all code by default** (opposite of mypy). **Five strictness levels:** `off`/`basic`/`standard`(default)/`strict`/`all`. `strict` adds ~30 rules, ~10x more errors than basic. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Per-rule `reportXxx` keys = `"none"|"warning"|"error"` (e.g. `reportUnknownMemberType`). Config `[tool.pyright]` or `pyrightconfig.json`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **No plugins** (stubs only). Powers **Pylance** (closed-source VS Code, best-in-class). **BasedPyright** = OSS fork, stricter defaults. Suppress: `# pyright: ignore[reportXxx]`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- uv/ruff team; Rust; **Salsa** fine-grained incremental engine → re-diagnoses a PyTorch file in ~4.7ms (~80x faster than Pyright's ~386ms). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Conservative inference (`Unknown` type) + strict gradual guarantee. **Only checker with intersection & negation types** (`MyClass & ~MySubclass`). Concise/structured errors. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **beta, 0.0.x, no stable API** — diagnostics can change between releases. Config `[tool.ty]`; full LSP (VS Code/Neovim/Zed/PyCharm). Roadmap: ruff/uv integration. CLI `ty check`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Rust **successor to Pyre** (Instagram's OCaml checker). MIT, open-sourced May 2025; **stable 1.0.0 May 2026**. Module-level incremental + multithreaded. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Aggressive inference** (mypy camp), strong generics. **`pyrefly infer`** writes inferred annotations directly into source (migration accelerator no other checker has). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Instagram (~20M LOC) in 13.4s; PyTorch ~2.4s. **Conformance >90%** (above ty/mypy). Adoption at PyTorch, JAX. Config `[tool.pyrefly]`; CLI `pyrefly check`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Existing project / established CI:** mypy (plugins, maturity). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Best VS Code:** Pyright/Pylance or BasedPyright (OSS, stricter). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **New project, max catch + speed, OK with aggressive inference:** Pyrefly (stable, highest conformance). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **Predictable incremental adoption + fastest, tolerate beta:** ty. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- **CI:** run a Rust checker as the fast gate; don't run two strict checkers as blocking gates (their inference disagreements fight). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Start permissive, ratchet strictness from a clean baseline. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Strict-by-default, loose-for-legacy via per-module overrides. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Fix missing third-party types: install `types-<pkg>` or scope `ignore_missing_imports` — don't blanket-ignore. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Auto-annotate with `pyrefly infer`, then review. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Ship `py.typed` (PEP 561) so downstream trusts your inline types. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Gate in CI once clean; track error count downward. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Trusting mypy's default coverage (it skips unannotated bodies — green can mean "nothing checked"). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Blanket `# type: ignore` — scope it (`# type: ignore[arg-type]`); set `warn_unused_ignores`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Two strict checkers as blocking gates (inference disagrees). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Expecting runtime enforcement — checkers never run code; for runtime validation use **Pydantic v2**. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- `Any` creep — prefer `object`/`Protocol`/precise union; `disallow_any_generics`/`warn_return_any`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Assuming ty diagnostics are stable (0.x — pin the version). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- "missing library stubs" → install `types-<pkg>` or scope `ignore_missing_imports`; check for `py.typed`. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- "works in mypy, errors in Pyright" → inference divergence (§3) or mypy-plugin behavior Pyright can't replicate. No parity. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Slow mypy → incremental cache (default on), `--num-workers`, or move fast gate to ty/Pyrefly. [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Pydantic/SQLAlchemy "untyped" on Pyright/ty/Pyrefly → those rely on mypy *plugins*; use native typing (Pydantic v2 is natively typed). [src: python-static-type-checking]
- Error flood after strict → expected (Pyright strict ≈ 10x basic); ratchet per-module. [src: python-static-type-checking]
