- **`--test-reporter-destination`** (`stdout` or a file). The two flags pair positionally, [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- so you can run **several at once** — e.g. spec to the terminal and junit to a file. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- A **custom reporter** is any module default-exporting a function/stream that consumes the [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- `TestsStream` events (`test:pass`, `test:fail`, `test:diagnostic`, `test:coverage`, …). [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Filtering & execution.** `node --test` discovers files by default globs: `*.test.*`, [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- `*-test.*`, `*_test.*`, files named `test.*`, files starting with `test-`, and **any [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- `.js/.cjs/.mjs` under a `test/` directory** (recursively). You can instead pass quoted [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- glob args. Filter by name with **`--test-name-pattern`** (regex; tests whose name [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- matches run) and **`--test-skip-pattern`** (regex; matches are skipped) — supply both [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- and a test must satisfy both. **`only`-mode**: mark `test('x', { only: true }, …)` (or [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **`--test-concurrency`** caps parallel *files* (default `availableParallelism() - 1`). [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **`--test-isolation`** chooses `process` (default — each file in its own child process, [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- crash-isolated) or `none` (all files in one process; faster, shares state, forces [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- across machines (incompatible with watch). **`--watch`** with `--test` re-runs affected [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- tests on file change (generic `--watch` semantics live in [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- `nodejs-builtin-modules-modern`). [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Snapshot testing (stable, Node 22.3+ / marked stable later):** `t.assert.snapshot(value, options?)` [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- compares `value` to a stored snapshot. Generate/update snapshots by running with [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **`--test-update-snapshots`**; the snapshot file defaults to `<testfile>.snapshot`. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- Customize **serializers** via `options.serializers` (array of `value => string` [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- functions, applied in order) and relocate files with [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Assertions:** `node:test` integrates **`node:assert/strict`** — use [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- `assert.strictEqual`, `assert.deepStrictEqual`, `assert.throws`, `assert.rejects`, [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Always `await` subtests** (`await t.test(...)`, or `await Promise.all([...])` for [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- parallel siblings) so they're counted and not orphaned. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Prefer `t.mock` over the global `mock`** — per-test mocks auto-restore at test end, [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- so you never leak a stub into the next test. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Pass `t.signal` into async work** (`fetch(url, { signal: t.signal })`, timers) so a [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Fake timers for time-logic**: `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setTimeout','Date'] })` [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- then `tick()` to drive debounce/retry/TTL code deterministically — no real waiting. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **CI reporter combo**: `node --test --experimental-test-coverage [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Un-awaited subtests** — the parent finishes, the subtest is cancelled and reported [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- as failing. The #1 node:test footgun. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Reusing the global `mock` without restoring** — stubs bleed across tests; use [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Static-importing the module you intend to `mock.module()`** — the import already [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Forgetting `--experimental-test-module-mocks`** — `mock.module()` silently does [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- nothing (or throws) without the flag. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Treating `--experimental-test-coverage` as a gate** — collection alone never fails [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- the build; you need the `--test-coverage-*` *threshold* flags for that. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Real timers / real sleeps in tests** — slow and flaky; fake them with `mock.timers`. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **`--test-isolation=none` while expecting per-file isolation** — all files share one [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- process and global state; a leak in one file corrupts others. [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- **Reaching for Jest/Vitest mocking idioms** (`jest.fn`, `vi.mock`) here — wrong API; [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Subtest "was cancelled" / counts wrong** → `await` the `t.test()` call (or the [src: nodejs-test-runner]
- `Promise.all` of them); check `t.plan()` matches the real assertion count. [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- `--test-coverage-exclude` didn't exclude your sources (test files are excluded by [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **Tests not discovered** → the file doesn't match the default globs and isn't under a [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- **`--test-name-pattern` skips everything** → it's a regex over the *full* test name; [src: nodejs-test-runner]

- resolve, lock, and secure* the dependencies a Node.js project pulls in. It covers the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- four mainstream package managers (npm, pnpm, Yarn Berry, bun), the lockfile + [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]

- mechanics, npm scripts/lifecycle, and the supply-chain hardening surface (audit, [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- provenance, install-script defenses, PM pinning). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- It deliberately stops at three boundaries owned by sibling references: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`nodejs-module-resolution`** — owns *how Node finds a module at runtime* [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- (`require`/CJS, `ESM_RESOLVE`, the `exports`/`imports` fields, conditional exports). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- This file gets the bytes onto disk; that file resolves a specifier against them. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`devops-containers-cicd` (library packaging)** — owns *publishing a library*: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]

- `semantic-release`. This file consumes the registry; that one ships to it. (Provenance [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- here is covered only as a *consumer* verification + the `--provenance` publish flag.) [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features`** — owns native TS loading, SEA, and the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]

- The mental model: **manifest (`package.json`) declares intent → resolver picks concrete [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- versions → lockfile freezes them → installer materializes `node_modules` (or a PnP map) → [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- lifecycle scripts run → audit/provenance/pinning guard the supply chain.** [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- All four read `package.json`, but they materialize dependencies very differently: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **npm** — the default. Builds a **flat, hoisted `node_modules`**: transitive deps are [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- pulled up to the top level when versions allow. Simple and maximally compatible, but [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- hoisting exposes **phantom dependencies** — your code can `require` a package you never [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- declared (because a *transitive* dep hoisted it), and the import silently breaks the day [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- that transitive dep drops it. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **pnpm** — a **content-addressable global store** (`~/.pnpm-store`/`~/.local/share/pnpm`): [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- every file of every package version is stored once and **hard-linked** into projects, so [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- N projects sharing a version cost ~one copy on disk. `node_modules` is **symlinked and [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- isolated**: only packages you *actually declared* are reachable at the top level (the rest [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- live under `node_modules/.pnpm/`), which **eliminates phantom deps by construction**. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- Fastest on large/monorepo installs. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Yarn (Berry, v2+) with Plug'n'Play (PnP)** — eliminates `node_modules` entirely. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- Resolution lives in a generated **`.pnp.cjs`** loader that maps every package to its [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- location inside zipped caches; Node loads it via a runtime hook. Strict ("semantic [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- erroring" on undeclared deps), fast, low storage, and supports **zero-installs** [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- (commit the cache + `.pnp.cjs`). Fallback to a classic layout via [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `nodeLinker: node-modules` in `.yarnrc.yml` for tools that can't speak PnP (e.g. some [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- React Native setups). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **bun install** — Bun's installer is a drop-in for `npm install` that uses a **global [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- cache** (`~/.bun/install/cache/`) with **hardlinks / copy-on-write**, parallel downloads, [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- and platform-tuned syscalls (`hardlink` backend on Linux). Materializes a normal [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `node_modules`; markedly faster than npm on cold and warm installs. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- A lockfile pins the **entire resolved tree** (exact versions + resolved URLs + [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **integrity** hashes, typically SHA-512 / SRI) so a second install reproduces the first [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- bit-for-bit. Each PM has its own: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Always commit the lockfile** for apps (libraries usually publish without dictating [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- consumers' trees). It is the single source of truth for what actually ran in CI/prod. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`npm ci` vs `npm install`**: `npm install` *reconciles* — if a range in [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `package.json` no longer matches the lock, it re-resolves and **rewrites the lock**. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `npm ci` is **strict and reproducible**: it requires an existing lock that matches [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `package.json`, wipes `node_modules`, installs **exactly** the locked versions, and [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **errors** on any mismatch (it never edits the lock). Use `npm ci` in CI/CD and [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- post-clone. The frozen equivalents: `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` (Classic) / [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `--immutable` (Berry), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- A workspace is a repo of multiple packages sharing one install + one lock, with local [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- packages linked to each other instead of being fetched from the registry. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Declaration**: npm and Yarn use a `"workspaces": [...]` array in the root [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `package.json`; **pnpm uses a dedicated `pnpm-workspace.yaml`** (`packages:` globs). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **The `workspace:` protocol** (originated in pnpm; supported by Yarn Berry and npm 7+): [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- a dependency written `"pkg-a": "workspace:*"` (or `workspace:^`) **must** resolve to the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- local workspace package, never the registry. On publish, the PM rewrites `workspace:*` [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- to the concrete version so external consumers get a normal range. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Hoisting vs isolation**: npm/Yarn-classic hoist shared deps to the root (re-exposing [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- phantom-dep risk across the monorepo); pnpm keeps each package isolated by default. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Running scripts across packages**: npm `--workspace=<name>` / `--workspaces`; Yarn [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `yarn workspace <name> <cmd>` / `yarn workspaces foreach`; pnpm `--filter <name>` and [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`-r`** (recursive). pnpm/Yarn order execution by the **dependency graph** (build a [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- package's local deps first); this topological awareness is a major monorepo win. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- Ranges in `package.json` are **semver** (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`); the resolver picks the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- highest published version satisfying every constraint, then **dedupes** shared transitive [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Range operators**: `^1.2.3` allows the **leftmost-non-zero** to stay fixed → `>=1.2.3 [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- <2.0.0` (npm/Yarn/pnpm default on `add`); `~1.2.3` allows only patch bumps → `>=1.2.3 [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- <1.3.0`. Beware `^0.x`: `^0.2.3` means `>=0.2.3 <0.3.0` (minor is treated as breaking [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- while major is 0). Also `1.2.x`, `*`, `>=`, `||`, hyphen ranges. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`peerDependencies`** — "the host must provide this" (e.g. a React plugin peers [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `react`). Auto-install behavior **differs per PM** — state it precisely: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **npm 7+**: auto-installs missing peers by default (npm ≤6 only *warned*). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **pnpm 8+**: `auto-install-peers` defaults to **true** (it was `false` in v7). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Yarn Berry**: does **not** auto-install peers — it warns and you add them yourself. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- On a *conflicting* peer requirement, PMs decline to auto-install and warn. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`optionalDependencies`** — install failure is non-fatal (used for platform-specific [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- native binaries); guard usage with try/catch since they may be absent. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Overriding a transitive version** (force a patched nested dep) — the field name [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **differs per PM**: npm `"overrides"`, **Yarn `"resolutions"`**, pnpm `"pnpm.overrides"`. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- The primary lever for fast supply-chain remediation when a deep dep is vulnerable but its [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- parent hasn't bumped. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`engines`** — declares supported `node`/PM versions; advisory by default, enforced with [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `engine-strict` (npm) / `engineStrict`. Pair with the `packageManager` field (concept 6). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `"scripts"` in `package.json` defines named commands run via `npm run <name>`. npm [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **auto-wraps** any script with hooks: running `<name>` executes `pre<name>` → `<name>` → [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `post<name>` in sequence (e.g. `prebuild`/`build`/`postbuild`). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Install lifecycle**: `preinstall` → `install` → `postinstall` run during [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `npm install`. **`postinstall` is the most-abused hook** — it's how a malicious dependency [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- gets arbitrary code execution on `npm install` (see concept 6). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`prepare`** runs on local install (no package args) and before `npm pack`/`npm publish`; [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- npm guidance is to **use `prepare` for build steps, not `install`/`preinstall`** — the only [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- legitimate use of `install`/`preinstall` is native compilation that must happen on the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Security note — `node --run` skips pre/post hooks.** Node's built-in `node --run <script>` [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- executes *only* the named script and, by **intentional design, does NOT run `pre`/`post` [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- lifecycle scripts** (and ignores `NODE_OPTIONS`). That makes it faster and more predictable, [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- but means a `predeploy`/`postdeploy` you *rely on* will silently not run. For the full [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `node --run` runtime semantics see **`nodejs-builtin-modules-modern`** (or [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features`). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- The dependency graph is the largest untrusted attack surface in a Node app. The defenses: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`npm audit`** cross-checks the installed tree against the advisory DB; `npm audit fix` [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- remediates within ranges, `--force` may bump majors (review the diff). **`npm audit [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- signatures`** verifies registry signatures **and provenance attestations** — tying audit [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- to concept-6 provenance. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Provenance & trusted publishing** (GA 2023, via **Sigstore**): publishing with [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`npm publish --provenance`** from a supported CI (GitHub Actions, GitLab) creates a [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- cryptographically signed, publicly logged (Rekor transparency log) link between the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- published tarball, the **source commit**, and the **build**. **Trusted publishing** uses [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- short-lived CI **OIDC** tokens instead of long-lived npm tokens, so a leaked token can't [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- publish. As a *consumer*, you verify with `npm audit signatures` / the package's [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- provenance badge. (Authoring/publishing detail lives in `devops-containers-cicd`.) [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Install-scripts attack surface**: a compromised package's `postinstall` runs on [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `npm install`. **`--ignore-scripts`** (or `npm config set ignore-scripts true`) blocks all [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- lifecycle scripts — OWASP calls it the single most effective mitigation; re-enable per-package [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- only for deps that genuinely need native compilation. **`--omit=dev`** / **`--omit=optional`** [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- trims the prod install surface (replaces the old `--production`/`--no-optional`). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Dependency confusion** (a.k.a. substitution): if a build pulls from a private *and* the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- public registry, an attacker publishes a public package with your **internal name** at a [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **higher version**, and the resolver grabs the malicious one. Mitigate by **scoping** [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- internal packages (`@org/...`) and pinning that scope's registry in `.npmrc`, and never [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- letting a public range win over an internal name. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Lockfile injection**: a malicious PR edits the lockfile to point a name at a different [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- tarball/URL while leaving `package.json` innocent-looking. Mitigate by **reviewing lockfile [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- diffs**, using `npm ci`/frozen installs (which honor the lock's integrity hash), and [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- version/cooldown policies (rejecting versions published in the last N days blunts [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- fast-moving compromise windows). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Pinning the package manager** — **corepack** + the **`packageManager` field**: [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `"packageManager": "pnpm@9.1.0+sha224.<hash>"` (name@version, optional but recommended [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- hash). Corepack (shipped with Node) reads it and transparently runs *that exact* PM [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- version, so every contributor and CI uses the same tool — closing a reproducibility/trust [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- gap the lockfile alone can't (the lock pins deps, not the resolver). `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- are the permitted values; explicit pinning beats `COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN`. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **CI/CD always uses the frozen install** — `npm ci` / `pnpm i --frozen-lockfile` / [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `yarn install --immutable` / `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. It's faster (skips [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- re-resolution), reproducible, and fails loudly on lock drift. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Pin the PM with `packageManager` + corepack** so "works on my machine" can't be a [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- resolver-version difference. Commit the field; let corepack enforce it. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Default to `--ignore-scripts` org-wide**, then allowlist the handful of deps that need [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- native builds. Combine with `--omit=dev`/`--omit=optional` for prod images. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Remediate deep CVEs with the override field** (`overrides`/`resolutions`/`pnpm.overrides`) [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- to force a patched transitive version while you wait for the parent to bump. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Reach for pnpm on monorepos** — graph-ordered `--filter -r` runs and the isolated store [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- are the biggest practical wins; reach for Yarn PnP for strictness + zero-installs, and bun [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- install for raw speed. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Verify provenance on critical deps** (`npm audit signatures`) and prefer packages [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- published with provenance/trusted publishing. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Not committing the lockfile** (or `.gitignore`-ing it) — you forfeit reproducibility and [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- can't audit what actually shipped. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`npm install` in CI** instead of `npm ci` — lets a stale/mismatched lock silently [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- re-resolve and rewrite, defeating the whole point of locking. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Relying on a phantom dependency** — importing a package you never declared because it [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- hoisted; it breaks the day a transitive dep drops it. (pnpm/PnP make this an immediate [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- error — a feature, not a nuisance.) [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Running `npm install` untrusted with scripts enabled** — a single `postinstall` is RCE. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- Audit new deps and default to `--ignore-scripts`. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`audit fix --force` without reading the diff** — it can pull a breaking major and quietly [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Mixing package managers in one repo** (an `npm install` over a pnpm project) — produces a [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- conflicting/second lockfile and an inconsistent tree. Pin one PM via `packageManager`. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Wide-open `*` / `latest` ranges or `^0.x` blindness** — surrenders control over what [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- resolves and widens the compromise window. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`npm ci` fails: "lock file's ... does not satisfy ... in package.json"** → the lock is [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- out of sync; run `npm install` locally to reconcile and **commit the updated lock**, then [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `npm ci` passes. Never hand-edit the lock to fix this. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`ERESOLVE` peer-dependency conflict (npm 7+)** → a peer range can't be satisfied across [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- the tree. Fix the real version, or use `overrides`; `--legacy-peer-deps` *suppresses* the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- check (last resort — it ships a tree npm considers invalid). [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **"Cannot find module X" after switching to pnpm/Yarn PnP** → X was a phantom dependency; [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **declare it** in `package.json` (PnP: or add via `packageExtensions`). This is the strict [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- layout doing its job. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Integrity / `EINTEGRITY` checksum mismatch** → the downloaded tarball's hash ≠ the lock's [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- `integrity`. Clear the cache (`npm cache clean --force`), confirm the registry, and treat an [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- unexplained mismatch as a possible tampering/lockfile-injection signal. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **Different results local vs CI** → almost always a **PM-version** drift (pin via corepack) [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- or `npm install` vs `npm ci`. Lock the resolver, not just the deps. [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- **`postinstall`/build step not running under `node --run`** → expected: `node --run` skips [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]
- pre/post hooks by design. Use `npm run` (or call the script explicitly) when you need the [src: nodejs-package-management-supply-chain]

- This reference is the **consolidated Node.js security playbook**: the threats that [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- are specific to running JavaScript on a server with full OS access, and the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- defenses Node ships for them. It is organized threat → defense so you can go from [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- a symptom ("untrusted JSON reaches a merge", "user input reaches `child_process`") [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- straight to the mitigation. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Node's own **threat model** sets the boundary: Node trusts the code it is asked to [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- run and the OS environment it runs in. Everything here is about defending the line [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- between **trusted application code** and **untrusted external input** — request [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- bodies, query strings, JSON, transcripts, file paths, third-party packages. It is [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- *not* about sandboxing untrusted code (Node explicitly does not do that). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- This file owns the *application-layer* attack surface. Several adjacent concerns [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- live in sibling references and are deferred, not duplicated: [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Permission-Model mechanics** (the full `--allow-fs-read`/`--allow-net`/SEA [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- flag matrix) → `nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features`. Here we cover only [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- *why* the model is defense-in-depth, not a sandbox. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Package-manager workflows** (lockfile/audit/workspace mechanics) → [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `nodejs-package-management-supply-chain`. Here we cover supply chain as *risk*. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **HTTP security headers** (Helmet, CSP, HSTS, CORS) → `http-security-headers`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Web Crypto / vault / encryption-at-rest** → `webcrypto-vault-reviewer`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **OAuth/OIDC/session auth flows** → `web-auth-patterns`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Event-loop / ReDoS-*blocking* mechanics** → `nodejs-concurrency-internals`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Here we cover ReDoS only from the *defense* angle. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- The mental model: **validate untrusted input at the boundary, deny shells and [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- dynamic eval, freeze what should be immutable, and treat every dependency as [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- untrusted code.** Defense-in-depth — no single flag makes a Node app safe. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- JavaScript objects inherit from `Object.prototype`. If an attacker can write a key [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- named `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` into an object built from [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- untrusted data, they mutate that shared prototype — and every object in the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- process suddenly carries the injected property. The classic sink is an **insecure [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- recursive merge / deep-clone / `extend`** (CVE-2018-16487 in lodash) or a [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **query-string parser** that auto-vivifies nested keys (`?__proto__[isAdmin]=1`). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- const data = JSON.parse('{"__proto__": { "polluted": true }}'); [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- const c = Object.assign({}, { a: 1 }, data); [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- console.log(({}).polluted); // true  — every object is now polluted [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Impact:** ranges from logic corruption and DoS to privilege escalation and, via [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- a *gadget*, full RCE (a polluted `.env`/`.shell` property read by a later [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `child_process` call — see concept 6). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Defenses (layer them):** [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Validate against a schema** (Ajv/zod) at the boundary — the strongest fix; [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- reject unexpected keys with `additionalProperties: false`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Use **null-prototype objects** for dictionaries: `Object.create(null)` (no [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `__proto__` to pollute) or a **`Map`** instead of an object-as-dictionary. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`Object.freeze(MyClass.prototype)`** / `Object.freeze(Object.prototype)` to [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- block writes to a specific prototype. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`--disable-proto=throw`** (or `=delete`) removes the `Object.prototype.__proto__` [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- accessor process-wide — `throw` raises `ERR_PROTO_ACCESS` on access, `delete` [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- A **`JSON.parse` reviver** that drops `__proto__`/`constructor` keys; check [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- ownership with `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)`, never inherited lookups. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Avoid hand-rolled recursive merges on untrusted data; if unavoidable, skip the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- three magic keys explicitly. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Command injection** is the highest-severity Node-specific sink. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `child_process.exec()` / `execSync()` **spawn a shell** (`/bin/sh`) and the Node [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- docs warn verbatim: *"Never pass unsanitized user input to this function. Any [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- input containing shell metacharacters may be used to trigger arbitrary command [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- execution."* Defense: prefer **`execFile()` or `spawn()`**, which run the binary [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- directly **without a shell by default**, and pass arguments as a **separate [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- array** (`spawn('git', ['log', userRef])`) so metacharacters are never parsed. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Keep **`shell: false`** (the default) — enabling `shell: true` re-introduces the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- exact `exec` vulnerability. Never build a command string by concatenating input. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`eval()` / `new Function()` / `vm` with untrusted strings** is direct RCE — OWASP [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- calls it inherently a remote-code-execution vulnerability. Don't evaluate user [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- input; use a parser/lookup table instead. `vm` is **not** a security sandbox. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Path traversal:** untrusted input flowing into `fs.*` enables `../../etc/passwd` [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- file inclusion. Normalize with `path.resolve()`, then assert the result [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `startsWith` the intended base directory; reject otherwise. Decode and strip [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `..`/null bytes before use. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **SQL/NoSQL injection** lives at the app layer: always use **parameterized [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- queries / prepared statements** (driver placeholders), never string-built SQL. For [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- MongoDB, reject object-typed values where a scalar is expected (`{$gt:''}` [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- operator injection from query strings) and cast inputs to their expected type. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Node ships process-level flags that shrink the attack surface as **defense-in-depth**: [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- The **Permission Model is defense-in-depth, not a security boundary.** The Node [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- docs are explicit: *"The permission model implements a 'seat belt' approach … [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- It does not provide security guarantees in the presence of malicious code. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Malicious code can bypass the permission model and execute arbitrary code."* It [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- *"trusts any code it is asked to run."* So `--permission` is useful to prevent [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- *trusted* code (and its dependencies) from *accidentally* touching the filesystem [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- or network — a containment layer, not a jail for untrusted code. (The [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `--allow-*` flag matrix, scoping, and SEA mechanics are deferred to [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features`.) Also: don't enable experimental [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- features in production unless you accept the breaking-change risk. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Keep secrets in the environment, not in source.** Read from `process.env`; [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- never commit `.env` files or hard-coded API keys/tokens (CWE-552). Add `.env` to [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `.gitignore` and use an allowlist (`files` in `package.json`, `.npmignore`) so a [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `npm publish` doesn't leak them — verify with `npm publish --dry-run`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`--env-file` caveat:** `--env-file=.env` loads vars into `process.env`, *and it [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- also parses Node-configuring vars like `NODE_OPTIONS`*. The docs warn Node *"will [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- not sanitize or perform validation on the user-provided configuration, so NEVER [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- use untrusted configuration files."* A writable `.env` is therefore a code-exec [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- vector (it can inject `NODE_OPTIONS`). `--env-file` is also **not** subject to [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Permission-Model restrictions. Use a real secrets manager for production. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Never put secrets in logs or error responses.** Redact tokens/passwords/keys [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- before logging; don't echo stack traces or `err.message` containing connection [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- strings to clients. Centralize redaction in the logger. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`process.env` hygiene:** read each secret once at startup into a typed config [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- object; don't pass the whole `process.env` into child processes or templates [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- (a prototype-pollution gadget can poison it — concept 6). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- Most of a Node app's code is third-party and runs with full privilege. Treat the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- dependency tree as an attack surface: [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`npm audit` + CVE response:** scan regularly; for a flagged CVE, upgrade to the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- fixed version (or apply an override) and re-test. Don't ignore transitive [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Install-script risk:** `postinstall`/`preinstall` scripts run arbitrary code at [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- install time. For untrusted or audited installs use **`npm install [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- -ignore-scripts`** (or `npm config set ignore-scripts true`) and allowlist the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- few packages that legitimately need a build step. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Dependency confusion:** if your build resolves from both a private and the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- public registry, an attacker can publish a public package with your *internal* [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- name and win. Defense: **publish internal packages under an `@your-scope/`**, [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- register that scope publicly even if unused, and pin the scope to the private [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- registry in `.npmrc` (`@your-scope:registry=…`). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Lockfile integrity:** commit `package-lock.json` (it records exact versions [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- *and* the resolved registry + integrity hash) and install with **`npm ci`**, [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- which fails on any lockfile/`package.json` mismatch. Guard against lockfile [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- poisoning in review. (Lockfile/workspace *workflow* mechanics → [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `nodejs-package-management-supply-chain`.) [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Keep Node patched:** track Node.js **security releases** and run a supported [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- (Active LTS or Maintenance) line; EOL versions get no security fixes. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **SSRF (server-side request forgery):** any server-side `fetch`/`undici`/`http` [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- call to a **user-controlled URL** can be steered at internal services or the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- cloud **metadata endpoint `169.254.169.254`** to steal credentials. Node's [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- built-in fetch has no SSRF guard. Defense: **allowlist** permitted hosts/schemes; [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **resolve the hostname to IP and reject private/reserved ranges** [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- (loopback/private/link-local/ULA/IPv4-mapped) *before* connecting; **disable or [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- re-validate redirects** (a 302 can point inward); beware DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU — [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- validate at connect time (libraries: `request-filtering-agent`, `ssrf-req-filter`). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **ReDoS (regex denial-of-service):** a regex with catastrophic backtracking [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- (nested quantifiers like `(a+)+$`, overlapping alternations) hangs on a crafted [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- input. *Defense angle:* avoid such patterns, **cap input length**, prefer a [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- linear engine (**RE2** / `node:re2`), and screen patterns with `safe-regex` / [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `vuln-regex-detector`. (*Why* it stalls the whole process — the event-loop [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- blocking mechanics — is in `nodejs-concurrency-internals`.) [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444):** ambiguous `Content-Length`/`Transfer-Encoding` [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- framing lets a request slip past a front-end. Don't set [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`insecureHTTPParser: true`**; normalize at the proxy; prefer end-to-end HTTP/2. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Unsafe deserialization:** `JSON.parse` is safe for data, but libraries that [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- deserialize *functions* (e.g. **`node-serialize` ≤0.0.4** `unserialize()`) execute [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- attacker-supplied **IIFE** payloads → RCE. Never deserialize untrusted input with a [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- function-capable format; restrict to JSON + schema validation. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Validate at the boundary, once.** Run every external payload through an Ajv/zod [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- schema with `additionalProperties:false` *before* it touches business logic — this [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- closes prototype pollution, type-confusion NoSQL injection, and oversized-field [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Ban the shell.** Lint for `child_process.exec`/`execSync` and `shell:true`; [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- standardize on `execFile`/`spawn` with argument arrays. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Run with `--disable-proto=throw`** (cheap, high-value) and consider [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `--frozen-intrinsics` once you've confirmed your polyfills load via `--require`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Wrap untrusted text** (transcripts, Slack, case bodies, anything fed to an LLM [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- or template) in an escaped envelope so it can't be interpreted as control input — [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- the same discipline as parameterizing a query. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Gate outbound URLs** through a single SSRF-filtering agent so no code path can [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- fetch an arbitrary user URL directly. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`npm ci` in CI**, `--ignore-scripts` for untrusted installs, and a scheduled [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `npm audit` + Node-version check so patch cadence isn't manual. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Deep-merging untrusted JSON** with a hand-rolled or old-lodash `merge` and no [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- schema — the #1 prototype-pollution foothold. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`child_process.exec('cmd ' + userInput)`** or flipping `shell:true` "to make it [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- work" — arbitrary command execution. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`eval`/`new Function` on request data**, or trusting `vm` as a sandbox. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Committing `.env`**, logging full error objects with secrets, or loading an [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **untrusted `--env-file`** (it can inject `NODE_OPTIONS`). [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Treating `--permission` as a sandbox** for untrusted code — it is a seat belt [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- for *trusted* code; malicious code bypasses it. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Fetching a user-supplied URL** server-side with no allowlist / private-range [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- block — SSRF to `169.254.169.254`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`node-serialize.unserialize()`** (or any function-deserializing format) on [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- untrusted input — instant RCE. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Running an EOL Node version** or ignoring `npm audit` advisories. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Prototype pollution slipped through schema validation** → the validator ran [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- *after* the merge, or allowed `additionalProperties`; validate first and set [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- `additionalProperties:false`. Confirm with `({}).polluted === undefined` after the [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`--frozen-intrinsics` breaks a dependency** → a library mutates a built-in; load [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- required polyfills via `--require`/`--import` (they run before the freeze) or drop [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- the flag for that service — it's experimental and root-context only. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **`execFile` still runs a shell** → you passed `shell:true` or a single [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- command-line string; pass the binary + an args array with `shell:false`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **SSRF filter bypassed** → likely DNS rebinding (TOCTOU) or an IPv6-mapped/redirect [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- bypass; re-validate the resolved IP at connect time and disallow redirects to new [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- **Regex still hangs after switching libraries** → the pattern is still [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- backtracking-prone; move to RE2 (linear) and cap input length. For *why* one [src: nodejs-security-hardening]
- blocked regex freezes all requests, see `nodejs-concurrency-internals`. [src: nodejs-security-hardening]

- This reference is about **turning Node.js + TypeScript source into a production [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- artifact** — a bundled server, a single-file CLI, a Lambda zip, or a publishable [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- library — and picking the tool that fits each shape. It is the *build-time* companion [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- to three sibling references that own adjacent layers: [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features`** — *runtime* TypeScript: native [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- type-stripping and dev runners (`tsx`, `ts-node`) that execute `.ts` directly. This [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- file covers `tsx` only at the boundary — "dev runner vs prod bundler." [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`nodejs-module-resolution`** — the resolution algorithm and `package.json` [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `"exports"`/conditions. This file *reads* those fields but does not re-derive them. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`nodejs-package-management-supply-chain`** / **`devops-containers-cicd`** — [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `npm`/`pnpm` install, lockfiles, publishing/provenance. This file produces the [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- artifact; those own how it is installed and shipped. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- The mental model: **most Node backends do not need a bundler at all.** Reach for one [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- only when single-file packaging, startup-time/cold-start, or library output quality [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- justifies it. Then choose by *output shape*: **esbuild/swc** to transpile fast, [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **tsup** for a dual-format library with types, **Rollup** for the cleanest library [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- bundle, **@vercel/ncc** to collapse everything into one file. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- Unlike the browser (where every byte is downloaded), a Node backend already has the [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- files on disk, so bundling is **optional and situational**. Ship **source + [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `node_modules`** for a normal long-lived server in a container: simplest path, honest [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- stack traces, native addons resolve normally. **Bundle** when you need: [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **A single distributable file** — a CLI published to npm (smaller install, fewer [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- files), a GitHub Action, or a Lambda/Edge artifact that must be self-contained. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Faster cold starts** — serverless functions pay per-file I/O at init; one [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- pre-resolved file with **dead-code elimination** (DCE) reduces parse/resolve cost. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **A library with multiple output formats** (ESM + CJS) and bundled internal modules. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Tree-shaking / DCE** statically drop unused exports; they work on **ES module** [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- syntax (`import`/`export`), not CommonJS `require`, which is why ESM input matters. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Minification** (whitespace + identifier renaming + syntax compression) shrinks bytes [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- — useful for libraries and Lambda size limits, rarely worth the debugging cost for a [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- plain server. Key caveat: keep **native addons** (`.node`), workers, and dynamic [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `require` paths **external** — bundlers can't trace them. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- raw speed. Two entry points: [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Transform API** (`esbuild.transform(code, opts)`) — processes a single in-memory [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- string "in an isolated environment that's completely disconnected from any other [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- files." No bundling, no plugins. Use it to transpile one file (TS→JS) in a pipeline. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Build API** (`esbuild.build(opts)`) — the primary interface: reads `entryPoints`, [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- follows imports, writes to `outfile`/`outdir`. Supports `bundle`, plugins, watch/rebuild. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- Node-relevant options: [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`platform: 'node'`** — sets `format` to `cjs`, marks Node built-ins external, and [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- adds the `node` export condition. (`'browser'` → `iife`; `'neutral'` → `esm`.) [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`format`** — `'esm'` | `'cjs'` | `'iife'`. Override the platform default explicitly [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- for ESM output on Node (`.mjs` or `"type":"module"`). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`bundle: true`** — inline imported deps (off by default). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`external: ['pg', '*.node']`** and **`packages: 'external'`** — the latter marks [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- *all* dependencies external (the common server recipe: bundle your code, leave [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `node_modules` on disk). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`minify`**, **`treeShaking`** (on by default when bundling; honors `package.json` [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `sideEffects`), **`target: 'node20'`**, **`sourcemap`** (`true`/`'inline'`/`'external'`). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Hard limit — no type-checking.** esbuild strips types; per the docs, *"esbuild does [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- not do any type checking so you will still need to run `tsc --noEmit` in parallel."* [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- It also never emits `.d.ts`. Enable `isolatedModules` in `tsconfig.json` because each [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- file is compiled independently. It honors `experimentalDecorators` but **not** [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `emitDecoratorMetadata` (that needs the type system). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- TS/JS. `@swc/core` exposes `transform` / `transformSync` / `transformFile` (plus [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `minify` and `parse`); it is "mainly useful for build-tool authors." Configured by [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`.swcrc`** (or inline `jsc`): [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`jsc.parser.syntax`** = `"typescript"` | `"ecmascript"`, with `tsx`/`jsx` and [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]

- **`jsc.target`** (e.g. `"es2022"`), **`jsc.transform.legacyDecorator`** / [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`decoratorMetadata`** — the SWC equivalents that **do** support [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `emitDecoratorMetadata`, which is why **NestJS/TypeORM stacks favor swc** over esbuild. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`module.type`** = `"commonjs"` | `"es6"` | `"umd"` | `"amd"`; **`minify: true`**. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **swc vs esbuild:** both are far faster than Babel/`tsc` and both skip type-checking. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- esbuild is also a *bundler*; swc is primarily a *compiler/transform* (bundling via the [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- separate, less-used `@swc/pack`). Pick **swc** for decorator metadata or its ecosystem [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- (Next.js, Jest via `@swc/jest`); pick **esbuild** when you want one tool that also [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- bundles. The dev-time runtime loader `@swc-node/register` belongs to [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features`. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- TypeScript libraries," an **esbuild wrapper** that adds the two things esbuild lacks for [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- libraries: easy **dual-format output** and **`.d.ts` generation**. Zero-config defaults [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- plus `tsup.config.ts`: [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`entry`** (entry points), **`format: ['esm', 'cjs']`** (or `--format esm,cjs`) → [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]

- **`dts: true`** (or `--dts`) → generates a bundled `.d.ts` (delegates to the TS [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- compiler) — the feature that makes it a *library* tool, not just a transpiler. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`target`**, **`minify`**, **`sourcemap`**, **`splitting`** (code-splitting, ESM [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]

- Note: tsup's README now points to **`tsdown`** (a Rolldown-based successor) as the [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- recommended direction with a migration guide; tsup remains widely used and the patterns [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- here transfer. Use tsup (or tsdown) for a **publishable package**; for an *application* [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- you usually want a plain esbuild build or no bundle at all. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- such as a library or application," and it pioneered **tree-shaking** ("statically [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- analyzes the code you are importing, and will exclude anything that isn't actually [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- used" — "more effective than simply running an automated minifier"). Reach for Rollup [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- You want the **cleanest library bundle** — Rollup's output is famously readable and [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- flat, with the best tree-shaking; many published packages are built with it. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- You need **output formats** beyond esbuild's set: **`es`**, **`cjs`**, **`umd`**, [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]

- precise control. The trade-off is speed: Rollup is slower than esbuild/swc. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- (Rolldown — a Rust port of Rollup — and tsdown are the emerging fast successors.) [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- file, together with all its dependencies, gcc-style." Built on webpack under the hood, [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- it does static analysis to **relocate assets** and handles binary addons and dynamic [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- requires better than a naive bundle. The canonical use cases are exactly the [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- self-contained ones: **CLIs, GitHub Actions** (a committed `dist/index.js`), and [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- ncc build src/index.ts -o dist   # -m minify, -s source-map, -e <pkg> external, -w watch [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- It handles TypeScript natively. Choose ncc when the deliverable is *"one file, drop it [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- anywhere, no `node_modules`"*; choose esbuild/tsup when you want speed or library [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- formats and are willing to keep some deps external. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- Two production-correctness concerns that bite bundled/transpiled Node code: [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Source maps.** Generate them in the bundler (`sourcemap: true` / `--sourcemap` / [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `-s`), then run Node with **`--enable-source-maps`** (or `NODE_OPTIONS`) so traces [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- "report stack traces relative to the original source file." Caveat from the docs: it [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- "can introduce latency... when `Error.stack` is accessed" — fine for most servers, [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- note it for hot error paths. If you override `Error.prepareStackTrace`, call the [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- original to preserve mapping. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **TS path aliases (`compilerOptions.paths`) in bundles.** `tsc` rewrites nothing at [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- runtime, so `@app/*` aliases break unless the bundler resolves them. esbuild reads [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `paths` from `tsconfig.json` — **but only when `--bundle` is set** (in transpile-only [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- mode the alias survives into output and fails at runtime). For non-bundling builds use [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- esbuild's `alias` option, a plugin (`esbuild-plugin-tsconfig-paths`), or a runtime [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- resolver. Rollup uses `@rollup/plugin-alias` / `rollup-plugin-typescript-paths`. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `tsx` ("TypeScript Execute") runs `.ts` directly in Node, **powered by esbuild** as a [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- *transpiler, not a bundler*. It is a **dev/script runner** (watch mode, zero-config, [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- no installation via `npx tsx`) and, like esbuild, **does not type-check** — it lets you [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- run code without being blocked by type errors. The decision rule: **`tsx` (or Node's [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- native type-stripping) for development and one-off scripts; a real bundler/build step [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- for production.** Don't ship a server by running `tsx` in prod — produce a built [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- artifact and run plain `node`. (Deep runtime-loader internals → the runtime-features [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Server recipe (esbuild):** `bundle: true, platform: 'node', format: 'esm', [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- target: 'node20', packages: 'external', sourcemap: true` → one entry file, deps stay [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- in `node_modules`; run with `node --enable-source-maps dist/index.js`. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Lambda / single-file recipe:** drop `packages: 'external'` so deps are inlined (or [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- use `ncc build`), add `minify: true`, keep only true natives external. Smaller cold [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- start, self-contained zip. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Library recipe (tsup):** `entry: ['src/index.ts'], format: ['esm','cjs'], [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- dts: true, sourcemap: true, treeshake: true`, and wire `package.json` `exports` to [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- the emitted ESM/CJS/`.d.ts` (resolution details → `nodejs-module-resolution`). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Always pair a fast transpiler with a type gate** — esbuild/swc/tsx skip types, so [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- run `tsc --noEmit` (or `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --emitDeclarationOnly` for types) [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- in CI alongside the build. Speed for builds, `tsc` for correctness. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Set `isolatedModules: true`** in any project transpiled file-by-file (esbuild/swc/ [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- tsx/Babel) so you catch unsafe cross-file `type` re-exports at design time. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Bundling a normal long-lived server "for performance."** A containerized server [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- rarely benefits; you trade simpler stack traces and native-addon resolution for [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- little. Bundle for *packaging* (CLI/Lambda/Action) or *cold start*, not by reflex. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Trusting a fast transpiler to catch type errors.** esbuild/swc/tsx emit happily on [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- broken types. No `tsc --noEmit` in CI = type safety lost. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Shipping a bundle with no source maps**, or generating maps but forgetting [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `--enable-source-maps` — every prod stack trace points at minified output. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Inlining native addons / dynamic `require` targets.** Bundlers can't trace `.node` [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- files or runtime-computed paths; mark them `external` or the artifact crashes at load. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Expecting `tsconfig` `paths` to "just work."** They only resolve when the bundler [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- is told to (esbuild needs `--bundle`; otherwise add a plugin/alias) — easy silent [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in production. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Running `tsx`/`ts-node` as your production process.** Per-request transpile cost and [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- no build artifact; build once, run `node`. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` / "exports is not defined" at runtime** → format mismatch. The [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- bundle is ESM but loaded as CJS (or vice-versa); set `format` to match `package.json` [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `"type"` and the file extension (`.mjs`/`.cjs`). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Stack traces point at bundled/minified code** → you didn't run with [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `--enable-source-maps`, or the bundler didn't emit a map (`sourcemap: true`). [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **`Cannot find module '@app/...'`** → `tsconfig` `paths` weren't resolved at build; [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- enable `--bundle` (esbuild), add a paths plugin, or use `alias`. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- **Decorator metadata missing (DI fails in Nest/TypeORM)** → esbuild ignores [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
- `emitDecoratorMetadata`; switch that build to **swc** (`decoratorMetadata: true`) or `tsc`. [src: nodejs-build-tooling-bundlers]
