- function bound(_v: unknown, ctx: ClassMethodDecoratorContext) { [src: typescript-decorators]
- const name = ctx.name; [src: typescript-decorators]
- if (ctx.private) throw new Error("cannot bind private members"); [src: typescript-decorators]
- ctx.addInitializer(function (this: any) { this[name] = this[name].bind(this); }); [src: typescript-decorators]
- @double accessor copies = 3;   // -> instance sees 6 [src: typescript-decorators]
- greet() { console.log(`Hi, I'm ${this.#name}`); } [src: typescript-decorators]
- `accessor x = init` de-sugars to a private backing field plus a `get`/`set` pair on the prototype. It shipped in **TS 4.9** (alongside `satisfies`), deliberately ahead of decorators, so that a `kind:"accessor"` decorator has a uniform `{ get, set }` to wrap and an `init` hook to transform the initial value. Supports `static` and `private` modifiers. [src: typescript-decorators]
- class Person { accessor name: string = "Ada"; } [src: typescript-decorators]
- get name() { return this.#name; } [src: typescript-decorators]
- set name(v: string) { this.#name = v; } [src: typescript-decorators]
- A **factory** is a function returning a decorator — parameterize behavior: [src: typescript-decorators]
- function logged(prefix = "LOG:") {            // factory [src: typescript-decorators]
- return function (target: any, ctx: ClassMethodDecoratorContext) {  // the decorator [src: typescript-decorators]
- const name = String(ctx.name); [src: typescript-decorators]
- return function (this: any, ...args: any[]) { [src: typescript-decorators]
- console.log(`${prefix} ${name}`); [src: typescript-decorators]
- return target.call(this, ...args); [src: typescript-decorators]
- class C { @logged("⚠️") run() {} } [src: typescript-decorators]
- Two separate orderings — do not conflate them: [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Decorator *expressions* are evaluated top-to-bottom, left-to-right** (interspersed with computed property names), and the results stashed. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Decorators are *applied* bottom-to-top** on a single element. In `@bound @logged greet()`, `@logged` (innermost/closest to the method) wraps the original first; `@bound` wraps the result. So the *expression* `logged(...)` is evaluated before `bound`, but `logged`'s decorator runs against the raw method and `bound`'s against `logged`'s output. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **The class decorator runs LAST**, after all method and non-static field decorators have been applied (the new class isn't available until then). **Static field initializers run after** the class decorator. Placement around `export` is allowed on one side only: `@reg export default class {}` or `export default @reg class {}`, never both. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Stage 3 (TS 5.2+, `proposal-decorator-metadata`):** `context.metadata` is a plain object shared by **all** decorators on one class. Decorators write into it; after the class is defined it's exposed as `TheClass[Symbol.metadata]`. No external library, no type reflection — you record what you choose. [src: typescript-decorators]
- const serializables = new WeakMap<object, string[]>(); [src: typescript-decorators]
- function serialize(_t: any, ctx: ClassFieldDecoratorContext | ClassAccessorDecoratorContext) { [src: typescript-decorators]
- if (ctx.static || ctx.private || typeof ctx.name !== "string") [src: typescript-decorators]
- throw new Error("public string instance members only"); [src: typescript-decorators]
- let names = serializables.get(ctx.metadata); [src: typescript-decorators]
- if (!names) serializables.set(ctx.metadata, names = []); [src: typescript-decorators]
- names.push(ctx.name); [src: typescript-decorators]
- function jsonify(instance: object): string { [src: typescript-decorators]
- const meta = (instance.constructor as any)[Symbol.metadata]; [src: typescript-decorators]
- const names = meta && serializables.get(meta); [src: typescript-decorators]
- if (!names) throw new Error("nothing marked @serialize"); [src: typescript-decorators]
- return `{ ${names.map(k => `${JSON.stringify(k)}: ${JSON.stringify((instance as any)[k])}`).join(", ")} }`; [src: typescript-decorators]
- // Polyfill (most runtimes lack it): Symbol.metadata ??= Symbol("Symbol.metadata"); [src: typescript-decorators]
- // tsconfig: target <= es2022, lib includes "esnext" or "esnext.decorators". [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Legacy (`emitDecoratorMetadata` + `reflect-metadata`):** when both `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` are on, `tsc` **emits design-time type metadata** for *decorated* declarations, readable via `reflect-metadata`'s `Reflect.getMetadata`: [src: typescript-decorators]
- `design:type` — the type of a property/accessor. [src: typescript-decorators]
- `design:paramtypes` — the constructor/method parameter types (**the basis of DI auto-wiring**). [src: typescript-decorators]
- `design:returntype` — a method's return type. [src: typescript-decorators]
- This is what powers `@Injectable()`/constructor injection: the framework reads `design:paramtypes` to know what to inject. **Stage 3 has no equivalent** — it records no types and has no parameter decorators. [src: typescript-decorators]
- `target` = the prototype for instance members, the constructor for static members. [src: typescript-decorators]
- // LEGACY (requires "experimentalDecorators": true) [src: typescript-decorators]
- import "reflect-metadata"; [src: typescript-decorators]
- function sealed(constructor: Function) {            // class decorator [src: typescript-decorators]
- Object.seal(constructor); Object.seal(constructor.prototype); [src: typescript-decorators]
- function enumerable(value: boolean) {               // method-decorator factory [src: typescript-decorators]
- return (target: any, key: string, desc: PropertyDescriptor) => { desc.enumerable = value; }; [src: typescript-decorators]
- const requiredKey = Symbol("required"); [src: typescript-decorators]
- function required(target: Object, key: string | symbol, index: number) { // PARAMETER decorator (legacy-only) [src: typescript-decorators]
- const existing: number[] = Reflect.getOwnMetadata(requiredKey, target, key) || []; [src: typescript-decorators]
- existing.push(index); Reflect.defineMetadata(requiredKey, existing, target, key); [src: typescript-decorators]
- @enumerable(false) toString() { return "report"; } [src: typescript-decorators]
- print(@required verbose: boolean) {} [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Legacy evaluation order** (distinct from the standard rule in §5) — TS Handbook "Decorator Evaluation": [src: typescript-decorators]
- Parameter decorators, then Method/Accessor/Property decorators, for **each instance member**. [src: typescript-decorators]
- Parameter decorators, then Method/Accessor/Property decorators, for **each static member**. [src: typescript-decorators]
- Parameter decorators for the **constructor**. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Class decorators** for the class. [src: typescript-decorators]
- (Within one member, expressions evaluate top-to-bottom, functions are called bottom-to-top — same composition rule as standard.) [src: typescript-decorators]
- **TypeScript 5.0+** — standard decorators by default; `experimentalDecorators` for legacy. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **`reflect-metadata`** — runtime metadata store for the *legacy* `emitDecoratorMetadata` path; the foundation of DI auto-wiring. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Angular (16+), NestJS (10+), TypeORM (0.3+), class-validator, TypeGraphQL, MikroORM, routing-controllers** — all on **legacy** decorators + `emitDecoratorMetadata`. They rely on `design:paramtypes` (DI) and/or parameter decorators, neither of which exists in Stage 3. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **tsx / ts-node / swc / esbuild / Babel** — runners/transpilers that can emit either system's helper code (esbuild supports legacy decorators; standard support varies by tool/version). [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Pick a system per project.** New code with no DI-framework constraint → **standard** (no flag) — it's ECMAScript-aligned and library-free. Code on Angular/NestJS/TypeORM/class-validator → **stay legacy** (`experimentalDecorators` + `emitDecoratorMetadata` + `reflect-metadata`). [src: typescript-decorators]
- **For standard decorators**, write `(value, context)`, branch on `context.kind`, guard `static`/`private`, and return the correct shape per kind (esp. the field *initializer mutator* and the accessor `{get,set,init}` object). [src: typescript-decorators]
- **For metadata**, choose by system: Stage 3 `context.metadata`/`Symbol.metadata` (TS 5.2+, record-what-you-choose) vs legacy `reflect-metadata` + `design:*` (auto type reflection). [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Never mix systems** in one compilation; the flag flips global semantics. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Method wrapping (standard):** return a replacement fn from a `method` decorator; use a factory for parameters. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Auto-bind:** `addInitializer(function(){ this[name] = this[name].bind(this); })` in a `method` decorator — no body edit. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Field transform:** `field` decorator returns `(initial) => transformed`; `value` is `undefined`. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Mark-and-collect:** write member names into `context.metadata`; read via `instance.constructor[Symbol.metadata]` (Stage 3 serialization/validation). [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Legacy DI:** `@Injectable()` class decorator + constructor params whose types `tsc` emits as `design:paramtypes`; the container reads them with `reflect-metadata`. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Reusing a legacy decorator under the standard system (or vice versa).** Signatures differ (`target, propertyKey, descriptor` vs `value, context`); it throws or mis-types. Convert deliberately. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Expecting standard decorators to give you parameter metadata / DI.** No parameter decorators, no `design:paramtypes` in Stage 3. Don't try to port a NestJS/Angular DI app to standard decorators expecting injection to keep working. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Treating a `field` decorator's `value` as the field value.** It's `undefined`; transform via the returned `(initial) => …` mutator. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Decorating both `get` and `set` of a legacy accessor.** Apply to the first accessor in document order only — one `PropertyDescriptor` covers both. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Returning a legacy class-replacement constructor without preserving the prototype** — the runtime won't do it for you. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Assuming standard decorators run after Node's native type-strip.** Decorators aren't type-only syntax — legacy emits `__decorate` runtime helpers (needs `tsc`/`tsx`/swc/Babel); standard needs engine support V8 hasn't shipped. So `.ts` with decorators won't run under Node's strip-only path. (Deep mechanics → `nodejs-typescript-and-runtime-features.md`.) [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Enabling `emitDecoratorMetadata` without `experimentalDecorators`** — it's legacy-only and has no effect in the standard system. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Decorator "not callable" / wrong-arity errors after a TS 5.0 upgrade** → you removed `experimentalDecorators` and your decorators are legacy-shaped. Re-add the flag or rewrite to `(value, context)`. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **DI stops resolving / `Cannot resolve dependencies` in NestJS/Angular** → `experimentalDecorators` or `emitDecoratorMetadata` got turned off, or `import "reflect-metadata"` is missing from the entrypoint. Restore all three. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **`Symbol.metadata` is `undefined` at runtime** → missing polyfill (`Symbol.metadata ??= Symbol("Symbol.metadata")`) and/or `lib` lacks `esnext.decorators`; needs TS 5.2+ and `target` ≤ es2022. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **`context.metadata` is `undefined`** → TS < 5.2, or you're on the legacy system (legacy decorators have no `context`). [src: typescript-decorators]
- **A parameter decorator "doesn't exist" under standard decorators** → correct; Stage 3 has none. Keep that file on legacy or move the concern to a method/class decorator. [src: typescript-decorators]
- **Property decorator return ignored (legacy)** → by design; property decorators can only observe, not modify. Use a method/accessor decorator or `accessor` + standard. [src: typescript-decorators]
- TypeScript 5.0 — Decorators: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-0.html [src: typescript-decorators]
- TypeScript 5.2 — Decorator Metadata: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-2.html [src: typescript-decorators]
- TypeScript 4.9 — Auto-Accessors in Classes: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-9.html [src: typescript-decorators]
- TS Handbook — Decorators (legacy/experimentalDecorators): https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/decorators.html [src: typescript-decorators]
- TSConfig — emitDecoratorMetadata: https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/emitDecoratorMetadata.html [src: typescript-decorators]
- TC39 — proposal-decorators (Stage 3): https://github.com/tc39/proposal-decorators [src: typescript-decorators]
- TC39 — proposal-decorator-metadata: https://github.com/tc39/proposal-decorator-metadata [src: typescript-decorators]
- TypeORM #10869 (legacy→standard decorator migration discussion): https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/issues/10869 [src: typescript-decorators]
- <!-- Provenance: reference under the `lang-js-ts` hub. Mirrored from ~/.claude/skills/lang-js-ts/references/typescript-project-references-monorepo.md by scripts/persist-spoke.mjs. --> [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- A `lang-js-ts` reference for **splitting a TypeScript codebase into multiple referenced projects and building them as a graph** with `tsc --build`. The goal: structure a monorepo (or any multi-`tsconfig` repo) so each package type-checks against its dependencies' emitted `.d.ts`, builds in dependency order, skips up-to-date work, and gives editors cross-package "go to definition." Defer single-project `compilerOptions`/strictness, the module-resolution *algorithm*, package-manager workspace plumbing, and bundler/task-runner orchestration to the siblings in the SKIP line. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- A **project reference** lets one `tsconfig.json` declare that it depends on another via a `references` array. This does three things at once: it tells the editor and `tsc` to treat the referenced project as a **prebuilt unit** (consumers load its emitted `.d.ts`, not its source), it lets the **build mode** (`tsc -b`) order and cache compilations across the whole graph, and — with `declarationMap` — it keeps editor navigation jumping to the original `.ts` source across package boundaries. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- The feature has three moving parts: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`composite: true`** on every *referenced* project — the opt-in that makes a project safely consumable as a dependency (forces `.d.ts` emit, enables incremental info, fixes the input-file set). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`references: [{ path }]`** on every *consuming* project — the dependency edges. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`tsc -b` / `tsc --build`** — a build *orchestrator* (distinct from the single-project `tsc -p`) that walks those edges topologically and uses `.tsbuildinfo` to skip up-to-date projects. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Version anchors (these drive "is this available?" questions):** [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- > **`tsc -b` vs `tsc -p` in one line:** `tsc -p ./x` type-checks/emits **one** project and does *not* build its dependencies; `tsc -b ./x` finds the referenced projects, checks which are out of date, and **builds the out-of-date ones in dependency order first**. In a referenced setup you almost always want `-b`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- Setting `"composite": true` (default `false`, since TS 3.0) is mandatory on any project that appears in another project's `references`. The handbook is explicit: *"Referenced projects must have the new `composite` setting enabled."* Enabling it **forces several options**: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`declaration` is set to `true`.** A referenced project *must* emit `.d.ts` — consumers type-check against that output, never the source. This is the single load-bearing reason composite exists. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`incremental` is set to `true`**, so the project writes a `.tsbuildinfo` and participates in up-to-date checks. (Corollary: `tsc -b` is **inherently incremental** for composite projects — you do *not* add `--incremental`; that flag is for standalone non-composite builds.) [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`rootDir` default changes** to the directory containing `tsconfig.json` (rather than the inferred longest-common-path of the inputs). This is **not** a hard "you must set `rootDir`" requirement — but if your sources live under `src/`, set `"rootDir": "src"` explicitly so emitted paths mirror `src/**` into `outDir` cleanly instead of including the config dir. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **All input files must be covered by `include`/`files`.** *"All implementation files must be matched by an `include` pattern or listed in the `files` array. If this constraint is violated, `tsc` will inform you which files weren't specified."* A file pulled in only by an `import` but excluded from the glob is an error under composite (see Anti-Patterns: composite-requires-all-files). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- In a *consuming* project: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "compilerOptions": { "composite": true /* if this project is itself referenced */ }, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "references": [{ "path": "../core" }, { "path": "../utils" }] [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- Each `path` "can point to a directory containing a `tsconfig.json` file, or to the config file itself (which may have any name)" — e.g. `"../core"` or `"../core/tsconfig.build.json"`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- The edge changes resolution: *"Importing modules from a referenced project will instead load its output declaration file (`.d.ts`)."* So `import { x } from "@scope/core"` is type-checked against `../core/dist/*.d.ts`, not `../core/src`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- Edges must form a **DAG** — the dependency graph must be acyclic. `tsc -b` rejects cycles. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- A repo-root config that builds the whole graph but compiles nothing itself: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- { "path": "packages/core" }, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- { "path": "packages/utils" }, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- { "path": "packages/api" } [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- The handbook's exact guidance: *"have a 'solution' `tsconfig.json` file that simply has `references` to all of your leaf-node projects and sets `files` to an empty array (otherwise the solution file will cause double compilation of files)."* The empty array is legal: *"starting with 3.0, it is no longer an error to have an empty `files` array if you have at least one `reference`."* `tsc -b` (from the repo root) then builds every package in dependency order. List **all** leaf projects here, not just the top-level app, or unreferenced packages won't build. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- Without it, "go to definition" on a symbol from a referenced package lands in the generated `.d.ts`. With `"declarationMap": true` (emits `.d.ts.map`), *"you'll be able to use editor features like 'Go to Definition' and Rename to transparently navigate and edit code across project boundaries."* It is **not** forced by `composite` — it's the recommended optional companion for any package whose source you have locally. Pair it with `sourceMap` for runtime debugging. (Ship the `.d.ts.map` and the `.ts` source if you want consumers of a *published* package to navigate too.) [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- `tsc -b` *"will: find all referenced projects, detect if they are up-to-date, build out-of-date projects in the correct order."* It decides up-to-date-ness from each project's **`.tsbuildinfo`** file — written when `incremental`/`composite` is on, it stores *"information about the project graph from the last compilation"* so the next run can *"detect the least number of files to re-check and re-emit."* [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`tsBuildInfoFile`** controls where that file goes; the default name is `.tsbuildinfo`, *"stored alongside the output files."* Under `outDir: dist` you'll see `dist/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. Pin it (e.g. into a cache dir) when you want it out of the publishable output. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`noEmitOnError` is implied across the build:** *"`tsc -b` effectively acts as if `noEmitOnError` is enabled for all projects"* — otherwise a broken upstream dep would emit once, then be skipped as "up to date" and you'd never see the error again. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- Before 5.5, relative paths in an `extends` base resolved against the *base* file's location — so a shared `tsconfig.base.json` (especially one in `node_modules`) couldn't set a useful `outDir`/`rootDir`. `${configDir}` resolves to *"the directory that the tsconfig is contained in"* — i.e. the **extending** config's dir. This makes one base reusable across every package: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- // tsconfig.base.json (shared) [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "declarationMap": true, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "rootDir": "${configDir}/src", [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "outDir": "${configDir}/dist", [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "tsBuildInfoFile": "${configDir}/dist/.tsbuildinfo" [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- Each package's `tsconfig.json` does `"extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json"` and `outDir`/`rootDir` land relative to *that* package, not the base. Requires TS 5.5+. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`tsc -b` / `tsc --build`** — the build orchestrator. Accepts multiple config paths (`tsc -b src test`); *"don't worry about ordering the files… `tsc` will re-order them so that dependencies are always built first."* Build-mode flags: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- `--verbose` — log what's being built and why (combine with any flag). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- `--dry` — show what *would* build without building (combine with `--clean`). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- `--clean` — delete the outputs of the specified projects. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- `--force` — *"act as if all projects are out of date"* (ignore `.tsbuildinfo`). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- `--watch` / `-w` — watch mode (*"may not be combined with any flag except `--verbose`"*). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`disableReferencedProjectLoad`** — stop the editor eagerly loading the *entire* reference graph in a huge monorepo (load on demand instead). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`disableSolutionSearching`** — exclude a project from "find all references"/"go to definition" solution-wide searches when it's only there to be built. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`disableSourceOfProjectReferenceRedirect`** — make the editor read a referenced project's `.d.ts` output instead of redirecting into its source (rarely needed; helps perf when source is huge). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Workspace managers (pnpm/npm/yarn)** — provide the *runtime* symlink so `@scope/core` resolves to the sibling package; project references provide the *build ordering and types*. The two are orthogonal — see Methodology. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Mark every leaf package `composite: true`** (via a shared `${configDir}` base) so each emits `.d.ts` + `.tsbuildinfo`. Add `declarationMap` for in-repo navigation. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Add `references` edges** from each consumer to its direct dependencies (point `path` at the dependency's dir/config). Keep the graph acyclic. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Create a solution root** with `files: []` + `references` to *all* leaf packages. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Build with `tsc -b` from the root** (`tsc -b --watch` in dev). Never `tsc -p` a referenced project expecting its deps to build. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **In a workspace monorepo, layer the two systems:** let the package manager's symlinks resolve package names at runtime; use `references` for build order + types. **Prefer this over `paths`** — `paths` are type-only and don't create build edges (next point). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Use `paths` only as a fallback** when you can't rely on workspace symlinks, and remember a bundler/`tsc-alias`/package `imports` must make them work at runtime. Set them in the shared base with `${configDir}`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Verify** with `tsc -b --dry --verbose` (what would build, in what order) and `tsc -b --force` to rule out a stale `.tsbuildinfo`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Referenced (leaf) package — `packages/core/tsconfig.json`:** [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json", [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "declarationMap": true, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "include": ["src/**/*"] [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Consuming package that depends on it — `packages/api/tsconfig.json`:** [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json", [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "include": ["src/**/*"], [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- "references": [{ "path": "../core" }, { "path": "../utils" }] [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Solution root — `tsconfig.json` (builds the whole graph, compiles nothing itself):** [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- { "path": "packages/utils" }, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- { "path": "packages/core" }, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- { "path": "packages/api" } [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`tsc -b` invocations:** [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b                       # build the solution in ./tsconfig.json (whole graph, in order) [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b --verbose             # ...and explain which projects build and why [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b --watch               # incremental rebuild on change (dev loop) [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b --dry --verbose       # preview the build plan without writing anything [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b --clean               # delete all emitted outputs (.js/.d.ts/.tsbuildinfo) [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b --force               # ignore .tsbuildinfo; rebuild everything [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- tsc -b packages/api          # build just api + its (out-of-date) dependencies [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Workspace + references together (the recommended monorepo shape):** [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- // package.json (pnpm/npm/yarn workspace) gives RUNTIME resolution: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- //   "@scope/api" → symlink to packages/api [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- // tsconfig references give BUILD ORDER + TYPES. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- // In packages/api/src/index.ts: [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- import { thing } from "@scope/core"; // resolves via workspace symlink at runtime, [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- // and is type-checked via the ../core reference's .d.ts [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Using `tsc -p` (or bare `tsc`) on a referenced project.** It won't build dependencies; you'll get stale or missing `.d.ts`. Use `tsc -b`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`paths` instead of `references` for cross-package imports.** `paths` are **type-only** and create **no build edge** — `tsc -b` won't build a sibling just because a `paths` entry points at it, and the emitted JS has unresolved bare specifiers without a bundler/`tsc-alias`/package `imports`. Use workspace symlinks + `references`; reserve `paths` for fallback resolution. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Forgetting `composite` on a referenced project.** Error: the referenced project must be composite. Add `composite: true` (which also forces `declaration`). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`include`/`files` that miss an imported file under composite** (composite-requires-all-files). A file reached only by `import` but outside the glob errors — widen `include` or add it to `files`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Omitting `files: []` in the solution root.** The root then compiles its own inputs *and* builds the references → double compilation. Keep it empty. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Circular references.** The graph must be a DAG; break the cycle (extract shared types into a third leaf package). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Expecting "go to definition" to reach source without `declarationMap`.** It lands in `.d.ts`. Enable `declarationMap` on the referenced package. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`prepend: true` / `outFile` bundling.** Legacy concat-output project references — deprecated since 5.0, no effect from 5.5, and an **error in 6.0**. Don't adopt them; use a real bundler for single-file output. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **A stale `.tsbuildinfo` masking changes** (e.g. after a git operation that rewrites mtimes). Symptom: "nothing to build" when there clearly is. Fix: `tsc -b --force` (or `--clean` then rebuild). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`tsc -b` over a huge graph in the editor feeling slow.** Reach for `disableReferencedProjectLoad` (lazy graph load) and `disableSolutionSearching` rather than collapsing packages back into one. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **"Referenced project '…' must have setting `composite: true`"** → add `composite: true` to that project's `tsconfig.json`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **"Output file '…/x.d.ts' has not been built from source file '…/x.ts'"** → a downstream project references an upstream one whose outputs are stale/missing; build with `tsc -b` (which orders deps) instead of `tsc -p`, or run `tsc -b --force`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **"File '…' is not listed within the file list of project '…'. Projects must list all files or use an `include` pattern."** → composite-requires-all-files; widen `include` or add to `files`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **"Cannot find module '@scope/core' or its type declarations"** → the `references` edge is missing *or* the referenced project hasn't emitted `.d.ts` yet; add the edge and run `tsc -b`. Runtime resolution is a separate concern (workspace symlink / `paths` + bundler). [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **`tsc -b` says everything is up to date but it isn't** → stale `.tsbuildinfo`; `tsc -b --force` or delete the `.tsbuildinfo`. Confirm the plan with `tsc -b --dry --verbose`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Go-to-definition lands in `.d.ts`, not `.ts`** → enable `declarationMap` on the referenced package and rebuild. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Editor slow / high memory in a large monorepo** → `disableReferencedProjectLoad: true` (load referenced projects lazily); consider `disableSolutionSearching` on build-only projects. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Shared base's `outDir` resolves to the wrong (base) directory** → you're on TS < 5.5 or didn't use `${configDir}`; upgrade to 5.5+ and wrap paths as `"${configDir}/dist"`. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- **Deprecation error on `prepend`/`out` after upgrading toward 6.0** → remove them; they no longer function and error in 6.0. [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- TypeScript Handbook — Project References (composite, references, solution config, declarationMap, build mode): https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/project-references.html [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- TypeScript — TSConfig Reference (`composite`, `incremental`, `tsBuildInfoFile`, `declarationMap`, `disableReferencedProjectLoad`, `disableSolutionSearching`): https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/ [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- TypeScript 5.5 release notes (`${configDir}` template variable): https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-5-5/ [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- TypeScript 5.0 release notes (deprecation of `prepend`/`out`): https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-0.html [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]

- Total TypeScript — TSConfig Cheat Sheet (monorepo/project-references baselines): https://www.totaltypescript.com/tsconfig-cheat-sheet [src: typescript-project-references-monorepo]
- <!-- Provenance: reference under the `lang-js-ts` hub. Mirrored from ~/.claude/skills/lang-js-ts/references/typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo.md by scripts/persist-spoke.mjs. --> [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- A `lang-js-ts` reference for **why `tsc` and the editor get slow, how to measure and fix it, and what the Go-based native port (TypeScript 7 / "Corsa" / `tsgo`) changes**. Three jobs: (1) instrument a slow type-check and read the numbers, (2) apply the build-level levers that cut type-check and editor latency, (3) understand the native-port preview accurately — version-precise, honest about preview status, no fabricated feature claims. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- Scope boundary up front: this skill tells you **where the type cost is and how to reduce it at the build/config level**. It is *not* a tutorial on writing conditional/mapped/template-literal types — when the fix is to refactor the type operator itself, that's `typescript-advanced-types`. General `compilerOptions` reference is `typescript-compiler-config`; the programmatic compiler/transformer/LS-plugin API is `typescript-compiler-api`; bundler/transpiler throughput (esbuild/swc/Vite) is the `*-build-tooling-bundlers` siblings. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- Type-checking cost is dominated by **how many types the checker has to create and compare**, not by lines of code. A handful of recursive conditional types, a 200-member union, or an unannotated export that forces whole-program inference can cost more than thousands of plain statements. The editor (tsserver) runs the same checker, so a slow `tsc --noEmit` and a laggy "go to definition" share a root cause. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- The workflow is always: **measure first** (`--extendedDiagnostics`, then `--generateTrace` if you need a per-construct breakdown) → **find the hot spot** (the file/type that dominates `Instantiations` or `checkTime`) → **apply the cheapest lever that moves it** (annotate a return type, cap a union, split into project references, `skipLibCheck`). Guessing at fixes without a trace wastes effort on cold paths. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- Separately, Microsoft is rewriting the entire compiler + language service in **Go** ("Project Corsa", shipping as **TypeScript 7**). It is in **public nightly preview** as `@typescript/native-preview` (binary `tsgo`) and reports ~10× faster type-checking and ~8× faster editor load on Microsoft's own benchmarks. It is **not yet feature-complete** and **drops the existing programmatic API** — details and current flux are in the "Native Go port" section. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- `tsc --extendedDiagnostics --noEmit` prints the timing + size breakdown. Run it first; it's cheap and tells you whether you have a *type-system* problem or an *I/O/program-graph* problem. The numbers that matter: [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- Heuristic: **high Check time + high Instantiations → a type problem** (go to a trace, fix the types). **High Program time with low Check time → a file-graph problem** (tighten `include`/`exclude`, add project references, `skipLibCheck`). `--diagnostics` is the shorter legacy subset of the same output. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- When `--extendedDiagnostics` says "types are expensive" but not *which*, capture an event trace: [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- tsc --noEmit --generateTrace ./trace-out [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- This emits **`trace.json`** (a Chrome-tracing/`about:tracing` event stream — `checkSourceFile`, `checkExpression`, `checkVariableDeclaration`, `structuredTypeRelatedTo` spans) and **`types.json`** (the types referenced by the trace). View `trace.json` in **[ui.perfetto.dev](https://ui.perfetto.dev)**, `chrome://tracing`, or `edge://tracing`. Wide bars = the files/checks eating the time; click a span to see the source position. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- For an automated readout, run the official analyzer: [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- npx @typescript/analyze-trace ./trace-out          # ranks hot spots [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- npx @typescript/analyze-trace ./trace-out --forceMillis 200   # lower the report threshold [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- `analyze-trace` prints the slow files and the specific expensive types (with `types.json` IDs) so you don't have to read the raw trace by hand. This is *diagnosis* — the **fix** (rewriting a conditional type, capping a union) belongs to `typescript-advanced-types`; this skill just gets you to the offending construct and applies the build-level mitigations below. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- These reduce the work the checker does. Keep them **diagnostic/build-level**; the deep "how to author the type" treatment is `typescript-advanced-types`. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Add explicit return-type annotations on exported functions.** Without them the checker must *infer* the return type — often the largest source of Instantiations in a hot file. Annotating cuts the inference and improves editor responsiveness. (This is also what `isolatedDeclarations` enforces.) [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Prefer `interface extends` over large intersection (`&`) types.** Interfaces are cached and compared by reference; a big intersection is recomputed structurally on every comparison. Same shape, far cheaper. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Cap union size.** Unions with many members (≈10+, and pathologically 100s) cost quadratically in assignability and *distribute* across conditional types. Replace giant unions with a base type + discriminant where possible. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Avoid recursive/deeply-nested conditional & template-literal blowups.** A single recursive conditional or a template-literal type over a large union can generate millions of instantiations. Find it via the trace; the *rewrite* is `typescript-advanced-types`' job. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`import type` / type-only imports.** Make value-vs-type imports explicit (`import type { T }`) so the type graph and the runtime graph stay separate; pairs with `verbatimModuleSyntax`/`isolatedModules` and avoids dragging value modules into type-only paths. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- The dominant modern build splits the two jobs `tsc` historically did: [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **A fast single-file transpiler emits JS** — `esbuild` / `swc` / Vite / Node's native type-stripping. Milliseconds, no type-checking. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsc --noEmit` is the type-checker gate** — run in CI and in the editor, produces no files. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- This is faster because emit no longer waits on the checker, and it parallelizes. It **requires** `isolatedModules: true` (and `verbatimModuleSyntax`/`erasableSyntaxOnly` for the native-Node path) so the per-file transpiler can't mis-handle constructs that need whole-program info (`const enum`, type-only re-exports, parameter properties). *The transpiler/bundler config itself → the `*-build-tooling-bundlers` siblings; the tsconfig flags → `typescript-compiler-config`.* [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **What it is.** A from-scratch **port of the TypeScript compiler *and* language service to Go** — codename **"Corsa"** (the existing JavaScript-based compiler is **"Strada"**). It ships as **TypeScript 7**. Staging repo: **`microsoft/typescript-go`**. Go was chosen for native compilation plus **shared-memory parallelism / concurrency** (the checker fans work across cores), which the single-threaded JS implementation can't do. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **The speed claim (Microsoft's own benchmarks — not a universal guarantee).** ~**10×** faster type-checking on real projects: VS Code (~1.5M LOC) 77.8s → 7.5s (**10.4×**), Playwright 11.1s → 1.1s (**10.1×**), TypeORM 17.5s → 1.3s (**13.5×**). Editor **project-load** ~9.6s → ~1.2s (**~8×**). Peak **memory ~half** of the JS implementation. Treat as "order-of-magnitude on large codebases," verify on your own repo. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Status (as of the December 2025 "Progress on TypeScript 7" post — currency-sensitive, confirm before quoting).** Stable enough to try daily; **not yet at full parity**. What now **works**: command-line type-checking at high compatibility (in a 6,000-error test corpus, only ~74 cases diverge); JSX checking; JS-via-JSDoc checking; **`--incremental` + `.tsbuildinfo`**; **project references**; **`--build` (`tsc -b`)**; **parallel multi-project compilation**; a real **LSP language service** in the editor (completions + auto-imports, go-to-definition/implementation/type-definition, find-all-references, rename, hover, signature help, formatting, code lens, call hierarchy). *(Note: the earlier May-2025 announcement listed no project refs / no `--build` / no declaration emit — that is **superseded**; the Dec-2025 state above is current.)* [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Still in flux — flag these explicitly:** [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **JS emit pipeline is incomplete.** Downlevel emit "realistically only goes as far back as the **`es2021`** target," and there is **no decorator emit** yet. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`--watch`** exists but "may be less-efficient than the existing TypeScript compiler in some scenarios." [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **The Strada compiler API is gone.** "Corsa / TypeScript 7.0 will not support the existing Strada API." This breaks **custom transformers, programmatic `ts.*` consumers, and language-service plugins**. "The Corsa API is still a work in progress, and no stable tooling integration exists for it." (Tools like ts-loader, ESLint type-aware rules, ts-jest, API-extractor must wait for / migrate to the new API.) *The Strada API surface itself → `typescript-compiler-api`.* [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **JSDoc was rewritten** with reduced backward compatibility (dropped `@enum`/`@constructor` recognition, stricter `Object` handling) — JS-heavy codebases may see new errors. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Versioning & how to try it.** Published as **nightly `7.0.0-dev.*`** builds on npm under **`@typescript/native-preview`** (a moving dev tag — don't pin one nightly as "the version"). Binary is **`tsgo`**, a drop-in for `tsc`: [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- npm i -D @typescript/native-preview [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- npx tsgo --noEmit -p ./tsconfig.json   # use like tsc [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Editor:** install the **"TypeScript (Native Preview)"** extension (`TypeScriptTeam.native-preview`), then run the command-palette action **"TypeScript Native Preview: Enable (Experimental)"** (equivalently the `typescript.experimental.useTsgo` setting). It swaps the editor's language service to the `tsgo` LSP. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Release line.** **TypeScript 6.0 (March 2026) is the last JavaScript-based release** (no 6.1 planned); 6.x carries deprecations that pre-align with the native codebase. **TS 7.0 is the native compiler** and ships when parity is reached (no firm public date in the Dec-2025 post). *(Version anchors here match the `typescript-compiler-config` skill — keep them in sync.)* [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsc --extendedDiagnostics` / `--diagnostics`** — the first-look timing + size report (Instantiations, Types, Check/Program time, Memory). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsc --generateTrace <dir>`** — emit `trace.json` + `types.json` for Perfetto / `chrome://tracing` / `edge://tracing`. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`@typescript/analyze-trace`** — `npx @typescript/analyze-trace <dir>` (`--forceMillis N`) ranks the hot files/types automatically. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsc --explainFiles` / `--listFilesOnly`** — *why* is this file in the program? (catches an over-broad `include` inflating Program time). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsc -b --verbose` / `--dry`** — see what project references actually rebuild. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`@typescript/native-preview` (`tsgo`)** — the native-port nightly; benchmark it against your `tsc` baseline. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **esbuild / swc / Vite / Node `--experimental-strip-types`** — the fast emitters paired with `tsc --noEmit` (config → the bundler siblings). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`@arethetypeswrong/cli`** — orthogonal but adjacent: validates a published package's `.d.ts`/`exports` (correctness, not speed). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Reproduce with a number, not a vibe.** `tsc --extendedDiagnostics --noEmit`. Record Instantiations, Check time, Program time, Memory. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Classify.** High Check time + high Instantiations → **type problem** (step 3). High Program time / low Check time → **file-graph problem** (jump to step 5). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Trace the type problem.** `tsc --noEmit --generateTrace ./trace-out`; run `analyze-trace` (or open `trace.json` in Perfetto) to name the offending file/type. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Fix at the cheapest level.** Annotate the exported return type; swap a big intersection for an `interface extends`; cap/​discriminate a giant union. If the fix is *inside* the type operator, hand off to `typescript-advanced-types`. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Fix the file-graph / build.** `skipLibCheck: true`; tighten `include`/`exclude`; add `incremental`; split into **project references** for parallel/partial builds; consider `assumeChangesOnlyAffectDirectDependencies` for watch. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Decouple emit from checking** if not already: fast transpiler emits JS, `tsc --noEmit` is the gate (`isolatedModules: true`). Add `isolatedDeclarations: true` if you publish `.d.ts` and want parallel declaration emit. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Re-measure.** Confirm Instantiations/Check time actually dropped — don't trust the fix without the second `--extendedDiagnostics`. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Consider `tsgo` for the worst cases.** For a large slow repo, benchmark `npx tsgo --noEmit` against your `tsc` baseline — but **only as a non-authoritative second checker** until TS 7 is stable, and verify your emit target/decorators and any compiler-API tooling aren't on the unsupported list. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Measure, then trace, then auto-analyze:** [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- tsc --noEmit --extendedDiagnostics [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- tsc --noEmit --generateTrace ./trace-out [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- npx @typescript/analyze-trace ./trace-out --forceMillis 200 [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Fast-build config (transpiler emits, `tsc` gates):** [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- "skipLibCheck": true, [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- "isolatedModules": true, [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- "verbatimModuleSyntax": true, [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- "module": "preserve", [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- (esbuild/swc/Vite does the JS emit; this `tsconfig` is the type-gate only. Flag reference → `typescript-compiler-config`.) [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Library with parallel declaration emit:** [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- "isolatedDeclarations": true, [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- "skipLibCheck": true, [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- (Annotate every exported return type; a downstream tool or `transpileDeclaration` can now emit `.d.ts` per file in parallel.) [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]

- npm i -D @typescript/native-preview [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]

- **Optimizing without a trace.** Refactoring types you *guess* are slow. Always let `--extendedDiagnostics` → `--generateTrace`/`analyze-trace` name the hot spot first. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Treating `skipLibCheck` as the whole answer.** It's the biggest easy win but can hide real `@types` conflicts; pair it with a periodic full check, and don't use it to silence a genuine error. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Unannotated exported return types in hot modules.** Forces whole-program inference and inflates Instantiations; it also blocks `isolatedDeclarations` and slows the editor. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Giant unions / unconstrained recursive conditionals as a "clever" API.** They blow up Instantiations quadratically and distribute through conditionals. (Rewrite belongs to `typescript-advanced-types`, but *spotting the cost* is here.) [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **One monolithic project for a huge monorepo.** No parallelism, full re-checks, slow editor load. Split into project references. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Assuming `tsgo` is a finished drop-in.** As of Dec-2025 it has **incomplete emit (downlevel only ~es2021, no decorators)**, a **less-efficient `--watch`**, and **no Strada API** — so transformers, type-aware ESLint, ts-loader, ts-jest, API-extractor and similar tooling may not run against it yet. Use it as a fast second checker, not your authoritative emit/CI gate, until TS 7 is stable. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Pinning a specific `7.0.0-dev.*` nightly as "the TS 7 version."** It's a moving tag; describe the channel (`@typescript/native-preview`, `tsgo`) instead. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Quoting the old May-2025 announcement's limitations as current.** Project references, `tsc -b`, incremental, and the LSP all work as of the Dec-2025 progress post — cite the dated status. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsc --noEmit` takes minutes** → `--extendedDiagnostics`; if Check time + Instantiations dominate, trace it; if Program time dominates, tighten `include`/`exclude` and add `skipLibCheck`. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Editor "loading…"/laggy IntelliSense but `tsc` is okay** → tsserver loads the whole project; split into project references, add return-type annotations, and/or try the `tsgo` Native Preview language service. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Instantiations in the millions** → a recursive conditional or large distributed union; find it with `analyze-trace`, then refactor (→ `typescript-advanced-types`). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`analyze-trace` reports nothing useful** → lower `--forceMillis`, or open `trace.json` directly in Perfetto and look for the widest `checkSourceFile`/`structuredTypeRelatedTo` bars. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **Incremental build re-checks everything** → ensure `incremental`/`composite` is on and `.tsbuildinfo` isn't being deleted between runs; for watch, try `assumeChangesOnlyAffectDirectDependencies` (accept the soundness trade). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`isolatedDeclarations` errors flood in** → exported symbols lack explicit type annotations; annotate the public return/value types (that's the contract that enables fast DTS). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **`tsgo` emits nothing / wrong JS for old targets or decorators** → expected; the native emit pipeline only downlevels to ~`es2021` and doesn't emit decorators yet — keep `tsc`/esbuild for emit and use `tsgo` for checking. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **A transformer / type-aware lint rule / build plugin breaks under TS 7** → the Strada compiler API is dropped and the Corsa API is still WIP with no stable integration; stay on TS 6.x/`tsc` for that tooling until it migrates (→ `typescript-compiler-api`). [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]
- **New type/JSDoc errors only under `tsgo`** → JSDoc was rewritten with reduced compat (`@enum`/`@constructor` dropped, stricter `Object`); reconcile against the TS 7 notes before assuming a bug. [src: typescript-compiler-performance-tsgo]

- A `lang-js-ts` reference for **linting TypeScript with `typescript-eslint` v8**: stand up an [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `eslint.config.js` flat config, turn on *type-aware* (typed) linting via [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `parserOptions.projectService`, pick the right shared config, and know which high-value rules need [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- type information versus which are purely syntactic. The goal: a correct, version-appropriate ESLint [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- setup the first time, with the typed-linting performance cost understood and scoped. Defer the [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- TypeScript compiler API / `parserServices` internals, general bundler/linter *choice*, `tsconfig` [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- strictness, and non-TS ESLint config to the siblings listed below. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `typescript-eslint` is the toolkit that lets ESLint understand TypeScript. Two packages do the work, [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- both re-exported from the umbrella **`typescript-eslint`** package: [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **`@typescript-eslint/parser`** — replaces ESLint's default (Espree) parser so ESLint can read TS [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- syntax (types, generics, decorators) into an AST. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **`@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin`** — the rules themselves (~100+), including the typed rules. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **Linting is not type-checking.** ESLint + typescript-eslint finds *bad practices and likely bugs* [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- (floating promises, unsafe `any`, dead conditions). It does **not** replace `tsc`: you still run [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `tsc --noEmit` as the type gate. The two are complementary — `tsc` proves the program type-checks; [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- typed linting enforces opinions the compiler doesn't (e.g. "you ignored this promise"). [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **Version anchor (memorize — these drive "is this available / how do I configure it" questions):** [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- > **Flat config only.** This reference uses `eslint.config.js`/`.mjs`. If you're on a legacy [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- > `.eslintrc`, migrate first — ESLint 9 made flat config the default and v8 of typescript-eslint [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- > documents it exclusively. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- typescript-eslint ships shared configs as **arrays of flat-config objects**. How you splice them in [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- depends on which helper you use, and the spread (`...`) is **load-bearing**: [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **`tseslint.config(...)`** — typescript-eslint's own helper. Takes config objects as positional [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- arguments, so array-valued configs **must be spread**: `...tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked`. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- Forgetting the spread passes an array where an object is expected → broken config. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **`defineConfig(...)`** from `eslint/config` (ESLint 9.x) — the newer, framework-native helper. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- It flattens arrays for you, so you do **not** spread: pass `tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked` [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- directly, either positionally or inside an `extends: [...]` array. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- Both are valid in v8. Lead with whichever your project already uses; the rules and `parserOptions` [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- are identical between them. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- "Typed linting" means rules can call into the TypeScript type checker (`parserServices` / [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `getTypeChecker()`) to reason about the *types* of expressions, not just their syntax. That's what [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- makes `no-floating-promises` (is this expression a `Promise`?) possible at all. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- To turn it on you (1) extend a `*TypeChecked` config and (2) tell the parser how to find type info via [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `parserOptions.projectService`: [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]

- it and the parser resolves tsconfigs relative to the CWD, a real "works on my machine" footgun. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- For files **outside** any tsconfig (root config files, scripts), `projectService` takes an options [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- object instead of `true`: [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- allowDefaultProject: ['*.js', '*.config.js'], // lint these out-of-project files WITH types [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- defaultProject: 'tsconfig.json', [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- tsconfigRootDir: import.meta.dirname, [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `allowDefaultProject` is a glob of out-of-project files to lint with type information — no extra [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- tsconfig or compiler options needed. (Mechanics of `parserServices`/the checker API itself → [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `typescript-compiler-api`.) [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- Extend a preset rather than enabling rules one by one. The **`*TypeChecked`** variants require typed [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- linting (`projectService`/`project`); the plain ones do not. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **Picking:** no type info → `recommended` (+ `stylistic`). Type info → `recommendedTypeChecked` [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- (+ `stylisticTypeChecked`). Reach for `strict*` only if a real share of the team is highly [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- TS-proficient and will tolerate the friction. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- These are the rules that *justify* paying the typed-linting cost. All but the last **require type [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `consistent-type-imports` is the exception worth calling out: it's purely about *import syntax*, so it [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- runs without type info. It pairs with TypeScript's `verbatimModuleSyntax` / `isolatedModules` to make [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- type-only imports explicit and prevent a single-file transpiler from emitting a broken value import. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- (The tsconfig flags themselves → `typescript-compiler-config`.) [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- Several core ESLint rules are wrong or redundant under TypeScript — the compiler already covers them, [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- or they false-positive on TS syntax. The classic is **`no-undef`**: TS already errors on undefined [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- identifiers, and `no-undef` flags valid TS (global types, ambient declarations). **You don't disable [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- these by hand** — `typescript-eslint`'s `recommended*` configs include `eslintRecommended`, which [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- turns off the core rules TS subsumes (`no-undef`, `no-dupe-class-members`, `no-redeclare`, etc.). [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- Likewise, prefer the typescript-eslint *extension rules* (e.g. `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`, [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `@typescript-eslint/no-shadow`) over the core versions, and disable the core one when you enable the [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- **`typescript-eslint` (umbrella package)** — install `eslint typescript typescript-eslint` (plus [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `@eslint/js` for `js.configs.recommended`). Exposes `tseslint.config`, `tseslint.parser`, [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
- `tseslint.plugin`, and `tseslint.configs.*`. [src: typescript-eslint-typed-linting]
