- Every defect below is one **DETECT → RATE → FIX** entry. In a critique, name the defect, point at the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- on-screen tell, assign a severity, and give the concrete fix. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Severity scale** (aligned with the `frontend-ui` critique passes — Blocker → High → Medium → Low → Nit): [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Blocker** — breaks reading, changes meaning, or destroys brand credibility in a hero/wordmark; ship-stopper. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **High** — clear readability/legibility loss or a glaring amateur tell in prominent type. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Medium** — noticeable quality/polish defect; readers feel it even if they can't name it. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Low** — refinement-tier; visible to a trained eye, minor cost. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Nit** — connoisseur's detail; fix if cheap. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Critique discipline:** micro-typography is the domain where dogma is most tempting and most often [src: micro-typography-craft]
- wrong. Most "rules" here are *guidelines with documented exceptions* — read [When NOT to flag](#when-not-to-flag-disconfirming-findings) [src: micro-typography-craft]
- before rating anything High. Calibrate severity to the artifact: a one-word widow is a Blocker in a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- printed annual report and a Nit in a responsive web paragraph. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Medium where shown** means "screenshot-detectable but context-dependent" — confirm intent before flagging. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > ⚠️ **The widow/orphan labels are not standardized — name the visual position, not the label.** The [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > *most common* convention (Butterick, MDN, Wikipedia, Adobe) is: **widow** = a short last line of a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > paragraph stranded alone at the **top** of the next column/page ("a past but no future"); **orphan** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > = the first line of a paragraph stranded alone at the **bottom** of a column/page ("a future but no [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > past").[^widoworphan][^mdnwidows][^mdnorphans] But reputable sources *reverse* this — Fontfabric [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > (2025) defines orphan=top, widow=bottom — and Wikipedia states outright there is "no consistent [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > standard."[^fontfabricorphan][^widoworphan] A *third* usage (most CSS/web docs) calls the **runt** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > (§1.3) an "orphan." **In a critique, describe the tell — "a one-word last line stranded at the top [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > of column 2" — rather than rely on "widow."**[^widoworphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A near-empty line (often one or two words) floating at the very top of a column/page, the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- bulk of its paragraph on the previous page; a white gap sits above it and the text "color" breaks.[^butterickwidow][^fontfabricorphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** for a single word/part-word at a page or column top (the most distracting case — [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Butterick: widows "are more distracting" because they can be as short as one word).[^butterickwidow] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Medium** for a fuller last line. **Blocker** only in premium/published collateral (books, annual [src: micro-typography-craft]
- reports) where it reads as an oversight.[^fontfabricorphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Print/word-processor: enable widow/orphan control — InDesign **Keep Options → "Keep Lines [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Together"**; Word **Paragraph → Line and Page Breaks → Widow/Orphan control**.[^butterickwidow][^fontfabricorphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Or copy-edit (add/cut a word to reflow). **Do NOT insert a hard line break / carriage return** to [src: micro-typography-craft]
- fix it — it becomes a layout landmine on reflow.[^butterickhardbreak] CSS (paged/multicol only): [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `widows: 2;` (see §1.5 for the support caveat). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A lone opening line at the foot of a column, the paragraph body continuing overleaf; the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- reader starts a thought then must jump.[^butterickwidow][^mdnorphans] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** typically (it's at least a full line, so less ragged than a one-word widow). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Rises to **High** in formal published layouts.[^butterickwidow] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Same Keep Options / `orphans: 2;` controls as §1.1.[^adobekeep][^mdnorphans] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A lone short word on a paragraph's final line, *anywhere* on the page — the paragraph [src: micro-typography-craft]
- gap below then looks mistakenly large. Distinct from a true widow because it isn't tied to a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- column/page break. (Print purists say *runt*; word processors and CSS docs call it *widow* OR [src: micro-typography-craft]
- *orphan*.)[^bookhouserunt][^widoworphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium** on the web (very common, low stakes; this is the web's version of the widow [src: micro-typography-craft]
- problem); **Medium** in print body. A one- or two-letter runt is the worst-looking. Butterick: [src: micro-typography-craft]
- browsers "are happy to put a small word alone on the last line of a paragraph, which always looks [src: micro-typography-craft]
- bad."[^butterickwidow] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Web (modern, preferred): `text-wrap: pretty;` on body text — pulls a word back so the last [src: micro-typography-craft]
- line has ≥2 words.[^chrometextwrap][^webkittextwrap][^mdntextwrap] Web (manual/legacy): a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- non-breaking space `&nbsp;` between the **last two words** so they wrap together; avoid `<br>` (breaks [src: micro-typography-craft]
- responsive layouts).[^butterticknbsp][^bootstrapwidow] Print: copy-edit, or subtle tracking on the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- preceding lines to absorb the word.[^fontfabricorphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A bold subhead sitting as the last thing in a column, its paragraph beginning elsewhere [src: micro-typography-craft]
- — the label is severed from the content it introduces, misleading scanning.[^smashingfrag][^mdnbreak] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** — arguably worse than a text widow because it breaks a structural label from its [src: micro-typography-craft]
- content; **Blocker** in print/PDF deliverables. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** CSS: `break-after: avoid;` on the heading and/or `break-inside: avoid;` on a wrapping [src: micro-typography-craft]
- container.[^mdnbreak] **Support caveat (verified-as-of 2026-06-16):** `break-after: avoid` is broadly [src: micro-typography-craft]
- available in Chromium (since ~Dec 2022) but still patchy in Safari/Firefox for some break values — [src: micro-typography-craft]
- verify in target engines.[^mdnbreak] Print: InDesign **Keep Options → "Keep with Next ___ Lines"**.[^adobekeep] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `orphans` = minimum lines kept at the **bottom** of a fragment before a break; `widows` = minimum [src: micro-typography-craft]
- lines kept at the **top** after a break. Both: initial value **2**, inherited, apply to block [src: micro-typography-craft]
- containers, take an `<integer>` ≥ 1.[^mdnwidows][^mdnorphans] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **They act ONLY in fragmented contexts** (paged media / print / PDF, multi-column `columns`, or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- regions) — they do **nothing** in ordinary continuous web flow, and do **not** fix a runt in a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- single-column flowing article. Butterick lists CSS widow/orphan control as "not applicable" to [src: micro-typography-craft]
- normal web pages.[^mdnfrag][^butterickwidow] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Browser support (verified-as-of 2026-06-16):** supported in Blink (Chrome) and WebKit (Safari); [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **not supported in Firefox** (long-standing open bug) — treat as progressive enhancement.[^caniusewidows] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Squint or step back. **Good rag** = a soft, gentle, irregular taper where successive line [src: micro-typography-craft]
- lengths vary in *small* increments. **Bad rag** = wild swings in line length (a "hard rag"), a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- zig-zag/staircase edge, a deep "bite" out of the margin, or accidental shapes/words forming down the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- right edge.[^goodpage][^myfontsrag][^webkittextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium** (aesthetic/readability, rarely blocking). **Medium** when the rag is so deep [src: micro-typography-craft]
- that line lengths vary wildly or accidental shapes appear. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Web: `text-wrap: pretty;` — WebKit's implementation improves rag by reducing line-length [src: micro-typography-craft]
- variation across the whole paragraph (Chromium's only touches the last ~4 lines — see §2.5).[^webkittextwrap][^chrometextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Print: InDesign **"Balance Ragged Lines"** (note: it is overridden by justification, Keep options, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- "No Break", and trailing spaces).[^adobebalance] Adjust **measure** (§5), tune hyphenation, or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- hand-insert `&nbsp;`/soft breaks.[^runragged] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Don't reflexively flag rag depth alone** (see [When NOT to flag](#when-not-to-flag-disconfirming-findings)): Bringhurst prefers a deeper "hard rag" over a tight rag bought with bad breaks/excess hyphenation.[^webtyporag] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Two, three, or more stacked hyphens down the right edge.[^runragged][^webkittextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** — adds cognitive load (the split word's halves sit far apart) and looks careless. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- The common rule is **no more than two consecutive hyphenated lines** (a ladder is typically 3+; some [src: micro-typography-craft]
- style guides flag 4+ — the threshold varies).[^runragged][^mlarivers] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** InDesign: "Limit Consecutive Hyphens to: 2". CSS: there is **no property to cap consecutive [src: micro-typography-craft]
- hyphens** (verified-as-of 2026-06-16) — widen the measure, use `hyphens: manual`, or go ragged. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `text-wrap: pretty` reduces trailing consecutive hyphens.[^webkittextwrap][^chrometextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Gaps of inter-word white space that coincidentally line up across several lines, forming [src: micro-typography-craft]
- a "river" of white. **Mostly afflict justified text and narrow measures** (and monospaced fonts), [src: micro-typography-craft]
- where word spaces are stretched.[^wikiriver][^opusriver][^creativepro_river] **The detection test:** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- turn the proof **upside down** and/or **squint to defocus** and/or view from 2–3 ft — rivers then [src: micro-typography-craft]
- stand out as light streaks against the even gray.[^wikiriver][^opusriver] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** in justified body; **Low** in ragged text (rivers are rare there). Confirm at [src: micro-typography-craft]
- print resolution — rivers invisible on screen can be obvious in print, and "long rivers are unlikely [src: micro-typography-craft]
- in ordinary text," so screen-only critics over- or under-call them.[^creativepro_river] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Switch from **justified to ragged-right** (removes the stretched spacing that causes rivers — [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Bringhurst's core recommendation); or widen the measure, tighten H&J word-spacing limits, add [src: micro-typography-craft]
- hyphenation, or hand-reflow.[^webtyporiver] CSS `text-wrap: pretty` does **NOT** yet fix rivers in [src: micro-typography-craft]
- any browser (WebKit: "We are not yet making adjustments to prevent rivers").[^webkittextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT (the tells & the rules):** a **person's name / title+name** split across lines ("Sgt." | [src: micro-typography-craft]
- "Rock"); a **number split from its unit/symbol** ("5" | "km", "$" | "10", "Fig." | "23"); a **one- or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- two-letter word stranded at a line end** (esp. after a preposition); a line ending on a dash or an [src: micro-typography-craft]
- opening parenthesis; a **phone number or URL** broken at an arbitrary point.[^butterticknbsp][^runragged] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** for a broken name or number+unit (changes parsing, looks unprofessional); [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Low–Nit** for a stranded short word; **High** if it creates genuine ambiguity (a split phone [src: micro-typography-craft]
- number/URL the reader must reassemble). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** A **non-breaking space `&nbsp;`** ("invisible glue") between name parts, number+unit, or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- abbreviation+reference (Word: Ctrl+Shift+Space; Pages: Opt+Space).[^butterticknbsp] **`<wbr>`** marks [src: micro-typography-craft]
- an allowed break point inside a long URL; **soft hyphen `&shy;`** marks a permitted hyphenation [src: micro-typography-craft]
- point.[^runragged][^mdntextwrap] InDesign **"No Break"** character style glues a phrase.[^adobebalance] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Do **NOT** use a hard line break — it breaks on reflow.[^butterickhardbreak] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **`text-wrap: balance`** — makes all lines of a *short* block (~≤10 lines) roughly equal length; for [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **headlines, captions, teasers**. Side effect: the block becomes narrower than its container. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Support: Chrome 114 / Firefox 121 / Safari 17.5; **Chromium balances only the first 4 lines**, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- WebKit balances all.[^webkittextwrap][^logrockettextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **`text-wrap: pretty`** — for **body text**, and **implementations differ sharply**: Chromium [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (Chrome 117+) re-evaluates only the **last ~4 lines** (focus: prevent short last lines / runts + [src: micro-typography-craft]
- trailing hyphens); WebKit (Safari TP, ~2025) evaluates the **whole paragraph** (prevents runts, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- improves rag, reduces hyphenation; not rivers).[^chrometextwrap][^webkittextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **`text-wrap: pretty` does NOT fix true (paged) widows/orphans** — it only handles the *last lines* [src: micro-typography-craft]
- of a paragraph (the runt). Use the `widows`/`orphans` properties for paged contexts.[^logrockettextwrap][^mdntextwrap] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > **Definitions (keep them precise in critique).** **Kerning** = adjusting the space between a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > *specific pair* of letters; most fonts ship hundreds–thousands of kern pairs baked in (the font's [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > GPOS `kern` feature).[^buttericckern][^wikikern] **Tracking / letter-spacing** = a *uniform* [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > adjustment across a whole run.[^butterickletterspace][^wikiletterspace] Kerning fixes individual [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > awkward pairs; tracking changes overall density. CSS `letter-spacing` = tracking; `font-kerning` / [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > GPOS `kern` = kerning. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Specific pairs show uneven gaps — overhang-prone pairs `T Y V W A` leave a conspicuous [src: micro-typography-craft]
- *hole* ("Va", "To", "LY", "We"), OR tight pairs collapse so `r`+`n` reads as `m` ("burn"→"bum"), [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `cl`→`d`. The classic tell is "**keming**" (the word "kerning" itself mis-kerned so "rn" looks like [src: micro-typography-craft]
- "m").[^explainkern][^wikikern] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Blocker** when mis-kerning changes the word (legible-but-wrong) or appears in a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **logo/wordmark/hero headline**. **High** for visible uneven gaps in any large display heading (the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- larger the type, the more the eye catches gaps). **Medium/Low** for minor body unevenness; **Nit** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- for a single slightly-loose pair.[^buttericckern][^sitepointtracking] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** First ensure pair-kerning is on: CSS `font-kerning: normal` (forces stored kern data; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `auto` may disable it at small sizes), or `font-feature-settings: "kern"`.[^mdnfontkerning][^cssfontkerning] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Cross-browser caveat: Safari/WebKit historically needed `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility` to [src: micro-typography-craft]
- kern; Firefox kerns automatically ≥20px — so a headline can look kerned in one browser, not [src: micro-typography-craft]
- another.[^clagnutmanual] For the specific bad pair in display/logo work, apply **manual** correction [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (wrap the pair in a span + negative `letter-spacing`, or fix the pair in the design tool / font [src: micro-typography-craft]
- GPOS).[^clagnutmanual] Note: any non-zero `letter-spacing` disables optional ligatures.[^mdnletterspacing] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Reality check: built-in kerning is fine for non-professionals; manual pair-kerning earns its keep [src: micro-typography-craft]
- mainly in logos and large display.[^buttericckern][^clagnutmanual] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A run of capitals or small caps where letters sit too close — caps are drawn to nest [src: micro-typography-craft]
- beside lowercase, so packed together they look dense/cramped and read slower.[^butterickallcaps][^butterickletterspace] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** for all-caps body/UI labels at small sizes (legibility + accessibility hit); [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Medium** for an all-caps display line; **Low/Nit** for a 2–3-letter acronym. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Add **5–12% letter-spacing to caps and small caps — but not to lowercase**: CSS [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `letter-spacing: 0.05em` to `0.12em` (em units so it scales). Bake it into the style: [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em`.[^butterickletterspace][^butterickallcaps] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A big headline (~30px+/display) where letter spaces look airy/loose, so the word fails [src: micro-typography-craft]
- to read as one tight unit. Default metrics are tuned for ~9–13pt body; at display size they read [src: micro-typography-craft]
- loose.[^butterickletterspace] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (polish/hierarchy); **High** only for a brand wordmark/hero where looseness [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Apply **"the larger the type, the tighter the tracking; the smaller, the looser."** Tighten [src: micro-typography-craft]
- display type with small **negative** `letter-spacing`, typically `-0.01em` to `-0.03em`.[^sitepointtracking][^figrtracking][^butterickletterspace] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (The system font on Apple platforms does this automatically per point size; static mockups and web [src: micro-typography-craft]
- type must do it by hand.[^applehig]) [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Body/UI text where letters touch or overlap, counters close up, words become a smear — [src: micro-typography-craft]
- an over-aggressive negative `letter-spacing`. MDN warns a large negative value makes words [src: micro-typography-craft]
- "unrecognizable."[^mdnletterspacing] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** (direct legibility loss) → **Blocker** if it makes words unrecognizable or causes [src: micro-typography-craft]
- overlap at small sizes / for low-vision users. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Return body `letter-spacing` toward `normal`/`0` (default body metrics need no extra [src: micro-typography-craft]
- spacing). Never use negative tracking to cram more text into a column.[^butterickletterspace] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Body text with extra space between *lowercase* letters — words look spread, the rhythm [src: micro-typography-craft]
- breaks, text reads as strings of individual letters instead of word-shapes.[^kevinletterspace][^mdnletterspacing] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (readability + amateur tell); **High** at small sizes or large blocks; **Nit** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- for one short tracked sub-label. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** **Don't letter-space lowercase body text** — the font's built-in spacing already accounts [src: micro-typography-craft]
- for its counters/ascenders/descenders. Set `letter-spacing: normal`. (Goudy's maxim: "anyone who [src: micro-typography-craft]
- would letter-space lowercase would steal sheep" — strong guidance, not absolute; tiny tracking can [src: micro-typography-craft]
- aid *very small* lowercase <9pt.)[^kevinletterspace][^butterickletterspace] Butterick's overboard [src: micro-typography-craft]
- test: "If the spaces between letters are large enough to fit more letters, you've gone overboard."[^butterickletterspace] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > **Leading vs line-height.** "Leading" originally = the lead strips between lines of metal type; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > CSS `line-height` is its digital equivalent — but it sets an invisible box *around* the line [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > (half-leading above and below), so it does not sit on the text baseline. That disconnect is the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > root cause of baseline-grid pain on the web (§4.5).[^googleleading][^damatoline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Lines crowd vertically; descenders of one line (g, y, p, j) touch/overlap the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- ascenders/caps below; the block looks dense and "clashes".[^fontfabricdesc] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Blocker/High** for multi-line body — direct legibility failure + accessibility [src: micro-typography-craft]
- regression. Apple: "If you need to display three or more lines of text, avoid tight leading even in [src: micro-typography-craft]
- areas where height is limited."[^applehig] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Raise **unitless** `line-height`. Body baseline ~**1.4–1.6** (Butterick's optimal band is [src: micro-typography-craft]
- 120–145% of point size; 110% is "too tight"). Use unitless values so children recompute against [src: micro-typography-craft]
- their own font-size. Bump toward the top for faces with long descenders or large x-height.[^fontfabricdesc][^pimplineheight][^buttericklinespacing][^unitlessline][^bringhurst] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Lines float so far apart the paragraph reads as separate horizontal stripes, not a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- cohesive block; the eye loses the line-to-line connection. Butterick: 170% is "too loose."[^buttericklinespacing] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (cohesion/aesthetics) → **High** if it breaks the perception of the paragraph as [src: micro-typography-craft]
- one block or balloons the layout. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Reduce `line-height` into the body band (~1.4–1.6 / 120–145%). Design near ~1.4–1.5 (not [src: micro-typography-craft]
- above) for body so the layout still survives a user bumping line-height to 1.5 (§4.6).[^buttericklinespacing][^pimplineheight] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A long-measure (wide) column set with the same tight line-height as a narrow column — [src: micro-typography-craft]
- the eye struggles to find the next line's start on the return sweep.[^pimplineheight][^bringhurst][^nnglegibility] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (worse the wider the column). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** **"Longer lines → more leading; shorter/display → less."** Nudge `line-height` up ~0.1–0.2 [src: micro-typography-craft]
- for wide columns; tighten for narrow cards/sidebars. (Bringhurst recommends more leading for longer [src: micro-typography-craft]
- measures; NN/g: maintain 1.4–1.6em, wider for longer lines.)[^pimplineheight][^bringhurst][^nnglegibility] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Adjacent text blocks use visibly different line-heights for no functional reason; the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- page rhythm looks jittery. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (consistency/polish); **Low/Nit** if subtle. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Drive all body-tier text from one tokenized `line-height` scale; reserve tighter values [src: micro-typography-craft]
- deliberately for headings/display (1.1–1.3). A common root cause is mixing unitless and unit'd [src: micro-typography-craft]
- line-heights so inheritance differs — standardize on **unitless**.[^unitlessline][^ultimateline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Spacing between elements (headings, paragraphs, images, UI rows) doesn't fall on a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- consistent increment; baselines of adjacent columns don't line up; margins/padding look arbitrary. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium** (refinement/"design QA" tier, *not* a usability blocker — and see the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- disconfirming note below before over-indexing). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Snap spacing and line-heights to a shared increment — Material uses **8dp** for layout and a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **4dp** baseline grid, with the rule that **line-height must be a multiple of the base unit** (e.g. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- 15px text → 24px line-height) even if font-size strays off-grid.[^materialgrid] On the web, set body [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `line-height` to an integer multiple of the base unit and make vertical margins multiples of it; or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- use baseline-trim tooling (`leading-trim`/`text-box-trim`, the "basekick" technique) to remove the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- half-leading offset so text actually sits on the grid.[^damatoline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Don't over-rate this** (see [When NOT to flag](#when-not-to-flag-disconfirming-findings)): "a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- baseline grid does not automatically create good vertical rhythm," and on the responsive web it [src: micro-typography-craft]
- often "has no meaning" — prioritize a *consistent spacing scale* (4/8px) over true baseline [src: micro-typography-craft]
- snapping.[^vanseobaseline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- WCAG **2.2** SC **1.4.12 Text Spacing** (AA): a user must be able to override to at least line-height [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **1.5×**, paragraph spacing **2×**, letter-spacing **0.12×**, word-spacing **0.16×** without loss of [src: micro-typography-craft]
- content/function. Critical framing: "Content is **not required to use** these values" — so in a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- critique, ~1.5 body line-height is a **robustness floor not to break**, not a styling mandate (though [src: micro-typography-craft]
- NN/g independently recommends ~1.5–2× for comfort).[^wcagtextspacing][^dequetextspacing][^nnglegibility] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > **The rule.** Bringhurst: "Anything from 45 to 75 characters is widely regarded as a satisfactory [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > length of line… The 66-character line… is widely regarded as ideal. For multiple-column work, a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > better average is 40 to 50 characters." Butterick gives a wider working band (~45–90 incl. spaces) [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > and stresses measuring in **characters per line, not inches** (point size changes chars-per-inch but [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > not chars-per-line). UX sources converge on **50–75 CPL, ~66 ideal**; **~30–50 CPL on mobile**; the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > ~80-char ceiling is anchored by WCAG SC 1.4.8 (80 chars max).[^buttericklinelength][^webtypomeasure][^baymardline][^uxpinline][^wcagvisualpres] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Body copy runs the full width of a wide container/desktop viewport — lines visibly exceed [src: micro-typography-craft]
- ~90 characters; the paragraph is a wide "slab" with no max-width gutter, text touching both edges on [src: micro-typography-craft]
- a 1440px+ screen. (Count ~2 alphabets ≈ 52 chars and confirm the line runs well past it.) Too-long [src: micro-typography-craft]
- lines hurt the **return sweep** — the eye loses its place finding the next line and may re-read or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- skip ("doubling").[^baymardline][^uxpinline][^webtypomeasure] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** (readability + engagement loss); **High/Blocker** for accessibility-sensitive [src: micro-typography-craft]
- content sites if it also trips WCAG 1.4.8's 80-char ceiling.[^baymardline][^wcagvisualpres] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Constrain measure with the `ch` unit (width of "0", scales with font-size): [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `max-width: 66ch;` (~Bringhurst ideal) or `60–75ch`, centered with `margin-inline: auto`. `ch` is [src: micro-typography-craft]
- approximate, so treat 66ch as a target band. For responsiveness: `width: min(66ch, 100%)` so it never [src: micro-typography-craft]
- overflows narrow screens. Em-based widths (`width: 33em`) are the classic elastic alternative. In [src: micro-typography-craft]
- design tools, set a column width sized to ~45–75 chars (40–50 for multi-column).[^csstricksmeasure][^webtypomeasure] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A skinny column holding only a few words per line (well under ~40–45 chars); choppy rag; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- in justified narrow columns, big gaps and stacked hyphens (overlaps §6). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (Low/Nit for short captions or intentional sidebars). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Widen toward 45–75ch (single column) / 40–50ch (multi-column). If it must stay narrow, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- prefer ragged-right over justified and enable hyphenation.[^webtypomeasure] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Note:** the 45–75/66 band is a strong *design convention*; the causal reading-speed story behind it [src: micro-typography-craft]
- is weaker than design advice implies (see [When NOT to flag](#when-not-to-flag-disconfirming-findings)). Flag out-of-band *extremes*, not every line ≠ 66. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > **What justification does:** to flush both edges, the engine *adds inter-word (and sometimes [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > inter-letter) space* to fill the measure; browsers essentially only stretch *word* spacing. Web [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > justification is weak because the browser engine is "rudimentary compared to a professional [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > page-layout program." InDesign does it well via the **Adobe Paragraph Composer** (default), which [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > evaluates *all lines of a paragraph together* (a Knuth-Plass-style whole-paragraph approach), [src: micro-typography-craft]
- > yielding even spacing and fewer hyphens than the Single-line Composer.[^butterickjustified][^maxwelljustify][^adobecompose] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Fully-justified body where some lines have conspicuously wide word gaps (a few long words [src: micro-typography-craft]
- stretched across the measure), gaps varying line-to-line — the classic justified-`<p>` look on the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- web. Often co-occurs with vertical **rivers** (§2.3).[^butterickjustified][^maxwelljustify][^adobecompose] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** on the web without hyphenation; **Medium** in print/InDesign where the composer + [src: micro-typography-craft]
- H&J settings can largely fix it. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX (web):** either switch to ragged-right (`text-align: left;`, Butterick's default [src: micro-typography-craft]
- recommendation) OR, if justification is required, **always pair it with hyphenation**: [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `text-align: justify; hyphens: auto;` **and set `lang`** on `<html lang="…">` (browsers only [src: micro-typography-craft]
- hyphenate when `lang` is present and a hyphenation dictionary exists). Widen the measure to reduce [src: micro-typography-craft]
- gap pressure.[^butterickjustified][^mdnhyphens] **FIX (InDesign):** use the Paragraph Composer, turn [src: micro-typography-craft]
- on Hyphenation, and tune the H&J/Justification spacing (word/letter/glyph min–desired–max) for the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- measure.[^adobecompose] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- See **§2.2** (consecutive lines ending in hyphens). CSS has no property to cap consecutive hyphens.[^runragged][^mlarivers] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** The final line/word of a paragraph is hyphenated, or a hyphen lands right before the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low / Nit.** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** InDesign Hyphenation: "Hyphenate Last Word: off", "Hyphenate Across Column: off", raise [src: micro-typography-craft]
- minimum word length / letters-before-and-after. CSS can't target this; use a manual `&shy;`/`&nbsp;` [src: micro-typography-craft]
- fix or accept it with ragged-right.[^adobecompose] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `hyphens` is Baseline "widely available" (since Sept 2023), but **dictionary- and `lang`-dependent** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (no dictionary → no hyphenation); historically Chrome required `lang` and lacked some dictionaries. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Always set `lang`.[^mdnhyphens] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **What it is:** punctuation (quotes, bullets, hyphens, periods, commas) pushed *out past the text [src: micro-typography-craft]
- edge into the margin* so the text edge looks *optically* straight. Because punctuation has less [src: micro-typography-craft]
- visual weight than letters, leaving it inside the measure creates a visual "hole"/indentation in the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- flush edge.[^wikihanging] InDesign's **Optical Margin Alignment** also hangs serifs and overhanging [src: micro-typography-craft]
- letter edges (T, Y, A), not just punctuation.[^creativepro_hang] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A pull-quote/blockquote/bulleted paragraph whose first line begins with an opening quote [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (" or ') — making that line look *pushed in / indented* relative to the lines below, so a flush left [src: micro-typography-craft]
- edge looks subtly ragged. Same tell on the right edge with trailing commas/periods in justified text. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low / Nit** (refinement, not functional); **Medium** only for a brand/editorial design [src: micro-typography-craft]
- where flush-edge polish is a stated goal. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX (print/InDesign):** Type ▸ Story ▸ **Optical Margin Alignment**; the font-size field controls [src: micro-typography-craft]
- overhang amount; use "Ignore Optical Margin" to exclude specific lists.[^creativepro_hang] **FIX [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (web):** `hanging-punctuation: first;` (and/or `last`/`force-end`/`allow-end`) — **BUT** (verified-as-of [src: micro-typography-craft]
- 2026-06-16) `hanging-punctuation` is **Safari-only** (not Chrome or Firefox; MDN marks it "Limited [src: micro-typography-craft]
- availability / not Baseline"). Treat it as *progressive enhancement only*; the robust cross-browser [src: micro-typography-craft]
- fallback is a negative `text-indent` (or negative margin) on the quoted element, optionally behind [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `@supports not (hanging-punctuation: first)`.[^mdnhanging][^caniusehanging][^coyierhanging] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **The choice:** **Metrics** kerning uses the kern-pair tables the *font designer* built in (best for [src: micro-typography-craft]
- text set in a single professional font; InDesign's default). **Optical** kerning *ignores* those [src: micro-typography-craft]
- tables and spaces letters by their *shapes* — useful when a font has few/no kern pairs, when mixing [src: micro-typography-craft]
- multiple typefaces in a word, or mixing sizes on a line. There's no universally "right" answer.[^adobekerntrack][^creativepro_metricvsoptical] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Display/headline text with visibly uneven letter gaps (a gappy "T o" or tight "AV"), or a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- mixed-typeface logotype with inconsistent spacing. (Deep kerning is §3 — keep this as the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- *setting-choice* lens.) [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low** (setting nuance) unless egregious in a logo/hero → **Medium**. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** In InDesign, keep **Metrics** for a single quality font; switch to **Optical** for [src: micro-typography-craft]
- poorly-kerned fonts, multi-font words, or mixed sizes. On the web there is no metric/optical toggle — [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-kerning` only turns *built-in* kerning on/off; it cannot synthesize optical kerning.[^adobekerntrack][^creativepro_metricvsoptical] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **The principle:** some variable fonts carry an **`opsz` (optical size)** axis with size-specific [src: micro-typography-craft]
- designs — **text/body** sizes have lower stroke contrast, more open spacing, taller x-height; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **display** sizes are more delicate, higher-contrast, finer-serifed. A single optical size scaled [src: micro-typography-craft]
- up/down ("faux") looks wrong.[^mdnopticalsizing][^googleopsz] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Large display headings that look too heavy/clumsy (a text cut blown up), or tiny body [src: micro-typography-craft]
- text that looks too thin/fragile (a display cut shrunk); a variable font whose headline and body [src: micro-typography-craft]
- don't show the expected contrast/spacing shift. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low / Nit** (subtle; most visible in editorial/brand work). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Let it auto-track: `font-optical-sizing: auto;` (enabled by default for fonts with an `opsz` [src: micro-typography-craft]
- axis; allowed values are only `auto` | `none`). For manual control, set [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-variation-settings: 'opsz' <n>` to match the rendered font-size. In design tools, pick the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- correct named optical size (Caption/Text/Display) or set the opsz slider to the point size. Support: [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-optical-sizing` is Baseline "widely available" (since March 2020); verify visually as some [src: micro-typography-craft]
- fonts/engines apply opsz imperfectly.[^mdnopticalsizing][^googleopsz] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- These are **highly screenshot-detectable** and among the most common amateur tells. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Vertical, symmetrical tick marks (`'` `"`) instead of the four directional curly glyphs [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (` ' ` ` ' ` ` " ` ` " `): opening and closing marks look identical rather than mirrored; or a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- subtler crime — a contraction/decade opening with an upward-pointing **opening** single quote where a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- downward apostrophe is required (`'70s`, `rock 'n' roll`).[^butterickquotes][^butterickapostrophe] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** (Butterick: straight quotes "should never, ever appear in your documents" — a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- primary professionalism tell). Apostrophe-direction error = High. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Opening single `&lsquo;` (' U+2018), closing single / apostrophe `&rsquo;` (' U+2019), [src: micro-typography-craft]
- opening double `&ldquo;` (" U+201C), closing double `&rdquo;` (" U+201D). The apostrophe is *always* [src: micro-typography-craft]
- the closing single quote (U+2019) and always points downward.[^butterickquotes][^butterickapostrophe] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Hard exception:** straight quotes/backticks in source code and some databases must stay literal [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (see [When NOT to flag](#when-not-to-flag-disconfirming-findings)). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Feet/inches or minutes/seconds set with **curly** quotes (`5'10"`, `8.5" × 14"` with [src: micro-typography-craft]
- comma-shaped marks). The reverse over-correction also occurs (a true apostrophe where a sloped prime [src: micro-typography-craft]
- is wanted).[^butterickfootinch] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (domain-dependent; conspicuous in specs, real-estate, recipes, dimensions). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Butterick's *reliable* default for feet/inches is **straight quotes** (`'` U+0027, `"` [src: micro-typography-craft]
- U+0022) because true primes are rare in pro fonts; the typographically pure glyphs are prime [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `&prime;` (′ U+2032) and double-prime `&Prime;` (″ U+2033), sloping northeast-to-southwest. Present [src: micro-typography-craft]
- both; don't hard-fail straight quotes on measurements.[^butterickfootinch] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** a **hyphen used as a sentence break** (a short `-`, often spaced, or `--`/`---` doing an [src: micro-typography-craft]
- em dash's job); a **hyphen in a numeric range** (`1880-1912`) where an en dash belongs; a **slash [src: micro-typography-craft]
- where an en dash is correct**; a **crushed em dash** jammed against neighbors with no air. Dash [src: micro-typography-craft]
- *length* relative to a cap N/H is visible in a screenshot, so this is very detectable.[^butterickdashes] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (High in editorial/publishing). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Hyphen `-` (U+002D) for compounds + line-break hyphenation. **En dash** `&ndash;` (– U+2013) [src: micro-typography-craft]
- for ranges ("to"/"through") and connections (Sarbanes–Oxley) — but "from" pairs with "to", not an en [src: micro-typography-craft]
- dash. **Em dash** `&mdash;` (— U+2014, ≈ width of a cap H; en dash ≈ half) for a parenthetical break [src: micro-typography-craft]
- "when a comma is too weak but a colon/semicolon/parentheses too strong."[^butterickdashes] **Spacing [src: micro-typography-craft]
- is style-dependent, not a fixed crime:** Chicago = unspaced em ("like this"); British = spaced en; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Butterick allows spaces on screen to avoid crushing. Flag *inconsistency*, not the choice.[^butterickdashes][^cmosdashes] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Small caps whose **vertical strokes are visibly too light/thin** relative to the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- surrounding full caps and lowercase — they look like shrunken full caps (too tall, too light, grayer/ [src: micro-typography-craft]
- spindlier). Real small caps have strokes thickened so weight matches the text.[^dfhsmallcaps] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (a connoisseur's tell, but a real type crime). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Use a font that *contains* true small caps and request OpenType `smcp`: [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-variant-caps: small-caps` (preferred) or `font-feature-settings: "smcp"`. **Caveat:** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-variant: small-caps` historically *synthesized* fake small caps when the font lacked `smcp`; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- the reliable approach is to pick a font with true small caps AND set `font-synthesis: small-caps [src: micro-typography-craft]
- none` to *expose* (not hide) a missing feature. Re-verify real-vs-synthesized against the current [src: micro-typography-craft]
- target engine.[^mdnfontvariantcaps][^mdnfontsynthesis][^krycchosmallcaps] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT (three tells):** **lining figures shouting in running text** — digits all at cap-height, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- standing out like small all-caps words amid lowercase ("look like SHOUTING"); **old-style figures in [src: micro-typography-craft]
- all-caps/UI** — lowercase-style digits with descenders sitting awkwardly next to capitals; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **misaligned number columns** — proportional figures where tabular are needed, so price/table columns [src: micro-typography-craft]
- don't align vertically.[^mdnfontvariantnumeric][^harrellfigures] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium** (Medium for the misaligned-column case in data tables; Low/Nit for [src: micro-typography-craft]
- figure-style mismatch in prose). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** `font-variant-numeric:` `oldstyle-nums` (`onum`) in running text; `lining-nums` (`lnum`) in [src: micro-typography-craft]
- all-caps + UI; `tabular-nums` (`tnum`) for columns that must align; `proportional-nums` (`pnum`) for [src: micro-typography-craft]
- flowing text. Combinable (e.g. `oldstyle-nums tabular-nums`). Requires a font that carries the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- figures. (Baseline "widely available" since Jan 2020.)[^mdnfontvariantnumeric] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** **Missing standard ligature** — in a serif/high-contrast face the **dot of the i collides [src: micro-typography-craft]
- with the hook/terminal of a preceding f** (or f crashes into l/second f) in "fi/fl/ffi/ffl," a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- visible overlap at large/display sizes; **over-use of discretionary ligatures** — ornate connected [src: micro-typography-craft]
- pairs (ct, st, swash Th) distracting in body text.[^myfontslig][^creativepro_lig][^batchelderlig] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low** (Nit at text sizes; Medium at large display sizes where the collision is glaring). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Enable common ligatures (default on) via `font-variant-ligatures: common-ligatures` [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (`liga`/`clig`); suppress discretionary with `no-discretionary-ligatures` (`dlig`); kill problem [src: micro-typography-craft]
- pairs with `none` or `font-feature-settings: "liga" 0`.[^mdnfontvariantligatures] **Special case:** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- ligatures in **programming/code fonts are a crime regardless** — a `=>` ligature shaped like ⇒ [src: micro-typography-craft]
- misrepresents the code; disable in code views.[^butterickliga] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT (highly detectable):** **faux italic** = mechanically slanted uprights (the roman 'a','f', [src: micro-typography-craft]
- 'g' are oblique but keep their upright structure — double-story 'a' stays double-story; no true [src: micro-typography-craft]
- cursive forms; skew ≈ 14°). **faux bold** = strokes look smeared / uniformly outlined ("outlined with [src: micro-typography-craft]
- a magic marker"), clogged counters — worst is a **double-bolded** glyph (an already-bold font [src: micro-typography-craft]
- re-emboldened). Inspector tell: Safari's web-inspector Font pane warns when bolds are [src: micro-typography-craft]
- synthesized.[^alistapartfaux][^clagnutfaux] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Root cause:** applying `font-weight: bold`/`font-style: italic` when that cut isn't loaded, OR an [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `@font-face` rule mislabeling a bold file as `font-weight: normal` (so the browser bolds the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- bold).[^alistapartfaux][^smashingfaux][^clagnutfaux] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** (one of the most common, most visible web type crimes). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Load the real weight/style files and label `@font-face` correctly (`font-weight: 700`, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-style: italic`) under one shared `font-family`. To *expose* the defect in critique, set [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-synthesis: none` (or granular `font-synthesis-weight: none` / `-style: none`) — the fake style [src: micro-typography-craft]
- then disappears, revealing the missing cut. (Baseline "widely available" since Jan 2022; default is [src: micro-typography-craft]
- synthesis ON.) Note: `none` has an a11y downside if the real cut isn't loaded (the style change [src: micro-typography-craft]
- silently vanishes), so it's a *diagnostic*; the *fix* is loading the real cut. For a variable font, a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- "missing weight" may be reachable via `font-variation-settings`/`font-weight` on the variable face, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- not a separate file.[^mdnfontsynthesis][^alistapartfaux][^clagnutfaux] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** a lowercase **'x' used as a math operator/dimension** (`12 x 34`, `1920 x 1080`) instead [src: micro-typography-craft]
- of the centered, symmetric multiplication glyph; an **ellipsis** as three separate periods — jammed [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (`...`) or gapped (`. . .`) — or one that **wraps across a line**; a **faux fraction** (`1/2` on the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- baseline) instead of a proper fraction.[^butterickmath][^butterickellipses][^mdnfontvariantnumeric] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium** (Medium for × in dimensional/data UI and the wrapping ellipsis; Low/Nit [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Multiplication `&times;` (× U+00D7); minus `&minus;` (− U+2212, or an en dash); division [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `&divide;` (÷). Keep the letter x (U+0078) for x-ray/x-axis. Ellipsis `&hellip;` (… U+2026); if a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- house style mandates spaced periods, bind them with non-breaking spaces so they don't wrap. Proper [src: micro-typography-craft]
- fractions: `font-variant-numeric: diagonal-fractions` (`frac`) on a font that carries them, or the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- precomposed glyphs (½ U+00BD).[^butterickmath][^butterickellipses][^mdnfontvariantnumeric] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** **Distorted stroke contrast** — verticals and horizontals no longer in their designed [src: micro-typography-craft]
- proportion: stretched type shows thin verticals + normal horizontals (or vice-versa), round 'O'/'o' [src: micro-typography-craft]
- go oval/egg-shaped, a "fun-house" warp. In tools: InDesign/Illustrator Character panel **Horizontal [src: micro-typography-craft]
- or Vertical Scale ≠ 100%**; on web, `transform: scaleX()/scaleY()` on text. CreativePro: distorting [src: micro-typography-craft]
- type is "a type crime of the highest degree."[^creativepro_distort][^adobescale][^myfontscrimes] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **High** (destroys letter integrity and costs legibility). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Use a family's **true condensed/extended cut** (designed to keep weight contrast and [src: micro-typography-craft]
- proportions), never mechanical scaling. Reset scale to 100%.[^creativepro_distort][^adobescale] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** A single screen/page mixing **4+ unrelated families** (or many sizes/weights/colors of [src: micro-typography-craft]
- different faces) so it reads as a chaotic patchwork.[^design99crimes][^myfontscrimes] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium–High** (High when it destroys hierarchy/credibility). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Rule of thumb **~2 families (one display + one body), max 3**, paired across a clear contrast [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (serif + sans, or script + sans).[^creativemarketrules] **Temper this:** the two/three-font rule is a [src: micro-typography-craft]
- *guideline, not a law* — flag *unintentional/clashing* multiplicity, not a deliberate, well-contrasted [src: micro-typography-craft]
- 3–4-face system. The crime is incoherence, not the count (see [When NOT to flag](#when-not-to-flag-disconfirming-findings)).[^myfontspairing] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** two families **too similar to read as intentional** (two humanist sans, two geometric [src: micro-typography-craft]
- sans) producing a "did they mean that?" wobble; OR historically/aesthetically incompatible pairings [src: micro-typography-craft]
- with no shared contrast.[^sketchdeckpair] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium.** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Pair on *clear* contrast (classification, x-height, structure) while sharing a mood; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- superfamilies or a serif/sans designed together are safe.[^sketchdeckpair] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Multi-line paragraphs where **every line starts at a different horizontal position** [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (ragged left edge), forcing the eye to hunt for each new line. WebAIM: centered long blocks introduce [src: micro-typography-craft]
- reading overhead.[^webaimlayout] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (High for long passages / accessibility). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Left-align (LTR) running text; reserve centering for short headings, captions, a date, or [src: micro-typography-craft]
- single lines.[^webaimlayout] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Underlined words mid-paragraph used for *emphasis* (not links) — a typewriter habit that [src: micro-typography-craft]
- on the web also collides with the link convention (looks clickable) and cuts through descenders.[^webstyleguideemphasis][^nngformatting] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (Medium-High on web because it impersonates links). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Use **italic** (or bold for stronger/heading emphasis); reserve underline for hyperlinks. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Emphasis sparingly (NN/g: bold ≤30% of text).[^webstyleguideemphasis][^nngformatting] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Sentences/paragraphs (not short labels) set entirely in capitals — uniform rectangular [src: micro-typography-craft]
- word-shapes with no ascenders/descenders, defeating word-shape recognition.[^wikiallcaps][^teamwcaps] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Medium** (legibility + accessibility cost; **Low** for short headings/labels where it's [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Use sentence/mixed case for any multi-word passage; limit all-caps to short [src: micro-typography-craft]
- headings/labels/acronyms; if used, add tracking (§3.2). **Temper:** the "all caps is inherently [src: micro-typography-craft]
- harder to read" claim is partly a familiarity/size effect that vanishes at large sizes — flag [src: micro-typography-craft]
- all-caps **long passages**, not short display caps (harm is real for long passages, dyslexic readers, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- and 55+ readers).[^teamwcaps][^wikiallcaps] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **DETECT:** Unstyled browser/app defaults — Times/Arial/system-ui body, default sizes/weights/spacing, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- straight quotes, hyphen-dashes — signaling no typographic intent.[^myfontscrimes][^design99crimes] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **RATE:** **Low–Medium** (Nit for a quick utility; Medium for anything brand/customer-facing). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **FIX:** Set an intentional type stack, scale, and the §8 micro-typography (curly quotes, real dashes, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- proper figures, ligatures). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Named here; the mechanics live in **§6.1** (loose lines) and rivers in **§2.3**. WebAIM: fully-justified [src: micro-typography-craft]
- text impairs readability and creates "rivers of white."[^webaimlayout] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- -- [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Run top-to-bottom on a screenshot; each maps to a section above. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Glyphs** (§8): straight quotes? hyphen-as-dash? faux bold/italic (smeared/slanted)? lining figures [src: micro-typography-craft]
- shouting in body? misaligned number columns? `12 x 34` instead of `×`? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Faux styles** (§8.4, §8.7): small caps too light? bold smeared / italic just slanted? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Kerning/tracking** (§3): uneven display pairs / "keming"? all-caps with no tracking? loose big [src: micro-typography-craft]
- headline? letter-spaced lowercase body? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Leading** (§4): lines touching (too tight) or striping (too loose)? jittery block-to-block rhythm? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Measure** (§5): full-bleed body wider than ~90 chars? a column narrower than ~40? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Justification / rag** (§6, §2): loose lines/rivers in justified text? lumpy rag? hyphen ladder? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Breaks** (§1, §2.4): one-word runt last line? widow/orphan at a column break? stranded subhead? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- broken name / number+unit / URL? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Optical** (§7): un-hung opening quote making a flush edge look indented? a scaled single optical [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Type crimes** (§9): stretched/condensed (scale ≠ 100%)? 4+ clashing fonts? centered long body? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- underline-for-emphasis? all-caps paragraph? [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (Support stamps verified-as-of 2026-06-16.) [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Curly quotes / dashes / ×/…** — author the real glyph/entity (§8); no CSS toggle. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-kerning: normal` — force built-in pair kerning (§3.1). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `letter-spacing: 0.05–0.12em` (caps) / `-0.01–-0.03em` (display) / `normal` (body) (§3.2–3.5). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `line-height: <unitless ~1.4–1.6>` body; `1.1–1.3` headings; multiple of base unit for rhythm (§4). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `max-width: 66ch` / `width: min(66ch, 100%)` — constrain measure (§5). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `text-align: justify; hyphens: auto;` + `<html lang>` — only justify *with* hyphenation (§6); `hyphens` Baseline since Sept 2023, `lang`/dictionary-dependent. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `text-wrap: pretty` — fix runts/rag (engine-divergent: Chromium last ~4 lines, WebKit whole paragraph); `text-wrap: balance` — even short headlines (§1.3, §2.5). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `widows` / `orphans` — paged/multicol only; **no effect in normal web flow**; unsupported in Firefox (§1.5). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `break-after: avoid` / `break-inside: avoid` — keep a subhead with its body (paged/multicol) (§1.4). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-variant-caps: small-caps` + `font-synthesis: small-caps none` — real small caps, expose faux (§8.4). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums | lining-nums | tabular-nums | proportional-nums | diagonal-fractions` (§8.5, §8.8); Baseline since Jan 2020. [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-variant-ligatures: common-ligatures | no-discretionary-ligatures | none` (§8.6). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-synthesis: none` — expose faux bold/italic (diagnostic, not the fix); Baseline since Jan 2022 (§8.7). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `hanging-punctuation: first` — **Safari-only**; use negative `text-indent` fallback (§7.1). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- `font-optical-sizing: auto` (default) / `font-variation-settings: 'opsz' <n>` — opsz; Baseline since Mar 2020 (§7.3). [src: micro-typography-craft]
- Micro-typography critique fails when it applies rules as dogma. Hold fire when: [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Widow/orphan labels** — don't assert which is "worse" or rely on the label; sources reverse the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- definitions and disagree on severity. Describe the position.[^widoworphan][^fontfabricorphan] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Paged widows/orphans on the responsive web** — the *paged* widow/orphan is a print problem; the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- web's real version is the **runt**, a minor defect best fixed with `text-wrap: pretty`. Don't flag [src: micro-typography-craft]
- classic page-widow control on a flowing single-column article.[^butterickwidow][^bootstrapwidow] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Rag depth alone** — a deeper "hard rag" can beat a tight rag bought with bad breaks/excess [src: micro-typography-craft]
- hyphenation (Bringhurst). Flag *accidental shapes* and *wild swings*, not depth per se.[^webtyporag] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Manual kerning in body copy** — built-in/automatic kerning suffices for body and most UI; reserve [src: micro-typography-craft]
- High/Blocker kerning findings for logos, wordmarks, and large display.[^buttericckern][^clagnutmanual] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Baseline-grid misalignment** — a baseline grid "does not automatically create good vertical [src: micro-typography-craft]
- rhythm" and often "has no meaning" on the responsive web; prioritize a consistent 4/8px spacing scale [src: micro-typography-craft]
- over true baseline snapping. Rate Low–Medium.[^vanseobaseline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **The 45–75/66 CPL rule** — it's a strong design *convention*, but reading-speed research is mixed [src: micro-typography-craft]
- (one study read fastest at 95 CPL; the return-sweep mechanism is questioned; short lines help [src: micro-typography-craft]
- struggling/dyslexic readers). Flag out-of-band *extremes*, not every line ≠ 66.[^designregression][^uxpinline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Justified text per se** — it's a personal-preference choice, not an automatic crime; it works at [src: micro-typography-craft]
- narrow measures (newspaper columns) and in InDesign with the Paragraph Composer + hyphenation. The [src: micro-typography-craft]
- defect is *justified-on-the-web-without-hyphenation* or *justified-narrow-measure*.[^butterickjustified][^adamsjustify] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **`hanging-punctuation`** — Safari-only, so an un-hung quote edge is at most a Nit on the web; [src: micro-typography-craft]
- recommend the negative-`text-indent` fallback, don't rate it highly.[^mdnhanging][^coyierhanging] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Tight leading** — correct for headings/display (1.1–1.3) and single-line elements (buttons, nav, [src: micro-typography-craft]
- rows, even `line-height: 1`); only flag tight leading on multi-line running text.[^applehig][^ultimateline] [src: micro-typography-craft]
- **Curly quotes / em-dash spacing / straight-quote primes** — curly quotes are *wrong* in code and [src: micro-typography-craft]
- some databases; em/en-dash spacing is style-dependent (Chicago unspaced em vs British spaced en); [src: micro-typography-craft]
- straight quotes are Butterick's *practical* default for feet/inches. Flag *inconsistency*, not the [src: micro-typography-craft]
- legitimate choice.[^butterickquotes][^cmosdashes][^butterickfootinch] [src: micro-typography-craft]

- <!-- Provenance: standalone skill. Mirrored from ~/.claude/skills/student-loans/SKILL.md by scripts/persist-spoke.mjs. --> [src: student-loans]
- > **Framing — read first.** This is **general educational information, not financial, tax, or legal advice.** US student-loan policy is **exceptionally volatile (2024-2026)**: the SAVE plan was struck down, the *One Big Beautiful Bill Act* (OBBBA, 2025) is rewriting repayment, and PSLF regulations changed. **Every dollar figure, percentage, plan name, and deadline below is stated "as of 2026" and can change without notice — verify the current rule at [studentaid.gov](https://studentaid.gov) before relying on it or advising anyone.** When unsure, send the borrower to studentaid.gov and their loan servicer. [src: student-loans]
- This skill is a **spoke of the `consumer-finance` hub** (note only — do not modify the hub); route there for sibling personal-finance topics (banking, taxes, insurance, budgeting, investing, estate planning). The **`consumer-credit-and-debt`** hub is a **sibling** family — route there for credit-report/score, collections, lending, and consumer-credit-law topics. For neighboring topics see the cross-references at the end. [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- **Federal loans** (US Dept. of Education / Federal Student Aid) carry borrower protections private loans do not: fixed rates set by Congress, income-driven repayment, forgiveness programs (PSLF, IDR forgiveness), generous deferment/forbearance, and death/disability discharge. **Get federal first** by filing the FAFSA. [src: student-loans]
- **Private loans** (banks, credit unions, online lenders) are credit-underwritten, often need a **cosigner**, may carry **variable rates**, and have **no IDR, no PSLF, and no statutory deferment/forbearance**. Discharge on death/disability is at the lender's discretion (many but not all offer it). [src: student-loans]
- > **The refinancing trap (most important single point).** Refinancing **federal loans into a private loan** is permanent and **forfeits all federal protections** — IDR, PSLF, federal forgiveness/discharge, and federal deferment/forbearance. A lower rate rarely justifies losing those for a borrower who might ever need income-driven payments or public-service forgiveness. "Should I refinance?" → only consider it for **private-only** debt, or for a high earner with stable income who will never use federal benefits. (CFPB has cited lenders for *implying* borrowers keep federal benefits after refinancing — they do not.) [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- **Interest rates** are fixed for the life of each loan, set annually by Congress for loans disbursed July 1–June 30. **Look up the current year's rates at studentaid.gov** — do not quote a remembered number. [src: student-loans]
- **Capitalization** = unpaid interest added to principal (you then pay interest on interest). On unsubsidized/PLUS loans it can occur **after the grace period and at the end of deferment or forbearance**. Avoid it by paying interest as it accrues (e.g., while in school). [src: student-loans]
- **Annual/aggregate borrowing limits** exist (e.g., dependent undergrad first-year subsidized cap; lifetime undergrad subsidized aggregate). **OBBBA also introduced new borrowing limits — verify current limits at studentaid.gov.** [src: student-loans]
- **Servicers** collect payments and administer plans: **MOHELA, Aidvantage, Nelnet, EdFinancial** (assignments change). Find yours by logging into **studentaid.gov** → account dashboard. The servicer is who you actually call. [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- > **2026 status — IN FLUX.** A court order **ended the SAVE plan (effective ~March 10, 2026)**; borrowers were moved off it and must pick another plan. Under **OBBBA**, borrowers who take out a **new loan or consolidate on or after July 1, 2026** repay under the new **Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP)** or a **Tiered Standard** plan, and legacy IDR plans (ICR/PAYE, and SAVE) are being phased out for them. **Confirm which plans you can actually enroll in today at studentaid.gov/courtactions and studentaid.gov.** [src: student-loans]
- **IDR mechanics:** payment tied to income & family size; **recertify income annually**; spousal income may count depending on plan and tax-filing status; **amount forgiven under IDR can be taxable** (federal tax treatment has changed repeatedly — verify). [src: student-loans]
- **Use the official Loan Simulator at studentaid.gov/loan-simulator** to compare your actual numbers; it reflects current plan availability better than any static table. [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- **PSLF (Public Service Loan Forgiveness):** **120 qualifying monthly payments** (≈10 yrs) while working **full-time for government or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit**, on **Direct Loans** under a qualifying plan (Standard or IDR). Tax-free forgiveness. **New PSLF regulations took effect ~July 1, 2026 — verify qualifying-employer and payment rules.** Use the **PSLF Help Tool** and submit the employment-certification form annually. [src: student-loans]
- **PSLF Buyback:** lets you **pay for past months** that didn't count because you were in an **ineligible deferment/forbearance**, converting them to qualifying payments once you'd otherwise reach 120. [src: student-loans]
- **IDR forgiveness:** remaining balance forgiven after the plan's full term (**20–25 yrs**, RAP longer) — separate from PSLF, no employer requirement. [src: student-loans]
- **Teacher Loan Forgiveness:** up to **$17,500** (highly qualified math/science/special-ed; otherwise up to $5,000) after **5 complete & consecutive years** at a qualifying low-income school. Cannot double-count the same service for both TLF and PSLF simultaneously. [src: student-loans]
- **Borrower Defense to Repayment:** discharge for school **misconduct/misrepresentation** (e.g., fraud). Heavily litigated/paused at times — verify processing status. [src: student-loans]
- **Closed-School Discharge:** if your school closed while enrolled or shortly after withdrawal. [src: student-loans]
- **Total & Permanent Disability (TPD) Discharge:** via SSA, VA, or physician certification; also discharges TEACH-grant obligations. [src: student-loans]
- **Death Discharge:** federal loans (incl. Parent PLUS, on the student's or parent's death) are discharged on proof of death. [src: student-loans]
- > **Bankruptcy is a separate path.** Discharging student loans in **bankruptcy** (the *undue hardship* / Brunner standard, adversary proceeding) is **cross-referenced, not covered here → `bankruptcy-ch7-ch13`.** [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- Both **pause payments**; the difference is **who pays interest**: [src: student-loans]
- **Rule of thumb:** **prefer deferment** if eligible (free interest subsidy on subsidized loans). Use forbearance only if you don't qualify for deferment, and **pay accruing interest if you can** to avoid capitalization. For long-term affordability, an **IDR plan is usually better than repeated forbearance** (forbearance months generally don't count toward PSLF/IDR forgiveness; certain IDR payments can be **$0** and still count). [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- **Delinquent** = 1 day past due; reported to credit bureaus typically at **90 days**. **Default** on most Direct Loans = **~270 days** (about 9 months) past due. [src: student-loans]
- **Consequences of default** (federal, **without a court judgment**): [src: student-loans]
- Entire balance **accelerated**; **collection costs** added. [src: student-loans]
- **Treasury Offset Program:** seizure of **tax refunds and federal benefits** (including a portion of **Social Security**). [src: student-loans]
- **Administrative Wage Garnishment (AWG):** ED can order your employer to withhold **up to 15% of disposable pay administratively — no lawsuit or court order required.** [src: student-loans]
- > **NC note:** North Carolina generally **bans wage garnishment** for ordinary consumer debts, but **federal AWG for student loans bypasses that protection** because it operates under federal law. (NC's general garnishment rules themselves → **`north-carolina-credit-and-debt-law`**.) [src: student-loans]
- Loss of eligibility for further federal aid; damaged credit. [src: student-loans]
- **Getting out of default:** [src: student-loans]
- **Loan Rehabilitation:** agree to and make **9 on-time monthly payments** (income-based, can be modest) over ~10 months. After completion the **default notation is removed** from your credit report (late-payment history may remain). Involuntary collections generally stop after ~5 rehab payments. **One rehab per loan.** [src: student-loans]
- **Consolidation:** combine defaulted loan(s) into a new Direct Consolidation Loan (with 3 on-time payments or by agreeing to IDR) — **faster**, but the **default record stays** on your credit report. [src: student-loans]
- **Pay in full / settlement** (rare). [src: student-loans]
- **Fresh Start:** the temporary post-pandemic program that auto-restored defaulted borrowers to good standing **ended October 2, 2024.** Don't rely on it; **verify any successor program at studentaid.gov.** [src: student-loans]
- -- [src: student-loans]
- File the **FAFSA** every year (it's free; at studentaid.gov) — it's the gateway to grants, work-study, and federal loans, and many states/schools require it. [src: student-loans]
- **Borrow only what you need.** Prefer **grants/scholarships → subsidized → unsubsidized → (last) PLUS/private.** [src: student-loans]
- Favor **federal over private**; keep **subsidized** over unsubsidized when both are offered. [src: student-loans]
- Know your servicer, keep your **studentaid.gov** login current, and **never pay a company for help** you can get free from your servicer or studentaid.gov (student-loan "debt relief" scams are common — CFPB warns against advance-fee operators). [src: student-loans]

- <!-- Provenance: standalone skill. Mirrored from ~/.claude/skills/personal-banking/SKILL.md by scripts/persist-spoke.mjs. --> [src: personal-banking]
- > **Framing.** This is **general educational information, not financial advice.** [src: personal-banking]
